- D180 said the letter's facts keep every sentence other than CBP's reply wording, "as written". That held only for facts with blank `\n\n` lines and no abbreviations. With the committed facts' own breaks it could drop fact sentences, keep a fragment, or keep the boilerplate (#434). D250 fixes the function; the claim holds as D250 states it, with the limits listed there.

## D260 — A public "How it's built and tested" page at /method (21 Nov, review follow-up)
- **Why:** a judge reading "accuracy" may assume a trained model and ask how it was trained. Unde trains nothing: it prompts Gemini 4 Argon with retrieved earlier CBP rulings, with a Gemini 3.8 Flash router. The page says so first, then answers in order: what the model is, what data it sees, how prompts, bars and calibration were chosen, how the test sets are kept clean, what did not work, how stable it is, and how to check it.
- **Built:** `/method` (`frontend/src/components/op/screens/method-page.tsx`, data in `frontend/src/lib/method.ts`), linked from the top bar ("Method"; below `lg` the accuracy item reads "Accuracy" so four items fit), the landing's "What you can do" and footer, /accuracy and the README. A dated protocol timeline links each step to its entry here. Measured findings are charts with their numbers (the split windows, one leak path, the development arms that were not adopted, the repeat runs); process facts are plain text.
- **Numbers:** no new runs. The repeat runs come from `GET /v1/eval/summary`; every other figure is a row of docs/NUMBERS.md. Rows already in EVALUATION.md and this file but missing from the registry were added there (section "Method page (/method)"). `frontend/scripts/method.test.mjs` fails if a linked decision heading, file or section anchor changes, or a charted figure is no longer in NUMBERS.md.
- **Stated where the protocol fell short:** the first 0.92 bar was chosen with a rule that looked at both splits (D32; the 0.90 calibrated bar now in use was re-derived on dev only, D160); the textile, pharmaceutical and Part 102 bars came from their first held-out windows (D51, D61, D62); part of the plan check's prompt was written after seeing the 2026 flip pairs (D74); the D152 selection rule was written while two runs were in progress; router-v3/v4's &quot;trade programs&quot; cue was written after reading post-cutoff misses, so its post-cutoff figures are not clean held-out evidence (D233; D266); the research prototype scored the first held-out rulings before this repository froze them; earlier held-out rulings can be precedents; BM25 statistics use the whole corpus; pre-training exposure cannot be excluded. Two rows of the negative-results chart (the October Gemini 3.5 Flash runs) are not recomputed by `make reproduce`, and the page says so.
- **Correction:** /accuracy's "How it's built" said the held-out rulings were never used to tune thresholds. It now says prompts and retrieval were not, the general engine's bar is fitted on development rulings, and the specialist bars came from their first held-out windows.

## D261 — The regression slice re-runs provider outages once and reports them apart from wrong answers (21 Nov, review follow-up)
- **Why:** the post-merge slice (`eval slice`, `.github/workflows/eval-slice.yml`, D72, D88) counts a case that failed as wrong. Vertex 504s decided runs: one failed with timeouts counted as wrong and passed on a re-run with fewer. The 20 Nov failed run (Actions run 44677154743) had 9 cases each fail with `llm: model provider unavailable after 4 attempts: vertex: HTTP 504: Deadline expired`, 154 to 249 s after the call started.
- **Built:** after the first pass, every case whose row failed with a provider outage (a timeout, a 5xx or a 429; `evalslice.Transient`) is run once more after a cool-down (`-retry-cooldown`, default 60 s), within a time budget (`-retry-budget`, default 3 min) so the job stays under the workflow's 20-minute limit. Bad answers and other errors are never re-run. Rows record `error_class` (`unavailable` or `bad_response`, set by `cmd/eval` for every run), `retries` and the first try's error. The report adds "N cases hit a model provider error … M answered" and "N cases unavailable after retry (model provider errors, not wrong answers); counted as wrong for the gate". The gate is unchanged: an unavailable case still counts as wrong, and more than `EVAL_SLICE_MAX_ERRORS` failures still make the run inconclusive. `-retry=false` turns it off. Rows from before this change are classified from their error text; on the 20 Nov rows the report says the 9 cases "failed with a model provider error and were not re-run". No workflow file changed.
- **Tests:** `TestSliceRetriesProviderErrorsOnce` (llm.Fake: a 504 that recovers, a 504 that does not, a bad answer that must not be re-run, the budget, retry off, a cancelled cool-down) and `TestTransient`.
- **Production path, checked, not changed:** a single model call cannot run for 240 s. `LLM_TIMEOUT` defaults to 30 s per attempt (`config.go`), applied as the Vertex client's HTTP timeout. The 150–250 s in the slice is the shared client's whole retry chain: 1 + `LLM_MAX_RETRIES` (3) attempts of up to 30 s, backoff of 2, 4 and 8 s, and the workflow's pacing (8 s gap, 60 s cool-down after an overload). The production engine does not use that chain: with the fallback on (code default `gemini-3.8-flash`), the primary gets `ENGINE_ATTEMPTS` tries (code default 2; production sets 1) and then one fallback call with its own 60 s budget, so a predict waits at most about 30 s + 60 s plus pacing before an answer or a `model_unavailable` error, and a fallback answer always goes to review. The defaults look sensible for production. The eval slice uses the shared client without the fallback on purpose (it measures Argon); a shorter per-attempt timeout would turn slow-but-valid answers into failures. No code default changed.

## D262 — Correction to D156: the calibration map is weakly monotone and the ECE bins differ (21 Nov, review follow-up, #397)
- **Problem:** D156 and EVALUATION.md 4.2 called the dev-fitted map "monotone" and said it "ranks cases exactly as before". The isotonic fit pools adjacent values and the 0.99 cap ties the top three. On the 377 held-out rulings the 11 stated levels become 6 calibrated levels: 0.72, 0.78, 0.85 and 0.88 (42 cases) pool at 0.6136, and 0.98, 0.99 and 1.00 (180 cases) are all 0.99. A bar at a stated 0.99 or 1.00 has no equivalent calibrated cut, and accuracy-coverage points there cannot be read from calibrated values.
- **Second correction:** ECE with "one bin per emitted value" uses different partitions on the two sides, and merging bins alone can only reduce ECE. On the 377 that is 11 bins before and 6 after: scoring the stated confidences on the calibrated partition gives 0.0528, against 0.0585 on their own levels and 0.0300 calibrated on 6 levels — roughly a fifth of the reported 0.059 → 0.030 drop is the coarser partition, not better probabilities. Final2 (9 → 6) gives 0.0614 against 0.0667 and 0.0375 (~18%), and the pooled 460 (11 → 6) gives 0.0500 against 0.0547 and 0.0273 (~17%). Cal-v2 pools in the same way: its same-bin stated figures are 0.0528, 0.0614 and 0.0500 against calibrated own-bin ECEs 0.0285, 0.0367 and 0.0259 (~19%, 18%, 16%). Brier is bin-independent and stands on every set.
- **Decision:** keep the layer and its measured numbers; correct the wording everywhere those pairs are published. The 0.92 → 0.90 equivalence used by D160 still holds, and cal-v2's map and bar (D160) are unchanged. Use stated confidence for bars at or above 0.98. `build_accuracy.py` writes the same-bin value, level counts and per-level ties for all three sets under both maps into `eval/results/accuracy-v2-metrics.json` (`heldout_stated_on_calibrated_bins` and each split's `calibration_layer`, or `calibration_v2.*.stated_on_calibrated_bins` / `.level_counts`), so both corrections are recomputed by `make reproduce`. EVALUATION.md 4.2, RESULTS.md, NUMBERS.md, D160, the served `final_calibration_ece_*` labels and /accuracy carry the same caveat (#493). No model call, no probability or bar change.

## D263 — The readiness-eval leakage gate fails closed on unreadable dates (21 Nov, review follow-up, #375)
- **Problem:** `leakCheck` compared `ruling_date` and `retrieved[].date` to the frozen cutoff as raw strings. An absent or empty retrieved date, or a regional format such as `10/01/2026` or `1 Oct 2026`, sorts before a cutoff beginning with `2` and passed the pre-call hook, so a case with unproven post-cutoff retrievals was scored as clean. The case date already failed safe; the retrieved dates failed open.
- **Decision:** parse the cutoff and every case/retrieved date as `time.DateOnly`; a missing, empty or unparseable date excludes the case as `excluded_leak` with a reason, as does a non-ISO cutoff in the frozen config. Rebuilt comparisons use `time.Before`, so an item dated exactly on the exclusive cutoff is still excluded. Fixture authors must write ISO dates; no format guessing or assumed-earlier fallback.
- **Evidence:** `cmd/readiness-eval` unit tests cover the ISO control, an on-cutoff item, absent, empty, US-format and day-month-name retrieved dates, bad case dates and a bad cutoff, plus an end-to-end `--dry-run` that records the bad case as `excluded_leak=1` with no model call. `docs/evaluation-readiness.md` states the fixture rule. No published number changes: the real eval is still intentionally unavailable until the #275 protocol is frozen.

## D264 — Ruling-grounded template defaults no longer assert other products' parts (21 Nov, review follow-up, #392)
- **Problem:** the ten templates added in D138 and the motors/pumps family added in D212 were drafted from up to 45 rulings each. Several groups list the union of different products' processes. `Render` used those operations whenever a fixture supplied none for a moved group, and labelled them as an assumption — but still as facts about this case. The water-dispenser fixture's `dispenser_electronics` move to South Korea asserted "UV lamp assemblies, lamp PCBAs, quartz tubes, and RFID smart chip assemblies"; a needle's cannula move asserted "hot-forge and anneal stainless steel into the distinctive shape of surgical forceps". Extra in-house work at the target pushes toward a change of origin, so the error was one-directional. The committed water-dispenser live-check `variant_facts` contain the same wording.
- **Decision:** `Template.UnionDefaultOperations` marks the eleven ruling-grounded families. When it is set and the product supplied no operations for a group (including final assembly), `Render` writes a neutral statement — the named components will be made at the target, with the existing assumption label — and no process steps. Supplied operations still win unlabelled; the three earlier templates keep their original defaults. The flag set is pinned by `TestUnionDefaultFlagPinned`; render tests cover the water-dispenser move, a synthetic needle move and the supplied-operations path.
- **Evidence:** both new render tests fail with the union guard disabled and pass with it; `go test ./...` passes. The one-run family live checks were run on the old facts and are disclosed as such in D138 and RESULTS.md; their result files are unchanged and no model call was repeated.

## D270 — Judge panel round 3: one story about what was measured, a demo copy that cannot hide new fields, plan labels in the product's words, an enforced CSP (21 Nov, review follow-up)
- **Why:** the round-3 panel (mean 84.9) listed eight fixes. This entry covers items 1–6 and 8. Item 7 (pin and pre-run the five new-family demos) needs the owner and a small model spend, and is not done here.
- **What was measured, said the same everywhere:** /accuracy's intro and the README said repeatability was measured on the development set only; D240 and D241 also measured it on both held-out splits. Both now give the held-out repeats. /method's "Where we fell short" adds router-v4's "trade programs" cue, which came from reading post-cutoff misses: without the 6 cue rulings the routed path is 90/101 for router-v4 against 91/101 for router-v2 (D233, docs/NUMBERS.md). The router chart caption says the same beside "defined before its run".
- **Two inputs, two answers (#443) on the live flagship:** the API sent everything the sentence needs. The browser did not: for a pinned demo, `useCase` preferred a copy of the case kept in sessionStorage over the server's case, whole, and a copy saved before `facts_source` existed has no such field. A fresh tab showed the sentence; a tab that had visited before #443 shipped never did. The same stale copy kept plan descriptions from before D220 ("Make Motor-fan assembly, PCBA (SMT) and…"). The kept copy now records the server `updated_at` it was based on; it is used only while the server still reports that value, and it is laid over the server's case, so a field the server adds still arrives. A copy in the old format is dropped. `frontend/scripts/case-local.test.mjs` uses a trimmed copy of the live flagship response (`scripts/golden/flagship-case.json`) and fails without the fix.
- **Descriptions match production:** the /accuracy router card names textile beside pharmaceutical and Part 102. DETAILS says the specialist engines are off by default in code and on in production (deploy settings read, not changed).
- **One meaning per number:** /method plots the gateway parity row as the mean of its three runs (91.3%), with each run as a dot (91.8%, 91.1%, 91.1%); the paired test is the first run's. The three 88.8% figures on /accuracy carry their own labels: "All regimes · 616 rulings, each once" and "Routed product · 107 later rulings"; the photo import shows "151 of 170" with no percentage. Gateway rows in the negative-results chart say "gateway run".
- **Plan labels in the product's words:** a plan sentence names a moved group by its template name only when that name shares a word with a part filed under it (plural "s" dropped, PCBA read as printed circuit board, words such as "assembly", "module" and "part" ignored). Otherwise it names the parts, as the facts already do (`planner.Render`). Scanned over every demo product: the power bank's cells ("Power conversion or charging module") now read "the two cylindrical lithium-ion battery cells", the wheel's bar and forging ("Housings and structural parts") read as those parts, and the PCR analyser's "Hubs, clamps and housings" would name its parts if it moved. Every other group keeps its name. "What moves" lists parts, and a group's process steps only when none of its parts move (the gas grill listed 18 items). The frontend now shows template group names for every family instead of the group id.
- **Demo cards:** a card that starts a live run says "Runs a plan search too", not "Plan included". A pinned demo with no recorded current origin (the two dryer latches) takes "CBP held" from its demo entry, and one read from CBP's text alone says "Origin only: CBP's text, no parts list to plan" instead of "No plan search yet". The landing no longer says the pinned case may show no plan: its 18 Oct plan search is the run in DEMO.md section 6. scope-and-jurisdiction.md said 13 families; it is 14 (D212).
- **CSP enforced:** `frontend/next.config.ts` sends `Content-Security-Policy` instead of the report-only header, and allows Google profile pictures (`lh3.googleusercontent.com`) for the signed-in avatar, which the old policy would have blocked. Checked in a local production build with the production client ID: the Google script and its button frame loaded, and the landing, /cases, /accuracy, /method, /developers, /triage, /review and a case's origin, scenarios, plan and draft pages reported no violations (buffered `ReportingObserver`). A full sign-in (Google's popup, the credential and the signed-in page) was not completed locally; the popup is Google's own page, and the credential is posted to this site.
- **Calibration steps said on screen:** where calibrated values appear (Scenarios, /accuracy, and the calibrated-confidence explanation on Origin and the broker page), a short note says they come in steps: every stated confidence under 0.90 becomes 0.60, and 0.98 or more becomes 0.99 (`backend/internal/calibrate/map.json`).
- **Phone landing:** at 390 px the roles list and fig.4's five steps start folded behind a summary that says what is inside; wide screens are unchanged. fig.1's scroll track is 260vh instead of 360vh on phones (the animation runs on progress). Nothing was removed.
- **Not done:** item 7; "Needs expert review" against "Needs more facts" (different triage routes for different inputs, so left as is).

## D280 — MCP tool-call requests carry none of the outer request's context (21 Nov, review follow-up, follow-up to #481)
- **Why:** #385 showed that a tool call inherited the identity `withUser` had put in the `POST /mcp` request's context, because every in-process `/v1` request was built on that context. #481 fixed it by having `withUser` skip `/mcp` (a sign-in token there is ignored, not refused). That closes the user path, but any other value the outer middleware stores (an API key from a future change, audit state) would still ride into tool calls the same way.
- **Built:** `mcpserver` builds every tool request on `isolated(ctx)`: the MCP request's cancellation without any of its context values. A tool call's principal comes only from the headers `call` sets (the forwarded API key, the client address, the case access key), which the API's middleware checks again. The guard also drops `X-Review-Token`, as it drops the visitor ID and cookies. The #481 policy is unchanged: the admin token is refused with 403, a sign-in token is ignored.
- **Tests:** `TestMCPToolCallsDoNotInheritTheOuterPrincipal` puts a signed-in user and an authenticated API key straight into the outer context, past the guard and the `withUser` skip, and checks `get_case`, `list_cases` and that a key's `predict_origin` case belongs to the key; its three context rows fail on the code before this change. Also `TestMCPIgnoresABrokerReviewToken`, `TestIsolationMatrixOverMCP` (every matrix principal on `POST /mcp`, ownership on and off: admin refused, user token ignored, visitor ID dropped, key is the key) and `mcpserver.TestToolRequestsDoNotInheritContextValues`. `-race` passes on `httpapi` and `mcpserver`.

## D265 — Calibrated confidence is named on every surface that reports a prediction (review follow-up, #402)
- **Problem:** D160/D161 attached `calibrated_confidence` to general-engine predictions and triaged on the calibrated 0.90 bar, but five later surfaces still printed only the model's stated value. A batch row could read "China 0.85" beside a reason saying "calibrated confidence 0.60"; the BOM-version panel and `bom_updated` history event said "confidence 0.92" beside a reason saying calibrated 0.90; the ruling-watch "Changed" line, the Ask agent's `get_case`/`what_if` text and `predicted` history events had the same gap. Two different confidences for one prediction, with no label, are not defensible in a demo.
- **Decision:** use the Result screen's wording everywhere: calibrated first, with the stated value labelled as the model's own; without a map, label the value as stated. `BatchRow` and the BOM-version response carry `calibrated_confidence` and the map version; OpenAPI and `schema.d.ts` are regenerated. The triage page, its CSV, the BOM-version panel and the watch line use `originConf`/`originConfCaption`. `agentCaseText`, the `what_if` tool text and history summaries use the same phrase. No triage threshold or stored prediction changes; this is presentation only.
- **Evidence:** `calibration_everywhere_test.go` runs the offline fake engine with the committed cal-v2 map through batch, BOM version, watch, history and `agentCaseText`, and fails if any of them omits calibrated 0.60 or the "model stated 0.85" label; `caseagent/confidence_test.go` pins the what-if phrase. The four `golden281/flows_*.json` fixtures were regenerated for the labelled stated-value string; no other golden bytes changed. `npm run gen:api && git diff --exit-code src/lib/api/schema.d.ts` is clean.

## D266 — The method page carries the router-cue caveat and the router's own dates (review follow-up, #480)
- **Problem:** #473 disclosed that router-v3/v4's "trade programs" cue was written after reading post-cutoff misses on every surface that publishes the router figures — except `/method`, which did not exist when #464 was filed. The page still said the router was compared only on the July–December 2025 development split, listed it as an example of the clean pattern, and gave no router cue in its shortfall list. Its timeline band repeated the wrong dates. `/accuracy` also ran the caveat straight onto the previous sentence ("engine.Caveat:") because JSX trimmed the newline.
- **Decision:** `/method` now says the engine's development split is July–December 2025 for the prompt, precedents, calibration and bar, and that the router has its own 729-ruling split (25 Jan 2024 – 31 Dec 2025). Its "compared only there" claim is qualified; the cue shortfall is listed next to D233's disclosure, and D260's shortfall list names it. The /accuracy caveat starts with an explicit JSX space. No number changes: this is wording about runs already published.
- **Evidence:** `method.test.mjs` now fails if the cue disclosure, the 729-ruling window or the caveat spacing disappears. The router split dates were read from `eval/splits/splits_router.json` and the label files (729 rulings, 33 from 2024).

## D281 - MCP tool calls use the trusted-proxy client address rule (#479)
- **Problem:** #421 required that `X-Client-IP` be honoured only from `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`, and SECURITY.md promised that for `/mcp` too. #460 closed the REST path, but the MCP guard kept a caller-supplied header and each tool then made it the in-process request's `RemoteAddr`. A direct `/mcp` caller could rotate the header and get a fresh light (20/min) and heavy (4/min) bucket for every tool call. The outer POST still had the basic class on the real address, but the model-call limits did not apply to that caller.
- **Decision:** `mcpserver.Options.ClientAddress` resolves the address once in the guard. `httpapi` supplies `clientAddressWithProxy`, the same helper `clientKey` now uses: the header is used only from a configured trusted range, otherwise the connection address wins. Tools receive the resolved value, which is what `clientKeyWithProxy` sees as `RemoteAddr`. No limit changed; the documented rule is now the code's rule.
- **Evidence:** `mcpserver.TestGuardResolvesTheClientAddressOnce` pins the default and the trusted case. `TestMCPIgnoresACallerChosenClientAddress` drives the real handler chain with no trusted range and rotating headers: the second `predict_origin` and the second `plan_production_moves` are 429. `TestMCPHonoursTheHeaderFromATrustedProxy` shows two proxy-supplied addresses still get two buckets. SECURITY.md line 65 now describes both.

## D282 - The failed-key throttle reserves a lookup slot under the same lock (#386)
- **Problem:** `withAPIKeys` read the failure bucket, then did a key-store lookup, then recorded a failure. Fifty concurrent guesses from one address could all observe free tokens before any failure was recorded: 50 Firestore reads and 50 x 401, where the sequential path stopped at 10. `fail` also used `AllowN`, which spends nothing once the bucket is empty.
- **Decision:** `authFailures.begin` reserves an in-flight slot while checking the token bucket, under the existing mutex. Only invalid keys spend a token; valid keys and store errors return the slot. A lookup is refused when either the token bucket is empty (with its refill wait) or the per-client in-flight cap is full. SECURITY.md now states both conditions. Review-token throttling is unchanged.
- **Evidence:** `TestAPIKeyFailuresThrottledUnderConcurrency` sends 50 well-formed unknown keys from one address through the real handler with a 20 ms store and counts `Get` calls: at most 10 lookups, the rest 429. Removing the in-flight cap makes it 50. The sequential throttle test still passes.

## D283 - The draft facts accept pasted lists of any shape (#478)
- **Problem:** #472 only split a list from the previous sentence when that sentence ended in a full stop and the marker was one of six characters. Unpunctuated items, a colon lead-in, Word's `o` bullet, `+`, `◦`, `▪` or `‣`, multi-letter roman numerals and numbered items all let a boilerplate line swallow the facts; a dropped `2.` left a bare number in the letter.
- **Decision:** `splitFacts` treats a line break followed by any of those markers as a sentence boundary regardless of the previous line's ending, and the marker (including its `.` or `)`) is part of the item's sentence, so dropping the item drops the marker too. D250 and the `CleanFacts` comment now state the rule.
- **Evidence:** new table cases in `facts_test.go` cover the six reproductions from #478 and every marker above; `TestDraftHeatGunFactsAsBullets` rewrites the demo facts as `-` and `•` lists with LF and CRLF and checks that no lead-in survives and all three facts do. Removing either the line-break boundary or the marker-period guard fails these tests. The committed-facts corpus check (99.78%) still passes.

## D300 — Re-examining the 0.92 plan bar on committed rows: rule written before any re-computation (21 Nov, review follow-up, judge panel round 4 item 6)
- **Why:** the precedent-check bands on /accuracy (D86) show supported checks are real changes in almost every band, so the 0.92 bar's precision benefit is not shown, while it costs recall (about 30% of real-change pairs are shown in every run). The panel asked for a dev-only, pre-registered look at the bar before anyone argues for a different one.
- **No model calls.** Every row used already exists; each verdict's confidence is recorded.
- **What the analyst had already seen:** the D86 band table (dev and 2026 pairs), the published 0.92 results on the post-cutoff pairs (D170, D192), and three below-bar confidences named in D170's text (the pneumatic wrench at 0.78, the ratchet-wrench control at 0.78 unknown-a, the Waffle Cone purifier move at 0.85). So the held-out report below is not blind. It is a report of what a dev-chosen bar would mean, not a test of it.
- **Selection data (dev only):** the nine verifier-v2 runs D86 pools, `eval/results/flips-dev-verifier-v2*-{known,unknown}-a-litellm.jsonl` (54 pre-2026 pairs, heat-gun pair excluded, rows with a provider error left out). verifier-v1 and v3 runs are left out: production runs v2.
- **Definitions:** a verdict is *shown at bar b* when it says origin changes, cites a supporting ruling, and has confidence ≥ b. It is *right* when the pair is a real origin change and the check named CBP's later origin (`origin_b_ok`, the D170 rule); otherwise *wrong*. Pair level counts each pair once (D86): a wrong pair is one shown wrong in any run.
- **Candidate bars:** 0.92 (current), 0.90, 0.88, 0.85, 0.80, 0.75.
- **Rule:** the chosen bar b* is the lowest candidate such that it and every higher candidate meet both conditions on dev: (a) pooled, at least 100 shown verdicts and the Wilson 95% lower bound of precision ≥ 97%; (b) pair level, no wrong pair shown in any run.
- **Evidence gate for production:** production changes to b* only if b* < 0.92 **and** the dev rows hold at least 10 wrong supported verdicts at any confidence, so the bar is placed by where wrong verdicts fall and not by their absence. With fewer, the finding is reported, production keeps 0.92, and a lower bar waits for a scored run on new pairs (the panel's own advice).
- **Then, and only then, report (computed offline from existing rows, labelled so):** at b*, at 0.92 and at 0.85 (the alternative the panel named), the post-cutoff flip pairs (D170 + D192, 18 pairs, each mode scored once), the 2026 pairs (21 pairs, four v2 runs, contaminated per D74), and the plan searches already run: the five post-cutoff plan searches (D170) and the 23 per-family plan checks (D171), listing every move a lower bar would newly show.
- **Script:** `eval/planner/plan_bar.py` (no model, `--dev-only` prints the dev table and b* without opening a held-out file; the full run writes `eval/results/plan-bar-analysis.json`; `--check` recomputes it). Committed with this entry, before it was run.

## D301 — The 0.92 plan bar stays: the dev rule picks 0.92, and there are too few wrong verdicts to place a lower one (21 Nov, review follow-up, judge panel round 4 item 6)
- **Run:** `python3 -I -B eval/planner/plan_bar.py . --dev-only` after D300 was committed (e4a555e6), then the full report. No model calls; everything below is computed offline from rows that already existed. Output: `eval/results/plan-bar-analysis.json` (`--check` in `make reproduce`).
- **Dev (selection), nine verifier-v2 runs, 54 pairs, 485 verdicts (1 error row left out), D170 rule for right:**

  | bar | shown | wrong | precision (95% CI) | real changes shown, pooled | real-change pairs shown in every run | wrong pairs | meets D300 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 0.92 | 159 | 0 | 100% (97.6–100) | 159/413 = 38.5% | 13/46 | none | yes |
  | 0.90 | 193 | 2 | 99.0% (96.3–99.7) | 191/413 = 46.2% | 14/46 | 2 | no |
  | 0.88 | 198 | 2 | 99.0% (96.4–99.7) | 196/413 = 47.5% | 14/46 | 2 | no |
  | 0.85 | 256 | 3 | 98.8% (96.6–99.6) | 253/413 = 61.3% | 19/46 | 2 | no |
  | 0.80 | 262 | 3 | 98.9% (96.7–99.6) | 259/413 = 62.7% | 21/46 | 2 | no |
  | 0.75 | 284 | 3 | 98.9% (96.9–99.6) | 281/413 = 68.0% | 24/46 | 2 | no |

- **Chosen bar: 0.92.** The only wrong supported dev verdicts sit just below it: NEG-H323218 (a no-change control CBP reversed on reconsideration) at 0.90 and 0.85, and MS-N344318 (a real change with the wrong later origin named, unknown-a) at 0.90. Every lower candidate shows at least one wrong pair. So on dev the bar is not arbitrary: it is the lowest candidate with no wrong verdict above it. The panel's reading that checks are right in every band is close to true for the D86 definition (real change only), but the D170 definition, which also asks for the right later origin, finds the wrong ones in 0.85–0.90.
- **Evidence gate: not passed, and would not have been needed.** Dev holds 3 wrong supported verdicts out of 287 (2 pairs), under the 10 D300 asks for. The evidence is thin in both directions: it cannot show that 0.92 is better than 0.90, only that the few wrong verdicts there are all below it. Production keeps 0.92 (`config.DefaultPlanBar`, `PLAN_CONFIDENCE`). No code, UI or published figure changes.
- **Reported after the choice (offline, from existing rows; the 0.92 figures were already published):**
  - Post-cutoff pairs, 18 (D170 + D192), known-a: 0.92 and 0.85 are identical, shown 9, right 9/9 (70.1–100), real changes 9/12 = 75.0% (46.8–91.1), controls 0/6. Lowering the bar adds nothing: the three misses are the fracking unit (no change seen), the wrapping paper (no support) and the pneumatic wrench (supported at 0.78).
  - Same pairs, unknown-a: 0.92 shows 6, right 5/6, real changes 5/12; 0.85 shows 9, right 8/9 (56.5–98.0), real changes 8/12 = 66.7% (39.1–86.2), controls 0/6. The three added are right (windchime 0.85, wax warmer 0.90, stove heater 0.90).
  - 2026 pairs (contaminated, D74), four runs, 83 verdicts: 0.92 shows 23, right 21 (91.3%, 73.2–97.6; the two misses name the wrong later origin on one pair, which the D86 table counts as real changes); 0.85 shows 40, right 36 (90.0%, 77.0–96.0), and two no-change controls (NEG-N363700, NEG-N364156) become shown.
  - Plan searches already run: on the five post-cutoff searches, 0.85 would show plans on 4 of 5 instead of 2 of 5; the three added moves are all on the air-purifier reverse probes (target China; Champ one move, Waffle Cone two). CBP's same-day ruling directly contradicts one of them (Waffle Cone, motor-fan assembly alone to China; CBP kept Indonesia with a Chinese motor); the other two move more than the motor and have no CBP ruling either way. On the 23 per-family checks (D171) 0.85 would show a plan on 21 of 23 instead of 15 of 23, adding 10 moves at 0.85–0.90 with no ruling to say whether they are right.
- **Reading:** a lower bar buys real recall on unknown-a and on the per-family products, but the held-out rows also show where it costs: two 2026 controls and one post-cutoff move CBP contradicts would be shown at 0.85. Dev alone could not have predicted either, which is why the bar stays until a scored run on new pairs tests a lower one.
- **Correction:** RESULTS.md and NUMBERS.md said one air-purifier probe had a move supported at 0.85. Two did (Champ one move, Waffle Cone two); both now say so.

## D284 - Every UI group label comes from its template name (#391)
- **Problem:** D270 added a mirror of the 14 templates' group names, but `families.ts` still kept ids separately and `plan-bits.tsx` kept a hard-coded phrase map for the legacy groups. A synthetic plan without a backend description still said "the PCBA" and "the LED PCBA", and `final_assembly` was forced to "Final assembly" even though the pumps template says "Final assembly and testing". `families.test.mjs` skipped `final_assembly` and so could not see the reuse.
- **Decision:** `families.ts` carries `{ id, name }` for every group of every family, exactly as the templates do. `groupName(id, family?)` uses the family's name when known and a stable first-name fallback otherwise; the plan phrase builder has no hard-coded group list and lower-cases only ordinary leading capitals, so acronyms stay. Screens that know the product family pass it through. `families.test.mjs` compares the full group objects and checks every `groupName`, including the reused `final_assembly` id, and checks phrases such as "the PCBA (SMT)" and "the final assembly and testing".
- **Evidence:** with the old phrase map restored, the new phrase assertions fail; with a single global `final_assembly` name, the template comparison fails on the pumps family. The backend's own descriptions were already template-named; this aligns the fallback and the group labels with them.

## D302 - PDF page limits follow the page tree, not raw /Type /Page matches (#381)
- **Problem:** `media.PDFPages` counted every raw `/Type /Page` match and the largest `/Count`, then took a maximum. An incrementally saved 3-page scan kept three older revisions of its three page objects and was refused as 12 pages; a 40-page PDF that wrote `/P#61ge` and `/P#61ges` (the standard PDF name escapes) plus one loose `/Type /Page` in a comment was counted as 1 page and sent to the model. A `/Pages` dictionary with a small `/Count` and no `/Kids` could hide loose pages too.
- **Decision:** `pdf.go` performs a bounded PDF parse: decode `#xx` only in names, read top-level objects (later revisions first), apply the classic xref `/Prev` chain's free entries, reach `/Root` → `/Pages` → `/Kids` (including object streams with Flate, ASCII85+Flate or ASCIIHex filters), and return the number of leaf page objects. A mismatched `/Count`, an unreadable object stream, a `/Pages` node without `/Kids`, or no resolvable tree returns 0, which `Check` already refuses as "pages could not be counted". There is no raw-text fallback. Inflate stays capped at 4 MB per stream.
- **Evidence:** new generators build complete xref tables: 3 pages rewritten in three incremental saves count 3, and 40 escaped pages with a stray comment count 40 and are refused by `POST /v1/products/extract-media` with "40 pages together; the limit is 10" before any model call. Object streams with a nested dictionary and with `/Filter [/ASCII85Decode /FlateDecode]` count correctly; loose pages and `/Count` without `/Kids` are refused. Restoring the old raw regex makes the tests report 12 and 1 (and accept loose pages); disabling `#xx` decoding makes the escaped 40-page file unresolvable. Both mutations fail the new tests.

## D303 - Joining checks the target workspace, not a capped invitation list (#374)
- **Problem:** #373's pre-check for `POST /v1/workspaces/{id}/join` listed the caller's pending invitations and answered 404 unless the target appeared in that list. `teams.MaxInvites` is 20, and pending invitations are never cleared except by joining. A 21st invitation could therefore never be accepted even though the store's own `Join` would accept it; on Firestore the limited, unordered query made which invitations were visible undefined.
- **Decision:** the handler reads the target workspace with `Workspaces.Get` and checks `HasInvite(email)` on it. A missing workspace or one without that invitation still returns the same 404 and writes only the hidden denial in the requester's own trail; a store error still returns 500. The capped `Invites` query remains for `GET /v1/workspaces/mine` (the UI list), where it belongs. The store's transactional `Join` remains the authority for the actual write.
- **Evidence:** `TestJoinBeyondInvitationListCap` creates 21 workspaces that each invite the same user, checks `/mine` still returns 20 invites, then joins the 21st through the real handler and gets 200. Restoring the capped-list pre-check makes that join 404. `TestJoinWithoutAnInvitationWritesNothingIntoThatWorkspace` still passes: an uninvited join writes no events into the target's trail.

## D304 - New plant ids skip yearly costs left by removed plants (#372)
- **Problem:** #371 made removal clear a plant from parts and steps, but the money drawer's `group_costs` are keyed by plant id and were left alone. `plantId` reused the smallest free id, so removing Monterrey (`p3`) and adding Gdansk gave Gdansk `p3` and the 400,000/yr entered for Mexico. The planner looked up that cost by id and marked a move to Gdansk `net_priced: true`, citing a price the user never entered for Poland.
- **Decision:** `plantId` takes the current economics and treats every id appearing in any `group_costs` row as taken, alongside ids held by plants, parts and steps. Both "Add a plant" and plants created by typing a new "Made at"/"At plant" name use it. Costs are not silently deleted or rewritten: an old entry stays visible only to the user, and a new plant gets a fresh id with no cost until the user enters one. If no cost was entered for the removed plant, its id can still be reused, as before.
- **Evidence:** `parts-editor-gaps.test.mjs` removes the costed Monterrey plant, adds a plant, reassigns the step, and checks the new id is not `p3` and has no `final_assembly` cost; the existing `p3` cost is untouched. A control with no money inputs still gets `p3` back. Removing the cost-reservation line makes the new test fail (`new id p3`). Planner's existing `partial_costs` golden already records that a move whose plant has no group-cost entry is not priced, so the new plant's plan cannot claim a fully priced net.

## D305 - Scenario predictions also name calibrated confidence (#492)
- **Problem:** #486 applied D265 to the case's own prediction, batch, BOM versions, watch, the `predicted` history event and the Ask `PREDICTION` line, but left two surfaces for a *scenario's* prediction quoting the model's stated 0.85 alone. The history drawer showed `As today: China 0.85` under a `predicted` event that read `calibrated 0.60; model stated 0.85`, and `agentCaseText` gave the agent a `SCENARIO ... at 0.85` line next to the corrected PREDICTION line. The /triage CSV's first confidence column was simply `confidence`, so a spreadsheet reader could mistake the stated number for the calibrated one.
- **Decision:** the `scenarios` history summary and `agentCaseText`'s `SCENARIO` lines call the same `confidencePhrase` helper: calibrated first with the model's own value labelled when a map attached one, and explicitly uncalibrated when there is no map. The /triage CSV header names its stated column `stated_confidence`, leaving `calibrated_confidence` beside it.
- **Evidence:** `TestCalibratedConfidenceInScenarioHistoryAndAsk` runs the real predict/scenarios endpoints with `calibrate.Must()`, checks the stored scenario carries 0.6, and asserts both the history summary and the Ask case text name `calibrated 0.60; model stated 0.85`. Restoring either old format makes the test fail. The four `golden281/flows_*.json` handler snapshots were regenerated for the map-off wording `confidence 0.97 as stated by the model, not calibrated`; nothing else in those goldens changed. `triage-csv.test.mjs` checks the header mapping; replacing `stated_confidence` with the old bare label fails that test.

## D306 - Same-bin ECE on every held-out set and in the product map (#493)
- **Problem:** #477 (D262) computed the stated-on-calibrated-bins ECE only for the 377 rows under cal-v1. The final2 and pooled cal-v1 rows, NUMBERS.md, and every cal-v2 surface still published an ECE pair with 9–11 bins before and 6 after, without saying that the map's coarser partition accounts for 16–20% of the drop. /accuracy and `GET /v1/eval/summary` were the most exposed: they showed 0.059 against 0.028 with no caveat.
- **Decision:** `build_accuracy.py` writes `stated_on_calibrated_bins`, `level_counts` and `calibrated_levels` for final2 and pooled under cal-v1 and for all three sets under cal-v2, keeping the existing `heldout_*` names on the 377. `calibrate.Report` computes the same fields in Go; the served ECE labels name the two bin counts, and a new `final_calibration_ece_stated_same_bins` item gives 0.0528 beside them. /accuracy shows that figure and says the errors use different bins. EVALUATION.md 4.2 (both tables), RESULTS.md (both tables), NUMBERS.md rows 35–36 and D160 repeat the counts and same-bin values. No probability, map step or bar changed; Brier is bin-independent.
- **Evidence:** `TestEvaluateSameBinPartition` ties three stated levels into the map's 0.99 cap and checks the common-bin value; `calibration-claims.test.mjs` checks all six generated field sets, the doc caveats, the served summary keys/labels and the /accuracy copy, and fails if the caveat or same-bin figure is removed. `build_accuracy.py --check`, `eval summary -check`, the Go tests and the frontend checks pass after regenerating the two artifacts.

## D302 — Broker review links reserve a lookup slot before the case lookup (21 Nov, review follow-up, follow-up to #489)
- **Problem:** D282 (#489) fixed the check-then-count race for API keys and left review-link tokens unchanged. `reviewByToken` still read the bucket with `allowed`, looked the case up, and only then counted the failure, so concurrent well-formed bad tokens from one client all reached the case store (a Firestore read each).
- **Decision:** `reviewByToken` uses the same `authFailures.begin` slot as `withAPIKeys`: reserved under the bucket's lock before the lookup, given back when the handler returns; only a bad token spends a failure token. No limit changed.
- **Evidence:** `TestBrokerReviewBadTokensThrottledUnderConcurrency` sends 30 concurrent well-formed unknown tokens from one client through the real handler with a 50 ms case store and a budget of 3: at most 3 lookups, the rest 429; it fails on the code before this change. The sequential test `TestBrokerReviewBadTokensAndDemos` still passes; `-race` passes on `httpapi`.

## D310 — Backtest counts only parts that changed origin, shows what the plan moves beyond them, and says it is not blind (21 Nov, judge panel round 5 item 2)
- **Problem:** the heat-gun backtest said the plan "moves 6 of the 7 parts" CBP's real change moved. The seventh, the outer shells, was already Thai in 2022: N328954, as N357771 recounts it, lists only the motor, PCBA, fan, switch, power cord, knob, back cover, motor support, heat insulator, wiring, support rings and fasteners as Chinese, and N357771 lists the shells among the Thai parts. So the count read as a miss that was not one. It also hid the other direction: the plan moves the switch, wires and fasteners, which N357771 says stayed Chinese. And the backtest was shown as validation without saying that three-group moves were added after the team saw this change (D84).
- **Decision:** the comparison is now stated: parts whose origin CBP's real change switched (made in the old country before, in the target after) against parts the plan moves. The demo's `actual_change` gains `already_in_target` (the outer shells) and `still_from_china_as`, which maps N357771's still-Chinese parts to the product's components (switch → switch, wires → wiring, fasteners → "support ring, heat insulator and fasteners"; terminal blocks have no component). `planner.backtest` leaves already-there parts out of `actual_moved` and reports `already_in_target` and `plan_also_moves_kept`. The stored production result predates these fields, so the plan step works the same view out from the stored backtest, the demo request and the product (`backtestView`, `plan-bits.tsx`). The heat gun now reads: all 6 changed parts moved; also moves the switch, wires and fasteners; outer shells not counted; not a blind test (D84), date cutoff still holds. "Matches CBP's actual change" now also needs the plan to move nothing the change kept in place.
- **Changed:** plan header band, backtest section (with the kept-in-China parts as chips and a "Next: the broker draft" link in the tour), landing sheet 3 and fig.1 label and the 2026 setup step, /method Q2, NUMBERS.md (the "6 of 7" row and the "Plan shown" row), DEMO.md. Legacy plan goldens (`testdata/golden281`) were regenerated: only the backtest lines changed (the shells moved from `actual_moved` to `already_in_target`); the money lines are byte-identical.
- **Not done:** the landing's 3D drawing still shows the whole switch, cord and minor-parts group as Thai in its 2026 stage; the mesh does not separate the switch, wiring and fasteners. The template still groups them with the cord, knob and back cover, so the search cannot express CBP's smaller move. No model calls.
