## D400 — Revocations from the Customs Bulletin; pre-registration of the parse (22 Nov, judge panel round 7, larger build)
- **Problem:** the supersession map (D320, D370) only knows revocations whose letter is in our corpus (35 edges). CBP publishes proposed and final revocations and modifications of ruling letters (19 U.S.C. § 1625(c)) in the weekly Customs Bulletin and Decisions, and most of those letters are not in the corpus.
- **Source, as fetched on 22 Nov:** 28 bulletins from vol. 57 no. 32 (6 Sep 2023) to vol. 60 no. 30 (30 Sep 2026), listed with URL and SHA-256 in `eval/data/bulletins/index.jsonl`. They were found by web search for bulletins whose first notice is a ruling-letter notice, within a cap of 40 web requests. The bulletin is weekly, so this is a sample chosen for having such notices, not a census. cbp.gov answered direct downloads from our network with HTTP 403, so the PDFs were retrieved with a web-reading tool; `go run ./cmd/corpus bulletins fetch` is the repeatable fetcher (one request a second) and checks the hashes.
- **Extraction (built, `internal/bulletin`):** `eval/bulletins/pdftext.py` (pypdf) turns each PDF into text. `corpus bulletins extract` cuts it into notices at each ACTION line whose text names a ruling letter, and commits a short excerpt per notice (`eval/data/bulletins/notices.jsonl`, public domain): the header to the effective date or comment deadline, and per attached ruling its number, subject line and the sentences that revoke or modify. 81 notices.
- **Parse rule (frozen with this entry):** a ruling is changed when an attached letter says it "is/are hereby revoked/modified", "we hereby revoke/modify" it, or lists it under EFFECT ON OTHER RULINGS as revoked or modified; numbers count only after "NY", "HQ" or "PC" or in a list that starts with one. The new ruling is the attached letter. A letter that another attachment revokes is an attached old letter and its own sentences are ignored. A notice is final when it states an EFFECTIVE DATE, withdrawn when its ACTION is a withdrawal, otherwise proposed. A parse is flagged when a final notice has no effective date, no ruling is found, a ruling the changing letter's subject line names is not changed in its text, or the count differs from the ACTION line's count (a floor when the subject says some rulings change "by operation of law"). At this freeze 3 of 81 notices are flagged (vol. 59 no. 8 p. 1, vol. 59 no. 35 p. 7, vol. 60 no. 16 p. 58).
- **Model fallback (pre-registered, not yet run):** only flagged notices go to `gemini-3.5-flash` through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini, temperature 0 with the fixed seed, one call per notice, JSON answer `{rulings: [{ruling, kind}]}` from the excerpt alone. For a flagged notice an edge is kept when the regex and the model both name it; a ruling only the model names is added only if its number appears verbatim in the excerpt. A failed or unparseable reply drops the notice's edges, counted as a parse failure. Replies are committed (`eval/data/bulletins/model_reads.jsonl`) so `make reproduce` makes no model call. Cap $6 (expected under $0.05). No prompt or rule changes after the run; any change is a new decision with both results.
- **Merge rule:** final changes become supersession edges with source `customs_bulletin`, dated by the effective date (D370: they count for cases dated strictly after it), and cite the bulletin's volume, number, printed page and URL. When the corpus already has the same edge (same ruling and revoking letter) the corpus edge and its letter date stay, and the bulletin citation is added. Proposed changes are listed separately as proposed: shown, never used to bar a precedent. A proposal is dropped when a fetched final notice changes the same ruling, or a fetched withdrawal names it.
- **Not a model evaluation:** nothing is scored and no held-out split is read. The effect is reported as the offline recount of `eval/supersession/impact.py`.
- **Later update (23 Nov, #721):** edges added by this parse change the enforced-edge fingerprint the verifier cache uses for its repair slots. See D729.

## D401 — Customs Bulletin revocations: results (22 Nov)
Run as pre-registered in D400. The rules were frozen at commit 0ec6b447 and the model runner at 31bbeb16, before the run; both are kept as branch `improve/customs-bulletin-freeze` (the merged history has new hashes).
- **Notices.** 28 bulletins, 81 ruling-letter notices: 38 final, 42 proposed, 1 withdrawal. 77 of the 80 non-withdrawal notices passed every parse check.
- **Model fallback.** The 3 flagged notices were each read once by `gemini-3.5-flash` ($0.0403 gateway-reported, `eval/data/bulletins/model_reads.jsonl`). Every reply parsed, and the model named every ruling the regex found, so none was dropped. It added 2 numbers that are in the excerpts: N159975 (vol. 59 no. 35 p. 7, a proposal; the letter's text misprints it as N15997, which stays because both readers name it) and 080651 (vol. 60 no. 16 p. 58, revoked by operation of law and named only in the subject line; a proposal). In vol. 59 no. 8 the EFFECT ON OTHER RULINGS section names H303733 where the subject line says H303773; both readers name both, so both are edges, as they already were from the corpus copy of the letter.
- **Merge.** 117 final changes (ruling and changing letter): 109 new edges, dated by the notice's effective date, and 8 already in the corpus, which keep their letter date and now cite the bulletin. The map (`supersession-v2`) has 144 edges on 143 rulings (70 revoked, 74 modified), 14 of them in a precedent pool (4 general, 10 Part 102; the new one is N326416, general pool, modified by H342508 effective 18 Oct 2026). 78 proposals are pending, none in a pool. The withdrawal names no fetched proposal.
- **Offline recount** (`eval/supersession/impact.py`, no model calls): unchanged at 23 rows showing and 8 citing a superseded precedent of 13,166 rows in 148 files. Only N326416 of the bulletin-only rulings appears in a committed row: 6 textile development rows for a case dated 11 Dec 2025, before the change took effect, so none counts.
- **What changes in the product.** The precedent filter, the verifier, the case agent's search, the cached-prediction check and the ruling API read the larger map, so a ruling a bulletin revoked is not cited for a case dated after its effective date, and its link says "superseded by". A proposal is shown beside the ruling ("CBP proposed to revoke it in H…") and in the API's `proposed` field; it never bars the ruling.
- **Limits.** The 28 bulletins are a sample of a weekly publication, chosen by web search for issues with ruling-letter notices, within a 40-request cap; changes in other issues are missed, and a proposal made final in an unfetched issue is still shown as proposed. The PDF text comes from pypdf and the parse reads CBP's own misprints as written. Corpus letters are dated by issue date and bulletin-only changes by effective date, so the two sources are not dated the same way; D400 kept the corpus date where both exist. cbp.gov refused direct downloads from our network (HTTP 403), so the PDFs were retrieved with a web-reading tool; the hashes in the index pin what was read.

## D402 — A duplicate plan search joins the one running (22 Nov, #574)
- **Problem:** the ADK run (#574, D391) showed an MCP client timing out at 300 s on `plan_production_moves` and retrying. Each call ran its own plan search, the heaviest model work the API does, so a retry could double the cost of a search whose answer was seconds away.
- **Decision:** the JSON plan route keeps a table of searches in flight, keyed by the case and a hash of everything the answer depends on (the planner request as priced, the money basis, the case's input fingerprint and whether the result is stored). A request with the same key waits for the running search and gets its answer. The search runs on a context detached from the request that started it, and stops 2 minutes after its last waiting caller leaves unless someone rejoins. An optional `Idempotency-Key` header (MCP: `idempotency_key`) keys the search by case and key instead, replays a finished answer for 15 minutes (at most 256 per instance), and refuses the same key with other inputs (409 `conflict`). A failed search is not kept. The result is stored on the case once, by the search.
- **Alternatives:** a shared table in Firestore would join retries across instances, at a write per plan request and a lease to manage; not done. Joining streamed requests would need fan-out of the event stream; the website does not retry plan searches.
- **Evidence:** `TestPlanFlightsRunOncePerKey` (8 concurrent callers, 1 run), `TestPlanFlightsOutliveATimedOutCaller`, `TestPlanFlightsCancelWhenNobodyComesBack`, `TestPlanFlightsIdempotencyKey`, `TestPlanRouteJoinsADuplicateSearch` (3 concurrent requests, 1 planner call; replay; 409; bad key 400), `TestPlanSendsTheIdempotencyKey`; run with `-race`.
- **Limits:** in memory, per instance. A joining request still takes a heavy rate-limit token and an in-flight slot while it waits; the model cost is charged to the caller that started the search. Streamed requests are not joined. Correction (D411, #581): as first built, a search that kept running after every caller had left held no in-flight slot, so one client could run more searches at once than `RATE_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` by dropping requests. The starting caller's slot now stays with the search until it ends.

## D410 — The per-part HTS cache is per caller and keyed on the description (22 Nov, #577)
- **Problem:** D380 cached each per-part answer for a day under the part's and the product's name, in one map shared by every caller. The description goes into the prompt and the model writes its reasons from it, so a later caller with the same part and product name got the first caller's codes and reasons, written from the first caller's description, flagged `cached`. The route is classed as holding no case data, but the cache carried one caller's text to another.
- **Decision:** the cache key is a SHA-256 of the prompt version, the caller's scope, and everything about the part that goes into the prompt: the part's words, where it is made, and the product's name and description (lower case, punctuation dropped, the description cut as it is sent). The scope is the signed-in user's workspace (else the user), the API key, the visitor ID, else the client address bucket. A request with no scope (the evaluation, `NoCache`) caches nothing. Cached answers are never served across scopes, so no caller sees model text made from another caller's input.
- **Alternatives:** caching only the ruling candidates, which hold no caller input, was simpler but would drop the saving on a repeated request; the BM25 search is local and cheap, so there was nothing to share across callers. Not caching at all was the fallback.
- **Evidence:** `TestPartsCacheNeverCrossesCallersOrDescriptions` (hts: another scope, another description, or both, each asks the model again, and no reason carries the first description), `TestPartsHTSSuggestCacheIsPerCallerAndDescription` (route: two visitors and an anonymous caller), the key test in `TestPartsSuggestDeduplicatesAndCachesPerProduct`.
- **Limits:** members of one workspace share cached answers, as they share cases. A visitor who changes their visitor ID loses their cache. Still in memory, per instance, a day, at most 2,000 answers.

## D411 — A detached plan search keeps its caller's in-flight slot (22 Nov, #581)
- **Problem:** D402 runs a JSON plan search on a context detached from its request, and keeps it for 2 minutes after the last caller leaves. The in-flight slot (`RATE_MAX_IN_FLIGHT`) was given back when the handler returned, so a client that dropped its requests could have more searches running than the cap: the issue's offline repro showed 4 at once with a cap of 1.
- **Decision:** `limit` puts the request's slot in its context. When a request starts a new search, the search takes the slot over and gives it back when the search ends (finished, failed, or cancelled after the grace period), not when the handler returns. A joining or replayed request does not take it over: it holds its own slot only while it waits, as before. Each slot is given back exactly once.
- **Evidence:** `TestDetachedPlanSearchKeepsItsInFlightSlot` (cap 1: start a search, drop the request, then three plan requests with other targets get 429 `too_many_in_flight` and start no search; after the first search ends a new one runs), `TestJoiningPlanRequestHoldsASlotOnlyWhileWaiting`; both with `-race`. With the hand-off removed the first test fails with 4 searches running.
- **Limits:** per instance, like the cap itself. A client still gets the heavy rate limit on starts; a dropped search counts against its cap for up to the search time plus the 2-minute grace. The dropped request is still logged as an error.

## D412 — Rule-check parser: a trailing limitation and "or from" lists (22 Nov, #550, #551; post-freeze bug fix)
- **Problem:** two parser errors in the D360 rule layer, found after the D361 freeze. (#550) In "from any other heading, or from subheading 8481.90 except when resulting from a simple assembly" (8481.10–8481.80) and the GRI 2(a) twin on 8716.10–8716.80, the limitation qualifies the last listed source, but the parser applied it to the whole alternative. A material from another heading then needed the simple-assembly or GRI 2(a) fact, and with the fact stated it failed the shift, so 102.11(b) could name the material's country. Synthetic examples gave China where the row text gives the producing country. (#551) An exception list was split into exceptions only at ", or from" and ", and from" with the comma. In "except from subheading 9001.90 or from lens blanks of heading 7014" (9002), the two 9030 rows and three 8485 rows, a code-only exception was merged with a described one, so a material in that code was always "needs a fact" instead of "no shift".
- **Change:** a trailing "except when resulting from a simple assembly" or "except when that change is pursuant to GRI 2(a)" with no comma after a listed source that follows other sources is now a condition on that source (`not_simple_assembly`, or the new `not_gri_2a`). Set off by a comma, or after the only source, it still limits the whole alternative (8409.91–8409.99, 8540.91–8540.99, 8544.11–8544.70, 7315, 7321 are unchanged). An exception list splits at "or from" and "and from" with or without a comma and at a bare ", from"; a segment that starts with a number takes the level word before it ("from 8486.10 through 8486.40"). A trailing condition still goes to the last segment. `rules.json` is regenerated from its committed text with the new `go run ./cmd/tariffshift rules -reparse` (no eCFR download). 12 alternatives change: the 8481 and 8716 rows, the 9002, 9030.89, 9030.90 and three 8485 rows, the 8471.60–8472.90 exception (same meaning, now two exceptions), and a trailing comma dropped from three chapter 94 exception texts. Still 332 of 515 alternatives encoded.
- **Evidence:** `TestTrailingLimitationAttachesToTheLastSource` (the five #550 rows and the two decided cases, which now give Mexico and Canada under 102.11(a)(3); the whole-alternative rows still flagged) and `TestExceptionListsSplitWithoutAComma` (the six #551 materials give "no shift", the 9030.32 comma control still does, and materials in described segments stay "needs a fact"). With the old `rules.json` 13 of their checks fail. `TestRulesJSONMatchesParser` uses the same re-parse.
- **Re-run of the offline evaluations (no model calls, committed extractions and suggestions):** `go run ./cmd/tariffshift eval -check` (D362) and `go run ./cmd/tariffshift parts-eval -check` (D382) were run before and after the fix. Their output is identical. D362 stays: full ruling text, dev 2 of 72 and final 2 of 32 decided, all agreeing with CBP; facts 0 of 117. D382 stays: dev 9 of 69 decided with CBP's good code and the top part suggestions (9 agree), 10 of 69 with the suggested good code (9 agree); held-out 7 of 29 (6 agree) and 8 of 29 (7 agree); with CBP's stated codes 2 and 2. No committed row has a good of 8481.10–8481.80, 8716.10–8716.80, 9002, 9030.89, 9030.90 or 8485, and the extractions state no simple-assembly or GRI 2(a) facts, so no decision could change.
- **Held-out integrity:** this is a bug fix in the rule encoding, made from the regulation's text and synthetic cases, not from any held-out result. Both results are reported and are the same.

## D413 — Code stripping for the per-part evaluation; the leaked inputs reported (22 Nov, #576; post-freeze correction)
- **Problem:** D381 states that the suggester sees the facts "with every HTS number replaced" and that "no product carries a code". The v1 stripper (`stripCodes` in `cmd/tariffshift/parts.go`) needed a space between "subheading" and the number, removed only the first code of a list ("headings 8539 and 8540"), left the last two digits of a 10-digit code ("[code removed]00"), and did not touch the product name taken from the ruling's subject.
- **Change:** `stripCodes` now removes a code glued to the word before it, every code of a list after a heading word or before ", HTSUS", and whole 10-digit codes; it also runs on the product name. "The 2024 HTSUS" keeps its year. The frozen v1 stripper is kept as `stripCodesV1`; `parts-eval` rebuilds the inputs the committed runs saw and lists, per cell, the products whose input still carried a number of 4 digits or more (`input_codes` in `parts/summary.json`), and reports each cell without them (`without_input_codes`). The two last digits v1 left behind are not counted: they carry no heading or subheading.
- **Which inputs carried a code:** held out (5 of 29): N363600 "8419.34.0000" (the importer's code, which the model then proposed for the good), H351116 "9802.00.40", "9802.00.80" (in the name; chapter 98, which the suggester never returns) and "5405", and H355020, N357063, N364586 "3914" (the end of "headings 3901 to 3914" in the quoted text of heading 3926). Dev (4 of 69): H342474 "8540", N339851 "4421", N343893 "4016", "8484", N352810 "3914". The family fixtures carried none.
- **Re-scored without them (offline, no model calls; the committed suggestions are not re-run):**

| Split | Figure | As run | Without inputs that carried a code |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| final (held out) | rule check, top suggestion for the good and every part | 8 of 29 decided, 7 agree | 7 of 24, 6 agree |
| final (held out) | rule check, CBP's good code and top part suggestions | 7 of 29, 6 agree | 7 of 24, 6 agree |
| final (held out) | good's code, top-1 / top-3 | 14 / 15 of 27 | 12 / 12 of 23 |
| final (held out) | part top-1 / top-3 | 2 / 2 of 3 | 2 / 2 of 3 |
| dev | rule check, CBP's good code and top part suggestions | 9 of 69, 9 agree | 8 of 65, 8 agree |
| dev | rule check, top suggestion for the good and every part | 10 of 69, 9 agree | 10 of 65, 9 agree |
| dev | good's code, top-1 / top-3 | 36 / 42 of 68 | 34 / 39 of 64 |
| dev | part top-1 / top-3 | 20 / 22 of 27 | 20 / 21 of 26 |

- **Reading:** only N363600 is a clear leak into a decided rule-check figure. The three plastics products saw "3914", the last code of a range quoted from heading 3926's text, not the good's own code; their good top-3 hits are left out above to be safe, which is why held-out good top-3 drops from 15 to 12. We cannot tell offline what the model would have proposed without the leaks. Re-suggesting the 5 held-out products (about $0.06) was not done: it would be a second score on the held-out split.
- **On /method:** the pooled "16 of 98, 15 agree" is now given per split, as pre-registered: development 9 of 69 (9 agree), held out 7 of 29 (6 agree), with CBP's code for the good and the top part suggestions. That held-out row is unchanged by this correction.
- **Evidence:** `TestStripCodes`, `TestEvalProductsHideCodes` (every dev and held-out product's name and description, checked with a detector written apart from the stripper), `TestInputCodesOfTheCommittedRuns` (pins the list above); `parts-eval -check` in `make reproduce`.

## D430 — The rule check says whether its answer holds under every suggested part code (22 Nov, judge panel round 9, N2, N3, N4, N1)
- **Problem:** the rule check reads one code per part. When that code came from the suggester (D380), it is the top of up to three, and the top one can be wrong. On the recorded example (D421) the strip's top code, 7219.33, is for stainless steel 600 mm wide or more; the ruling's facts give coils 3 to 12 inches wide, so 7220.20 (under 600 mm), the second suggestion, is the likely code. The page did not say whether that changes the answer.
- **Decision:** a part can carry its other suggested codes (`components[].hts_alternatives`, at most 2, filled by the parts table when a suggestion is accepted and dropped when a code is typed). The rule check then runs on every combination of each part's codes and returns `rule_check.robustness`: whether every combination gives the same status and origin ("the same answer for every suggested code"), and, if not, which part's code alone changes it ("depends on the code for …"). Past 81 combinations it runs a deterministic sample of 81: the codes carried, every single-part change from them, then evenly spaced combinations; the result says it was sampled. Display only, like the check itself: the prediction, triage and auto-accept never read it. MCP: `predict_origin` and `get_case` add one sentence, and `suggest_part_hts` asks the agent to pass the other codes. The case panel shows one line, flagged when the answer depends on a code.
- **The recorded example:** the same answer (Canada) under 7219.33 and 7220.20. `parts-example` writes the robustness into the example and fails if it stops being stable. The recorded suggestions are not edited; our note on the strip's code is a separate field marked as added after the run.
- **Offline count (no model calls; committed D382 suggestions and D361 extractions; a figure added after the freeze, and the first time held-out rows are read for it):** each ruling the check decides with the top suggestions is re-checked over every combination of each part's top-3 codes.

| Split | Rule-check input | Decided | Same answer for every suggested code | Of those, agree with CBP | Depends on a part's code |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| dev | CBP's good code, top part suggestions | 9 of 69 | 8 | 8 | N338219 (cover and main-board castings) |
| dev | top suggestion for the good and every part | 10 of 69 | 9 | 8 | N338219 |
| final (held out) | CBP's good code, top part suggestions | 7 of 29 | 6 | 6 | N358639 (steel pipes) |
| final (held out) | top suggestion for the good and every part | 8 of 29 | 6 | 6 | N358639, N364328 |

- **Reading:** most decisions hold whichever suggested code is used. On the held-out row with CBP's good code, the one decision that disagrees with CBP (N358639, Mexico) is the one that depends on a part's code; with n = 7 that is one case, not a rate. 4 dev and 3 held-out decided rulings have more than 81 combinations, so "stable" there means stable over the sample. Without the inputs that carried a code (D413): dev 8 decided, 7 stable; held-out with CBP's good code 7 decided, 6 stable; held-out with the suggested good 7 decided, 5 stable. Source: `robustness` in `eval/tariffshift/parts/summary.json`, recomputed by `parts-eval -check` in `make reproduce`.
- **Also:** /method's rule-check paragraph gives the held-out figure as "7 of 29 (6 agree); 7 of 24 (6 agree) without the inputs that carried a code" (D413) and links the recorded example, as does /accuracy's HTS section. A stray copy of D402's old "Limits" bullet under D413, left by a merge in #582, is removed; D402 keeps its corrected text.
- **Evidence:** `TestRobustSameUnderEitherCode`, `TestRobustDependsOnOnePart`, `TestRobustNilWithoutAlternatives`, `TestRobustSamples` (729 combinations, a repeatable sample of 81), `TestRuleCheckRobustnessOverSuggestedCodes` (API: stored, read back, more than 2 alternatives refused), `TestRuleCheckLine` (MCP), `rule-check.test.mjs`, `parts-hts.test.mjs`, `rule-check-example.test.mjs`.
- **Limits:** only the parts' codes vary; the good's code and the facts (simple assembly, GRI 2(a), value shares) stay as given. Stable does not mean right: every suggested code can be wrong the same way. A typed code has no alternatives, so the line appears only for accepted suggestions.

## D440 — Pre-registration: the 102.20 rule check on each committed plan move (22 Nov, judge panel round 9, item 3)
Committed before the per-move check exists in code and before any move is checked. Offline, no model calls. Nothing below changes because of a result.
- **What is checked.** For each move of a committed plan search, the product as it would be after the move (`planner.Apply`: the moved groups' parts take the target plant's country), the good produced where the final-assembly group is (else the plant of the last operation, else the only plant, as D363), and the 19 CFR 102.20 rule check (`tariffshift`, D360, with the D412 parser) on the good's code and every part's code and country. Each move gets one status: `shifts` (the check decides and names the target), `no_shift` (it decides another country because at least one foreign part does not make the required change), `other_country` (it decides another country although no part fails, because the good is still finished elsewhere) or `undetermined`, with the reason class: out of scope (the good's chapter is not encoded), a part with no code, a fact the codes cannot give (simple assembly, GRI 2(a), a described alternative), the value of the parts that do not shift (102.13 de minimis), essential character to be judged (102.11(b) between countries), a chapter note, or the country of production not known. The current setup (the baseline row) is checked the same way and counted apart.
- **Which runs.** Every committed plan search whose product gives the good's code and every part's code, as committed: expected none (no committed plan fixture carries part codes; only the heat gun gives the good's code). Then the 23 per-family plan searches of D171 (`eval/results/planner-families-*-litellm.json`, fixtures `backend/testdata/planner_families`, dev and train rulings, none held out) with codes filled in from the D381 development run only (`eval/tariffshift/parts/suggest-dev-v1.jsonl`, set `family`): the top suggestion for the good and for every part. No held-out suggestion file (`suggest-final.jsonl`) is read. All 23 targets are outside Canada and Mexico and every family case is decided under substantial transformation, so every check here is informational: there is no committed Part 102-routed plan search to count.
- **Counts.** Moves (plans and rejected moves, not the current-setup row) per status and per undetermined reason; plan searches with at least one decided move. For decided moves with a precedent check (`verdict`): agree when the check is precedent-supported and the rule says `shifts`, or not supported and the rule names another country; disagree otherwise, split into "precedent supports, rule gives another country" (the review flag) and "rule shifts, precedent not supported". For every decided move: agreement with the engine's predicted origin (target or not). For the current setup: decided, and agreement with CBP's held origin of the fixture's ruling and with the engine's baseline prediction.
- **Later ruling.** None of the 23 fixtures has a later ruling on a changed setup (no backtest). The plan searches that have one (the heat gun, the D170 post-cutoff pairs) have no part codes and no recorded suggestions, so the rule cannot be compared with a later CBP holding on a move here: reported as 0, not estimated.
- **Reading.** Substantial transformation, not 102.20, decides these cases, so agreement with the precedent check is not accuracy. A disagreement says where the two tests part, which is what the review flag is for. The suggested codes are unverified (D382: dev top-1 20 of 27 gold parts), and the fixtures carry no part values, so the de minimis test cannot run.
- **Expectation stated now:** low coverage. The good's chapter is encoded for most families, but part codes from other chapters, described alternatives and missing values leave most moves undetermined; a handful of searches with a decided move at most.
- **Tool.** `go run ./cmd/tariffshift plans-eval` writes one row per move and the summary to `eval/tariffshift/plans/`; `-check` recomputes it from committed files and is part of `make reproduce`.

## D441 — Each plan move carries the 102.20 rule check, display only (22 Nov, judge panel round 9, item 3)
- **Problem:** the planner moves operation groups between plants and the verifier checks each move against CBP precedent. The deterministic 19 CFR 102.20 check (D360, D363) ran only on the case as it is. A Part 102 case could get a plan the tariff-shift rule does not support, and nothing said so.
- **What:** `backend/internal/planrule` checks each move. It applies the move to the product (`planner.Apply`: the moved groups' parts take the target plant's country), takes the country where the final-assembly group would be (else the plant of the last operation, else the only plant: the D363 rule, now shared with the case check), and runs `tariffshift.Evaluate` on the good's code and every part's code and country. Each plan, and the current setup, gets `rule_check`: `status` `shifts` (the rule gives the target), `no_shift` (it gives another country because a foreign part fails the change), `other_country` (it gives another country although no part fails: the good is still finished there) or `undetermined` with `why` (out of scope, a part without a code, a fact the codes cannot give, the de minimis value, essential character, a chapter note, no country). `label` says it in a few words ("Shifts under 102.20 (8543.70)", "Does not shift under 102.20 (blade fails) unless de minimis", "102.20 undetermined (no code for 2 parts)"), with the rule, basis, reason and the parts that fail.
- **Where it applies:** on a Part 102-routed case, always (an undetermined check says which codes to add). On a substantial-transformation case, only when the good and every part have a code, marked `applies: informational`; without codes nothing is shown. `RULE_CHECK=off` removes it with the case's check.
- **Never changes a plan:** it is added when a plan search is returned (the plan response, the streamed `baseline`, `move_done` and `done` events) or read (`GET /v1/cases/{id}`, its `plan` and each comparison's searches), from the case's product, and is never stored. The verdict, `shown`, the tier and the order are what they were. `TestPlanMovesCarryTheRuleCheck` reads the stored case and finds no check on it; `TestAnnotateNeverChangesThePlans` checks that the input plans are not written to.
- **Disagreement is a flag:** when the rule decides and the move has a precedent check, `agrees_with_precedent` says whether they agree. "An earlier ruling supports this move, but the 102.20 rule gives another country" sets `review` with a note. "The rule gives the target, but no ruling supports the move" sets `review` only on a Part 102 case, where 102.20 is the marking rule; on a substantial-transformation case it is not the test, so a flag there would be noise. The flag changes nothing; a person decides.
- **Screens and MCP:** the plan card and each row of the moves table show a chip with the label: calm, or amber with the note when `review` is set (the case panel's style, D363). A line above the table says the check is display only, and for comparison on a substantial-transformation case. `plan_production_moves` lists the label after each move, with the flag, and says the check is display only (`planLine`, `planRuleWords`).
- **Not done:** the per-move check reads each part's accepted code only, not its other suggested codes (`hts_alternatives`, D430), so it does not say whether a move's answer depends on the code; the broker draft and the country-comparison table do not show it; ranking by "precedent and tariff shift both support" (the panel's next step) is not built. Moves are checked with the codes the user gave or accepted, never with suggestions the user has not accepted.

## D442 — The rule check on the committed plan moves: results (22 Nov)
Counted as pre-registered in D440 (committed first as 726d0239, kept as branch `improve/p9-plans102-prereg`; the merged history has new hashes), offline (`go run ./cmd/tariffshift plans-eval -check`, in `make reproduce`). No model call; $0.
- **Coverage of committed data:** 43 committed plan fixtures, none of which gives every part's code as committed; 0 committed Part 102-routed plan searches; 0 moves with both codes and a later CBP ruling. So nothing here compares the rule with CBP on a changed setup.
- **The 23 per-family searches with the D381 development suggestions:** 57 moves. 25 decided (22 `shifts`, 3 `other_country`), in 14 of the 23 searches; 32 undetermined: 24 need a fact (17 because a rule sentence names goods in words, 5 the GRI 2(a) fact, 1 a goods description, 1 simple assembly), 7 the de minimis value of the parts that do not shift (the fixtures give no values), 1 out of scope (the suggested good code is in chapter 63).
- **Against the precedent check:** 23 decided moves have one; 21 agree. The 2 that do not are both from N354220 (a survival tool, target Vietnam): an earlier ruling supports moving the machining to Vietnam, but the good is still finished in China, so the rule gives China. Both are below the plan bar, so neither is a shown plan. No move had the rule shift with no ruling in support. 15 of the 19 shown plans are decided, and the rule gives the target for all 15.
- **Against the engine:** 20 of 25 decided moves agree with the engine's predicted origin (target or not).
- **The current setup:** 11 of 23 decided; 4 give CBP's held origin and 3 the engine's prediction. These cases are decided under substantial transformation, and Part 102 often gives the assembly country where substantial transformation does not (N350727: assembled in Thailand from a Chinese PCBA, CBP held China, the rule gives Thailand). This is a difference between the two tests, not an error count.
- **Reading:** coverage is higher than D440 expected (25 of 57 moves), but 9 of the 22 `shifts` hold because the move puts every part in the target (102.11(a)(2)), which needs no tariff shift at all. The codes are unverified suggestions (D382), the good's code included. Agreement with the precedent check is not accuracy: these are substantial-transformation cases, and on a Part 102 case the rule, not precedent, is the marking test. There is no Part 102 plan search with codes to score yet.
- **Rows:** `eval/tariffshift/plans/moves-dev.jsonl` (one row per move and current setup), `eval/tariffshift/plans/summary.json`.

## D450 — ADK agent evaluation: the set, what is scored, written before the scored run (22 Nov, judge panel round 9, item 5)
- **Why:** the ADK agent (`examples/adk-agent`, D391, D422) had run once, on one product. This scores it on several, with rules fixed before the scored run.
- **Set:** `eval/agent/products.jsonl`, 14 products, each from a ruling in the development split (`eval/splits/splits_final.json` `dev`, Jul–Dec 2025); none is in a held-out split, and `eval/agent/score.py` fails if one is. Each holds a short product description written by hand from the ruling's facts (parts, where each is made, where it is assembled), the product family, a target country for production moves, whether the description names a plant in that country (10 do, 4 do not), and CBP's held origin from `labels.jsonl`. Every prompt asks for the same task: predict the origin, plan moves to the target, draft for a broker. Products a01–a12 are the live set.
- **Expected tool sequence:** `extract_product` → `predict_origin` → `plan_production_moves` → `export_ruling_request_draft`. `suggest_part_hts` is allowed after extract, `get_ruling` anywhere.
- **Scored per run** (`eval/agent/score.py`):
  1. Tool order: each required tool called (export only when the plan search showed a plan), first calls in the order above, no tool outside the six offered, `predict_origin` at most once (a second call makes a second case), plan repeated only after a failed call and with the same idempotency key.
  2. Arguments: extract gets the description and the named family; predict gets a structured product and the named family; plan gets the target country named in the prompt, a non-empty `idempotency_key`, the case `predict_origin` made, and that call's `case_access_key`; export gets the same case and key and a `move_key` or `plan_index`. Reported apart, not in the pass: when the description names no plant in the target country, did the agent add one to the product (the instruction asks it to).
  3. Origin: the final answer's first sentence that speaks of the predicted or likely origin names the origin `predict_origin` returned (or, with no such sentence, the answer names it somewhere). Read by hand as well.
  4. Rulings: the answer cites at least one ruling number that some tool result contains (text or structuredContent); any ruling number in the answer that no tool returned counts as invented.
  5. The line "Not a ruling — confirm with a licensed customs broker." word for word (a dash-insensitive match is reported too).
  6. Cost (agent model, gateway-reported) and wall time per run. The tools' own model calls run on Unde's side and are not in this cost.
  A run passes when it finishes and meets 1–5.
- **Not an accuracy figure:** whether `predict_origin` agrees with CBP is reported, but the source ruling is in the precedent pool the engine retrieves from, so agreement here measures nothing about the engine. The engine's accuracy is the held-out rows in NUMBERS.
- **Runs:** first a scripted stand-in for the model against a local server with `LLM_PROVIDER=fake` (plumbing; no model, no cost). Then, budget allowing (sub-cap $2 for this item), one scored run: the agent on Gemini 3.8 Flash through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini, against `https://undelabs.dev/mcp`, anonymously, on a01–a12, one run each, three at a time. Each run makes one anonymous case and one plan search. Every run is kept and scored, failures included; the agent's instruction is not changed between runs.

## D460 — Pre-registration: ten more chapters in the 102.20 rule check (22 Nov, judge panel round 9, item 4)
Committed with the code, before any evaluation is re-run with the wider rules. Offline, no model calls. Nothing below changes because of a result.
- **Which chapters, and why.** The rule check (D360) encodes chapters 73, 82, 84, 85, 87, 90 and 94. The goods' chapters were counted on development and earlier data only, not held-out (rule: select on development): the 69 development Part 102 rulings with CBP's code in the full-text extraction (D361) and the first HTS code in the facts of the 356 earlier labelled Part 102 rulings (dated before 2024; 126 have one). 95 of those 195 goods are already in scope. Every other chapter with at least 4 goods is added: 44 wood (12), 39 plastics (11), 48 paper (10), 83 miscellaneous base metal (5), 95 toys and sports goods (5), 15 fats and oils (4), 21 food preparations (4), 40 rubber (4), 71 jewellery (4), 76 aluminium (4). None is textile (102.21). The 14 planner families' goods add nothing: their suggested good codes are all in scope but one (chapter 63, textile). Script output: `eval/tariffshift/chapter-counts.json`.
- **Source.** The same eCFR XML of 19 CFR Part 102 as D360 (point in time 18 Nov 2026, retrieved 22 Nov); `rules -ecfr` rebuilds the table with the new chapter list, and the seven existing chapters come out byte for byte the same. No new fetch.
- **Parser changes, made from the regulation's text and synthetic cases only.** (1) A "provided that" proviso on content or weight ("less than 65 percent by dry weight of sugar") makes the sentence not encoded; the simple-assembly proviso is unchanged. (2) An exception for goods "of other materials of headings 3901 to 3914 of heading 9619" names goods of heading 9619; the inner headings are their material. (3) A chapter note that sends listed codes to 102.21 (the chapter 39 note) marks those codes out of scope, and a code too short to tell is undetermined. (4) Lists read 10-digit codes. (5) The eCFR prints a second row for headings 4413-4421 with the column "4441-4421"; its sentences change to heading 4413 through 4421, so it is read as that range, and a good there is undetermined ("more than one rule covers") rather than one row being picked. Sentences that describe goods in words stay not encoded, as before.
- **What is reported, before and after, nothing else changed:** (a) D361/D362 on the committed extractions: per split and input, out of scope, decided, agrees with CBP (Wilson interval), differs from the model; (b) D381/D382 rule-check rows: CBP's codes; CBP's good code with the top part suggestions; the top suggestions for the good and every part; each out of scope, decided, agrees with CBP; (c) D430 robustness over the suggested codes per D382 row: decided, same answer for every suggested code, of those agreeing with CBP, which rulings depend on a part's code; (d) D440/D442 plan-move counts. Every new disagreement with CBP is named with its ruling. Also: rules and alternatives encoded per chapter.
- **Held out.** Development (dev rows, family fixtures) is computed first. If it shows a bug in the encoding, the fix is made from the regulation's text, disclosed and the development figures re-run; then the code is frozen at a named commit and the held-out rows (`final`, `final2`) are computed once. No held-out result changes the code.
- **Expectation stated now:** small gains. On the facts input, coverage stays near zero (the facts rarely give part codes). On the full text and with suggested codes, a few more development and held-out rulings in plastics, aluminium and base-metal goods may be decided; toys (9503), most paper of 4811 and 4823.90, and wood of 4413-4421 stay undetermined because their rows are written by description or doubled. The plan-move counts should not change: the families' goods are already in scope.

## D480 — Revocation alerts on saved cases (22 Nov, judge panel round 9)
- **Problem:** the supersession guard (D320, D370, D400, D401) stops Unde citing a ruling CBP had already revoked or modified at the case date. A saved case is not looked at again: when CBP changes a ruling the case relied on after the case was decided, nothing told the user. The ruling watch (re-check with later rulings) runs only when someone asks for it.
- **Decision (built):** `domain.RulingAlerts` lists, for each ruling a saved case relies on, CBP's change to it from the committed map (`backend/internal/domain/supersession.json`). Relied on means cited by the prediction, a shown plan's supporting ruling, or the ruling given as CBP's holding on the current setup (`store.Case.RulingRefs`); rulings the prediction only read are listed apart. A final change is reported at any date: on or after the case date it is a change since the case; before it (`before_case`) the guard would refuse the citation today, so only an answer stored before the guard can carry it. A final change whose effective date is after today is "scheduled" (`in_effect` absent). A ruling with no final change and a pending proposal is "proposed": shown, never applied, as in D400.
- **Where it shows:** worked out at read time, never stored. `GET /v1/cases/{id}` carries `ruling_alerts {counts, items, rechecked_at}` only when there is one, so every other case reads byte for byte as before; each `GET /v1/cases` row carries `ruling_alerts {final, proposed}` only then. The case page shows a box above every step: the "look again" style when a relied-on ruling has a final change ("Ruling N… cited by this answer was revoked by H… on …. Re-check recommended."), the calm style for proposals and rulings only read. The cases list shows "1 cited ruling revoked or modified" under the case name. MCP `get_case` adds a "Changed rulings:" line and `list_cases` a count per case. /method question 2 says it in one sentence.
- **Re-check:** the stored answer is never changed. "Re-check now" calls the existing per-case ruling watch (`POST /v1/cases/{id}/watch`, its rate limit and the spend caps unchanged), which predicts again with today's rulings and so without revoked ones; afterwards the box says when it was re-checked (`rechecked_at`: the watch ran on or after the latest final change in force). A pinned demo cannot be re-checked, as before (D220). The admin watch job (`POST /v1/watch/run`) now also returns `ruling_alerts` by case id, and with `alerts_only=true` returns only those, re-running nothing and calling no model. It stays admin-only; no deploy, schedule or workflow change.
- **Tests:** `TestRulingAlertsTimeEdges` (revoked before, on and after the case date), `TestRulingAlertsScheduledBulletinChange`, `TestRulingAlertsProposedVersusFinal`, `TestRulingAlertsMultipleCitations`, `TestCaseShowsRevocationAlerts`, `TestCaseWithoutChangedRulingsHasNoAlertField`, `TestWatchRunListsRevocationAlerts`, `TestRecheckAfterRevocationMarksTheAlert`, `TestAlertOnAnswerStoredBeforeTheGuard` (all with `-race`), `TestGetCaseWordsRulingAlerts`, `frontend/scripts/ruling-alerts.test.mjs`.
- **Not done:** the map only knows the 28 fetched bulletins and the corpus letters (D401 limits), so an alert can be missing; no one is notified by email or push, the alert shows when the case is opened or listed, or in the admin job's answer; chat answers' citations are not checked.

## D470 — Agent evaluation follow-ups: plan_id, the no-plan line, the current-setup draft, long names; a fix check written before it runs (22 Nov)
- **Why:** D451 listed what the evaluation saw and did not fix: two drafts where one was asked for (a04, a10), an answer that claimed a move works after a plan search that supported none (a03), and a `predict_origin` call refused because `extract_product` returned a 203-character operation name (a06). Built here.
- **One way to name a plan.** Every plan a response returns (plan search, its stream, case read, country comparison) now carries `plan_id`, its move key (`group@plant` joined by `+` in move order). It is added when the plan is returned or read, like the rule check (D441), and never stored. `POST /export` and `POST /reviews` take `plan_id` and read it as `move_key` (both given: they must agree; with `plan_index`: 400). `plan_index` keeps working; its descriptions now say it counts from 0 (0 is the first shown plan), and an out-of-range index says so. In the MCP text, `plan_production_moves` lists plans as `- plan_id <id> (plan_index <n>): ...` with no 1-based number beside them (the old "1." beside `plan_index` 0 is what a04 and a10 misread), and `structuredContent` carries `plan_index` on each shown plan. Tool descriptions (`plan_production_moves`, `export_ruling_request_draft`, `create_broker_review_link`) and OpenAPI updated.
- **No plan.** When a search shows no plan, the MCP text says, word for word, "No move is supported by an earlier ruling; do not claim a move changes origin." and that `export_ruling_request_draft` without `plan_id`, `plan_index` or `move_key` drafts the current setup. That export behaviour is not new; it is now stated in the tool and OpenAPI descriptions.
- **Agent instruction** (`examples/adk-agent/unde_agent/agent.py`, steps 4 and 5): with no supported plan, say that and nothing more (the predicted origin stands; no move is said to work); call export once, with the plan's `plan_id`, or with no plan selector for the current setup.
- **Long names (a06).** `extract_product` cuts a part or operation name over 200 characters (the MCP product schema's limit) at a word boundary and says so in a warning, so its draft can go to `predict_origin` as returned.
- **Scorer.** `eval/agent/score.py` accepts `plan_id` as the export's plan selector (it is the move key under its new name). No other rule changes; the committed rows score as before.
- **Fix check, written before it runs.** Products a03, a04, a06, a10 and a12 only, once each, with `examples/adk-agent/run_eval.py` and the changed agent on Gemini 3.8 Flash through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini, against a local server built from this branch (not undelabs.dev, which does not have these changes). The server's committed providers are Vertex and fake (D49), so the local server runs with a provider patch that is not committed, and with the engine, router and verifier on Gemini 3.8 Flash through the same gateway to keep the cost down (production's engine and verifier are Gemini 4 Argon). Its plan searches can therefore differ from undelabs.dev's. This checks whether each issue is gone on development products already seen; it is not a new score, is not pooled with D451 and gives no pass rate. Rows go to `eval/agent/results/fixcheck-d470-local.jsonl` (the scorer lists them as their own run). Per issue: a04, a10 fixed when the agent drafts once, with the `plan_id` (or the `plan_index`) of the plan its answer reports; a03 fixed when, if the search shows no plan, the answer claims no working move (read by hand) and the draft is for the current setup (the D450 arguments rule still counts that draft as a miss: reported, not rescored); if the search does show a plan, a03's issue is not tested and is reported so; a06 fixed when `predict_origin` is called once and is not refused; a12 fixed when any far-chapter code the tool returns carries a check note (D471) and the answer does not present it as likely (by hand); with no far-chapter code, not tested. Budget: at most $0.50 for the run, agent and server model calls together, within this item's $1 cap.

## D471 — Per-part HTS codes: a plausibility check that flags, never removes (22 Nov)
- **Why:** D451's a12: `suggest_part_hts` (its model unavailable, so codes from the part index only) gave heading 1704 (sugar confectionery) for a CV axle's "centre bar" and 6401 (rubber footwear) for its "CV boots", and the agent restated them.
- **Check** (`backend/internal/hts/plausible.go`, deterministic, no model): a part candidate gets a `check` note ending "check this code" when (a) its chapter is one no part of a planner family is expected in (food and farm goods 01–24, ores 26, fertilisers 31, explosives 36, furskins 43, clothing 61–62, footwear 64, headgear 65, umbrellas 66, feathers and wigs 67, precious stones, jewellery and articles of precious metal in 71 except headings 7106–7112, musical instruments 92, arms 93, art 97), and the product has one of the 14 families (furniture may use 05, 14 and 67; medical devices 61, 62 and 65), or, with no family, the product's chapter (its `hts`, else the good's top suggestion) is 72–96; or (b) the part's name states a material (plastic, rubber, steel or iron, aluminium, copper, glass, wood, paper, metal; a coating such as "rubber-coated" does not count) and the code is in another material's chapter. A flagged code stays in its place; nothing is removed or reordered. `POST /v1/products/parts-hts-suggest` adds `check` per candidate and `flagged` (a count); the MCP tool shows the note beside the code and says how many to check; the parts table shows a "Check this code" chip with the note, and "Accept all top suggestions" passes over a flagged code for the part's next one (a part whose every code is flagged is left for the user).
- **Measured offline** on the committed suggestion rows of D381/D382 (`eval/tariffshift/parts/`), gold by D381's rule, recomputed by `go test ./internal/hts` into `eval/parts-check/summary.json`. Family-fixture rows take the fixture's family; Part 102 rows have none and use the good's top suggestion as the product's chapter.
- **Development.** The check was written and changed on the dev rows only (`suggest-dev-v1.jsonl`). Its first version flagged 7 of 1,060 dev candidates, none on a part with gold; read by hand, all 7 were plausible codes (silver paste and silver solder in 7106, a metal frame with plastic parts and a rubber-coated handle in 7326, glass-epoxy and paper-phenolic sheets in 3921). The changes: headings 7106–7112 kept, coatings ignored, resin words (epoxy, phenolic, polyester, vinyl) read as plastic, "metal" a material. The version committed here flags 0 of the 1,060 dev candidates. The 15 dev candidates that are wrong against gold are all in nearby chapters (for example 3506 for an adhesive CBP put in 4811, 8536.50 for a pressure switch in 8421.29), which this check does not aim at.
- **Held out, written before it is read.** The check is frozen at the commit that adds this entry. Then `suggest-final.jsonl` with `gold-final.jsonl` (the Part 102 `final` split, D382) is measured once with it and reported whatever it shows, in D472.

## D490 — A revoking ruling is not alerted on the ruling it revokes; recount of D481 (22 Nov, judge panel round 10, N4)
- **Problem:** H325607 revoked N331974 on its own date and cites it. Scored against H325607, an answer citing N331974 got the "look again" alert, naming H325607 as the change. The case was the change. 2 of D481's 4 "look again" rows were this.
- **Decision (built):** `domain.RulingAlerts` leaves out a final change when the ruling that made it is the case itself (a new role, `self`, given by the offline count for a result row's own `ruling`) or is a ruling the case relies on (cited, a plan's support, the current setup's holding): an answer that names the revoker already knows of the change. A revoker the case only read does not count. Proposals are unchanged. Saved cases have no `self` ruling, so for them only the second rule applies. Test: `TestRulingAlertsSkipTheCaseOwnRevocation`.
- **Recount (`go run ./cmd/corpus alerts`, offline, $0):** of 13,107 result rows naming rulings, 2 rows (was 4) would show "look again": N356467 citing N344694, modified by H344999 on 2026-05-06, in 2 development runs. 7 rows (was 8) rely on a ruling changed before their case date: one textile development row for N356391 cites both N345891 and H346161, the letter that revoked it. 64 rows (was 85) only read a changed ruling: 18 are H325607's own rows reading N331974, 3 cite the revoker. Stored case documents (0 of 7) and demo fixtures (0 of 10) are unchanged.
- **Also (judge panel round 10, N1-N3, N7):** the README gets a "Checks beside the model" section (the rule check, per-part codes, per-move checks, revocation alerts, the ADK evaluation), each with its measured figure and PR, and its ADK paragraph cites the evaluation. /method and MODEL-CARD.md give the rule check's coverage per split (full text: development 8 of 72, held out 4 of 32; facts: 0 of 72 and 1 of 45), not pooled as 12 of 104 and 1 of 117. The agent scorer's a06 label says the first `predict_origin` call was refused and no second case was made; the score is unchanged. The cases list stacks each row below 640 px (the header row hidden, each cell naming its column), so it no longer scrolls sideways at 390 px.

## D500 — Pre-registration: on a Part 102 case, rank shown plans by tier, then the 102.20 rule check, then net (22 Nov, judge panel round 10, item 4)
Committed before the ranking is written and before any Part 102 plan search exists (D442 counted 0 committed). Nothing below changes because of a result.
- **Why:** on a case routed to Part 102 (router regime `usmca`), 19 CFR 102.20 and 102.11 are the marking rules, and precedent decided under substantial transformation is the weaker signal. D441 shows the rule check on each move but leaves the order to the precedent check and net, so a move the rule says does not change origin can rank first.
- **Rule, Part 102-routed cases only.** Shown plans (precedent-supported, check at least 0.92, unchanged) sort by: (1) tier (D341: clear margin, then at the bar); (2) within a tier, the move's rule check: first `shifts` (precedent and the rule both support the move), then `undetermined` (precedent only: the codes or a fact leave the rule open), then `no_shift` or `other_country` (precedent supports, the rule gives another country; the amber flag of D441 stays on the move); (3) within that, the planner's order as today (net a year, or in operations mode priced first, then modelled net). A shown plan with no rule check counts as `undetermined`. Nothing is hidden or moved between shown and rejected; rejected moves keep their order; the verdict and tier do not change. The smallest supported move (D340) is worked out again on the new order. The search's `ranking.rule` reads `tier_then_rule_then_net`.
- **Country comparison:** on a Part 102 case, each country's best plan is the first shown plan in this order, and countries with a shown plan rank by the best plan's tier, then its rule class, then as today.
- **Substantial-transformation cases:** order unchanged. The check stays informational and display only there (D441).
- **Where it applies:** where D441 adds the check, when a search is returned or read, from the case's current product: never stored, so codes accepted after the search re-rank it on the next read, and `RULE_CHECK=off` gives the stored order. `plan_index` counts the order a read shows; `plan_id` is unaffected.
- **Tests:** a Part 102 search with one shown plan per class in each tier ranks shifts, undetermined, flagged within each tier; the same plans on a substantial-transformation case keep their order; the stored search is not written; `plan_index` 0 in the draft is the first plan a read shows; the comparison's best plan and country order follow the rule.
- **Expected effect on committed data:** none. There is no committed Part 102 plan search (D442); D501's are the first.

None of them is a move the planner can make from N350133 (none moves a group to another country), so there is no plan backtest. What can be checked: the rule on N354024's setup, with CBP's good code and the top D381 suggestion for each part. The D382 row already computed it (decided, Mexico, agrees); it is reported again here, not new evidence.
