Components: the D362 full-text materials of the ruling (names and countries as extracted), each part's code the top D381 dev suggestion, the good's code CBP's (D362). Plants, groups and operations: assigned by hand from the facts to the template groups, with every assignment in the script. Target by the D171 rule: CBP held China, so the country where the good is finished (actuator: Canada); otherwise the other country with the most work (lawn mower, compressors: China, a reverse probe). The target plant gets every movable group present (the D171 assumption). Economics illustrative, as D171. `exclude_rulings`: the ruling itself and, for the lawn mower, its later rulings.
- **Run.** `go run ./cmd/eval plan` once per fixture, production configuration as D171 (verifier-v2, gemini-4-argon, bar 0.92, one vote, local corpus search), through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini with `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`. Cap $3 in all (no suggestion calls are needed; the codes come from committed rows). A failed or timed-out search is reported as failed and not re-run more than once.
- **Scored, offline (`go run ./cmd/tariffshift plans102-eval`, in `make reproduce`).** Per search: the rule check on the current setup (decided, and whether it gives CBP's holding); every move's status (shifts, no_shift, other_country, undetermined and why); whether the search found a move the rule says shifts, and whether that move is shown (precedent-supported at the bar); moves where precedent supports and the rule gives another country (the D500 demotion); the order before and after D500; agreement of the engine's predicted origin with the rule on decided moves; gateway-reported cost and wall time.
- **Expectations stated now.** Actuator: moving the motor group to Canada makes every foreign part shift into 8501, so the rule says shifts for any move that includes it; whether the precedent check supports it is open. Lawn mower and compressors: final assembly stays in Mexico (it is not a movable group), so the rule gives Mexico for every move to China (`other_country`): no move shifts, and any shown plan carries the flag and ranks last in its tier under D500.
- **Reading.** Three searches, one run each, on products chosen to exercise the rule, not a sample. Suggested codes are unverified (D382). The precedent check reads substantial-transformation rulings, so on these cases the rule, not precedent, is the marking test; agreement between them is not accuracy.

## D502 — Part 102-aware plans finished: the check in the draft and the comparison, the D500 order, and the three D501 searches (22 Nov, judge panel round 10, item 4)
- **Built (D500, as pre-registered).** `planrule.Rank` puts a Part 102 case's shown plans in the D500 order (tier, then `shifts`, undetermined, another country, then the planner's order) when `planrule.Annotate` adds the checks, so every read and every response (plan, stream `done`, case read, country comparison) shows it; `ranking.rule` reads `tier_then_rule_then_net`. A substantial-transformation case keeps its order. The draft resolves `plan_index` against the order a read shows. Tests: `TestRankPart102TierThenRuleThenOrder`, `TestRankLeavesAnUnrankedSearch`, `TestAnnotateRanksOnlyPart102`, `TestPart102ReadRanksByTheRuleAndDraftsItsOrder`, `TestInformationalReadKeepsTheOrder`, `TestRankTargetsPart102RuleClass`.
- **Broker draft.** Both formats state the check of the setup the draft asks about in one paragraph, "Tariff-shift check (19 C.F.R. § 102.20)": what the rule gives on the component codes and on what basis, the parts that do not make the change, or why it could not be applied; "for reference only" on a substantial-transformation case; ended by "[CONFIRM WITH COUNSEL]" (Markdown) or a [FILL IN] (the 177.2 letter). When precedent and the rule disagree, the letter says the result differs from the cited ruling and the reviewer notes beside it carry the flag. The current-setup draft carries the current setup's check. `export.TariffShiftLine`; goldens `usmca_rule_shifts`, `usmca_rule_review`, `plan_rule_undetermined`.
- **Country comparison.** Each country's best plan carries its check (chip and flag in the table, a caption and a line under "How the ranking works"); on a Part 102 case the best plan is the first in the D500 order and countries rank by tier, then its rule class. MCP `plan_production_moves` and `compare_target_countries` say which applies.
- **The three D501 searches, run as pre-registered** (fixtures commit 1496f7fe, kept as branch `improve/p10-part102-fixtures`; the merged history has new hashes; `eval/tariffshift/plans102/runs/plan-p102-*-d501-litellm.json`; scored by `go run ./cmd/tariffshift plans102-eval`, in `make reproduce`; rows `eval/tariffshift/plans102/`). Development rulings, one run each, $0.4333 gateway-reported in all, no failures.

  | Ruling (target) | Moves | Shown | Rule: shifts / another country / undetermined | Precedent supports, rule gives another country | Current setup: rule (CBP) | Cost, wall |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | N348465 actuator (Canada) | 12 | 1 | 6 / 0 / 6 | 0 | undetermined: the DC motor does not shift unless de minimis (China) | $0.3542, 79 s |
  | N344002 compressors (China) | 1 | 0 | 0 / 1 / 0 | 1 (below the bar, 0.85) | Mexico (Mexico) | $0.0433, 28 s |
  | N350133 lawn mower (China) | 1 | 0 | 0 / 1 / 0 | 1 (below the bar, 0.75) | Mexico (Mexico) | $0.0358, 26 s |

- **Actuator.** The rule says every move that includes the motor group shifts to Canada (6), and every move without it does not, because the Chinese motor stays in the good's own heading 8501 (undetermined only because the fixture gives no value for the de minimis test). That is CBP's own reason for holding China. The search found the motor moves; precedent supports all 6, but only one (motor, gearbox and controls, 0.94, N346961) clears the bar, and it is the shown plan. Moving the motor alone, the smallest move the rule supports, was checked at 0.82 with a counter-ruling. One move without the motor (gearbox and controls, 0.85) had precedent support below the bar while the rule says the motor fails; the general engine predicted Canada for it and for two other moves without the motor. The engine agrees with the rule on all 6 decided moves.
- **Compressors and lawn mower (reverse probes).** As expected, final assembly stays in Mexico, so the rule gives Mexico for the only move each search had (the stator and rotor; the deck and wheel work). Both moves had precedent support below the bar and the engine predicted China for both, so both are flagged "precedent supports, rule gives another country". Neither is shown, so the D500 demotion had nothing to act on.
- **D500 order on these searches:** no change. No search showed more than one plan.
- **Later ruling.** The rule on N354024's setup (CBP's good code, top suggestions) gives Mexico, as CBP held. This checks the rule on a later product, not a plan move; there is still no plan backtest.
- **Reading.** On the one search where a move can change the answer, the rule and precedent point to the same move, and the rule also names the cheaper move precedent did not clear (the motor alone). On the two reverse probes, precedent below the bar and the general engine both lean to China while the marking rule gives Mexico; if a later check put either move above the bar, D500 would now rank it last and flag it. Three searches on products chosen to exercise the rule, one run each, unverified suggested codes, illustrative plant capabilities: this shows the mechanism on real rulings, not an accuracy figure.

## D510 — ADK agent evaluation v2: two live runs per product, D450's checks plus the D470 changes, written before the runs (22 Nov, judge panel round 10, item 5)
- **Why:** D451 ran each product once, so it says nothing about how often a run repeats, and the D470 changes (plan_id, the no-plan line, the current-setup draft) were checked only on five products against a local server (D472). This runs the agent twice per product against the live server, with the checks fixed here first.
- **Set:** the same 12 products as D451, a01–a12 of `eval/agent/products.jsonl`, all from the development split (the scorer still fails on a held-out ruling). a13 and a14 are not run.
- **Agent and server:** `examples/adk-agent` as on this commit (the D470 instruction), not changed between or during runs. Gemini 3.8 Flash through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini, as in D451. `https://undelabs.dev/mcp`, anonymously; its tool list was read before this entry and carries `plan_id` (D470 is live). `examples/adk-agent/run_eval.py` now also keeps each shown plan's `plan_id`, so the scorer can check the one the export names; nothing else in the harness changed.
- **Runs:** two per product. Run 1 is a01–a12, three at a time; then run 2, the same. Each run is a new ADK session and makes a new anonymous case, so the plan idempotency key the instruction asks for (`<case_id>-plan-<target>`) is new in every run. Each run may run one plan search. Rows go to `eval/agent/results/live-v2-run1.jsonl` and `live-v2-run2.jsonl`; their meta files name the series (`v2`), the run number and the baseline (`live-gemini-3.8-flash-undelabs`). Every row is kept and scored, failures included; no product is re-run.
- **Plan timeouts are expected:** the hosted front end cuts a request at 300 s (#587). A plan call cut there and called again with the same input and key joins the running search (#580, D422); D450 rule 1 already allows that repeat, and it is not counted as a failure.
- **Checks (D510 rules), in `eval/agent/score.py`:** D450 rules 1–5 unchanged, except:
  1. Tool order adds: `export_ruling_request_draft` is called again after a draft that worked fails the run (the instruction asks for one draft, D470).
  2. Arguments, the export's plan selector, replacing D450's "a `move_key` or `plan_index`": when the plan search showed a plan, the export must name one by `plan_id`, `plan_index` or `move_key`; a `plan_id` must be one the search returned, and a `plan_index` must be in range. When the search showed no plan, the export must name none: the current-setup draft is the right call, and naming a plan fails.
  3. New rule 7, no-plan honesty: when a plan search answered and showed no plan, no sentence of the final answer outside code blocks may claim that a move to the target country changes the origin. The scorer flags a sentence that names the target country with "make", "establish", "become", "confer", "shift", "change" or "render" followed by "origin", or "would/will/could be (the) origin", or "origin would become/change to" the target, and that has no negation ("no", "not", "cannot", "none", "stands" and the like). On the committed rows it flags D451's a03 and not D472's a03 or a06. I will also read every no-plan answer by hand and report any disagreement; the scorer's verdict is the score.
  A run passes when it finishes and meets D450 rules 1–5 as changed here and rule 7. D450's own pass is still reported beside it.
- **Reported:** pass rate per run (D510 rules, with D450's beside it) and over both runs; repeatability per product: same pass or fail in both runs, same predicted origin, plan found in both or neither, same number of plans shown, same plan drafted (`plan_id`), same order of the four required tools, same full tool sequence; v1 against v2: D451's run as published (D450 rules), D451's run rescored under D510 rules, and each v2 run. Rescored under D510, D451's run passes 8 of 12 (a04 and a10 drafted twice; a03 claimed a move after no plan; a06 as before); this figure is computed before the v2 runs, from committed rows.
- **Not an accuracy figure,** as D450: each product's own ruling is in the precedent pool.
- **Budget:** agent model cost about $0.04 a run (D451: $0.0394), so about $0.95 for 24 runs. If run 1 costs over $1.00, run 2 is not started and that is reported. This item's cap is $2 of gateway spend, including any `adk eval` run.
- **ADK's own format:** an `.evalset.json` for the same 12 cases with the expected tool trajectory, and its config, are added after this entry. They are not a source for the D510 score; if `adk eval` is run, its result is reported apart, in D511.

## D511 — ADK agent evaluation v2: results so far; run 2 blocked by the live server's per-client budget (22 Nov, judge panel round 10, item 5)
- **Run 1, as D510 says:** a01–a12, three at a time, 22 Nov 2026 10:30–10:40 +08:00, after the D510 commit (af36d5f9 after rebasing; pushed as 5bcf1c4a at about 10:30:20 +08:00, authored 10:30:14, before the first run started at 10:30:40). Rows `eval/agent/results/live-v2-run1.jsonl`. Agent model cost $0.4189 gateway-reported over 61 model calls.
- **The budget stop.** From about 10:39:50 +08:00 the live server answered every model-backed call from this address with 429 `client_budget_reached`: the anonymous per-client share of the day's model budget was used up (D451's 12 runs and these ran from the same address today). It reopens at 00:00 UTC. a09's plan search, a10's `suggest_part_hts`, and a11's and a12's `extract_product` were refused; each agent reported the error and stopped, as its instruction says. The rows are kept and scored as the rules say. This is the server's spend control working, not an agent fault, but it is counted.
- **Run 2 was not started.** Every anonymous model call from this address is refused until the budget reopens, so run 2 cannot run today. It stays pre-registered as D510 wrote it and runs unchanged after 00:00 UTC; its rows go to `live-v2-run2.jsonl` and the committed scorer compares them run against run with no change. Until then there is no repeatability figure: one run per product says nothing about how often a run repeats. Using another address or an API key to get past the limit would change the pre-registered setup, so it was not done.
- **Scores, run 1 (D510 rules):** 9/12 passed every check. All 8 runs the budget did not touch (a01–a08) passed. Of the 4 it cut, a09 passes (the plan search was refused, the agent said so and stopped; the rules ask for nothing more), and a10, a11 and a12 fail on missing tools. Under D450's rules as published, run 1 passes 8/12: a03's current-setup draft is still a D450 miss.
- **v1 against v2 (D510 rules):** D451's run rescores to 8/12 (a03 claimed a move after no plan, a04 and a10 drafted twice, a06's refused `predict_origin` call); this figure was in D510 before the run. On a01–a08, the products both runs tested in full, D451 passes 5/8 and v2 run 1 passes 8/8. The three D451 issues D470 targeted did not recur on a01–a08: a03 found no plan to Vietnam again, said the origin stands and drafted the current setup; a04 and every other run that saw a plan drafted once, by a `plan_id` the search returned; a06 called `predict_origin` once. Plans were found in 7 of the 8 (1 to 4 shown); no plan call reached the front end's 300 s cut this time, and the median wall time on a01–a08 was 210 s (D451: 313 s over 12).
- **Hand reading.** Rule 7 applied once (a03, no plan); the scorer and the hand reading agree that the answer claims no move. a06's answer writes rulings as CBP does, "NY N350622" and "NY N340438"; the scorer read the second as NN340438 and counted it as invented. That is a parsing bug: N340438 is in the tool results. The scorer now reads "NY N" and "HQ H" as the ruling number (`norm_one`); this changes only a06 in run 1 (pass under both rule sets after the fix, fail before), and no committed earlier row. One more miss reported, not in the pass: the target plant was added in 3 of 4 runs whose description names none; the fourth is a12, whose extraction was refused, so nothing was added.
- **ADK's own format.** `eval/agent/adk/unde_agent.evalset.json` (the 12 live cases, expected tool trajectory `extract_product` → `predict_origin` → `plan_production_moves` → `export_ruling_request_draft`) and `test_config.json` (`tool_trajectory_avg_score` 1.0, `IN_ORDER`, arguments ignored because case ids and keys change every run, two runs per case), written by `eval/agent/score.py` and checked in `make reproduce`. Validated against google-adk 2.14.1's `EvalSet` and `EvalConfig` models, and loaded by `adk eval` itself with no model key and no server (the case reached the model call and stopped there, $0). Not run live: the same budget stop. `eval/agent/adk/replay_trajectory.py` scores the recorded rows with ADK's `TrajectoryEvaluator` and that config, offline: D451 12/12, v2 run 1 8/12 (`eval/agent/adk/replay.json`). That metric checks tool order only, so it is looser than D510's checks.
- **Spend:** $0.4189 for this item so far, within its $2 cap.

## D520 — Broker draft wording: no doubled ruling subjects, and the Part 102 question on every Part 102 case (22 Nov, review follow-up of #613)
- **Problem 1, doubled names.** The Part 102 plan fixtures (D501) take their product names from CBP ruling subjects, so the draft read "the country of origin of The country of origin of an electrical actuator". `export.DraftName` now removes a leading "the country of origin of" or "country of origin of" (any case) and keeps the article after it ("an electrical actuator"). A subject that asks more than origin ("The country of origin and eligibility of the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) of a Walk-Behind Lawn Mower") is cut after its last " of a " or " of an ". Any other name is kept as given. Both letters use it in the opening, the RE line, the transaction and the question; the 177.2 "Name and model" line drops the leading "a" or "an" of a subject-derived name and capitalises it ("Electrical actuator"). The other places that show a product name (MCP export text, the broker review page heading, the case list) print the name without a "country of origin of" template, so nothing there doubles; they are unchanged. Tests: `TestDraftName` (the three committed fixture names and normal names that must not change), `TestNoDoubledSubjectInDrafts`.
- **Problem 2, the wrong question.** A plan search always uses the general engine, so a plan draft on a case routed to Part 102 asked the substantial-transformation question and added only the 102.20 paragraph. Now `export.Input.Part102` (set when the router's regime is Part 102 and the prediction is the general engine's) gives the Part 102 letter: the question asks for the country of origin for marking under the Part 102 rules, the 102.20 paragraph is not "for reference only", and Section 301 is kept apart as before. The note beside the letter says the position comes from the general engine and is not a Part 102 determination. The Part 102 engine's own drafts, textile, pharmaceutical and substantial-transformation drafts keep their question. A Part 102 case whose prediction has no recorded engine keeps the general draft and its "not recorded" note. Tests: `TestPart102RoutedGeneralAsksThePart102Question`, `TestPart102FlagOnlyForGeneralPredictions`, the updated `TestExportRegimeMatrixThroughHandler` and `TestExportPlanDraftInSpecialistCase`; golden `part102_routed_plan`.
- **Part 102 wording, from the regulation text (eCFR, 19 CFR Part 102 as of 1 Nov 2026).** § 102.11 is a hierarchy: paragraph (a), whose (a)(3) is the tariff shift of § 102.20, then (b), (c) and (d), each only where the ones before cannot decide. § 102.0 makes §§ 102.1 to 102.18 and 102.20 the rules for marking origin of goods under the USMCA. The rule is now named "the Part 102 rules of origin (the general rules of 19 C.F.R. § 102.11, applied in order, with the tariff shifts of § 102.20)", and the question ends "for purposes of country of origin marking (19 C.F.R. § 102.0)". This changes the six existing Part 102 goldens in those two sentences only. No new legal claim: the letter still asks CBP and states the rule check's result neutrally.

## D540 — Pre-registration: plan searches on Part 102 cases predict each move with the Part 102 engine (22 Nov, judge panel round 11, item 5)
Committed before the change is written and before any run. Nothing below changes because of a result.
- **Why:** on a case the router sends to Part 102 (regime `usmca_part102`), the case's own prediction comes from the Part 102 engine (`usmca-v1`, 19 CFR 102.11 with the 102.20 tariff shifts; D61), but a plan search predicts each move with the general engine, which reads earlier rulings under substantial transformation. So the plan's predicted origin, the 102.20 rule check on each move (D441) and the D500 order reason under different tests. On the D501 actuator (N348465) the general engine predicted Canada for 3 moves without the motor, where the rule says the Chinese motor fails the shift into heading 8501 (undetermined only for de minimis); on both reverse probes it predicted China where the rule gives Mexico.
- **Change:** a plan search (and a country comparison) on a case whose router regime is `usmca_part102` predicts the current setup and every move with the Part 102 engine, when it is on (`USMCA_ENGINE=on`, as in production). The engine, its prompt (`usmca-v1`, unchanged) and its precedent pool are the ones the case prediction uses; predictions are cached under their prompt version as now. If the Part 102 engine is off the search uses the general engine as today. A move whose engine call fails is handled as today (D88); there is no per-move fallback to the general engine, so one search never mixes engines. Substantial-transformation, textile and pharmaceutical cases are unchanged (general engine). The precedent check (verifier) is unchanged: it does not need the regime to run, and it still reads the general corpus. A draft of such a plan is then asked under Part 102 with the Part 102 engine's own note (its trace is `usmca-v1`), and the D520 note, now worded for plans stored before this change or a Part 102 engine that is off or failed, stays for those.
- **Check (a re-run on seen development products, not new evidence of accuracy).** The three D501 fixtures (N348465 actuator, N344002 compressors, N350133 lawn mower; development rulings, already run and read in D501/D502), one plan search each, same configuration as D501 (verifier-v2, gemini-4-argon, bar 0.92, one vote, local corpus search, no near-miss advice), with the Part 102 engine (`go run ./cmd/eval plan -regime usmca_part102`, which builds it as the server does, from `eval/data/labels_usmca.jsonl`), through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini with `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`. Tag `d540`. Cap $2 in all (D502 cost $0.4333 for the three). A failed search is reported and re-run at most once.
- **Compared with the committed D502 runs, per search (scored offline by `go run ./cmd/tariffshift plans102-eval`, in `make reproduce`):** (1) agreement of the predicted origin with the rule on decided moves (D502: actuator 6/6, compressors 0/1, lawn mower 0/1; 6/8 in all); (2) agreement on moves the rule leaves undetermined only for de minimis, where it names a part that fails the shift (the rule's lean is "does not shift"; the engine agrees when it does not predict the target) (D502: actuator 3/6); (3) the predicted origin of the current setup against CBP's holding (D502: 3/3); (4) shown plans and their rule status, moves sent to the precedent check, moves flagged "precedent supports, rule gives another country"; (5) gateway-reported cost and wall time.
- **Expectations stated now:** the Part 102 engine predicts China for the actuator moves without the motor and Mexico on both reverse probes, so (1) and (2) rise and fewer moves go to the precedent check; the motor moves stay Canada. Shown plans on the actuator may differ from D502 by the precedent check's run-to-run spread, not only by the engine.
- **Decision rule:** the change ships on the legal ground above (the case's own prediction already uses this engine), not on these three runs. If agreement does not rise, or falls, that is reported as it is in D541 and in the docs, and the change is not presented as an accuracy gain. Three products picked to exercise the rule, one run each: a mechanism check.

## D541 — Part 102 engine in plan searches: built, and the D540 check on the three D501 products (22 Nov, judge panel round 11, item 5)
- **Built (D540, as pre-registered).** `planner.Options.Engines` maps a regime to its engine and `planner.Request.Regime` names the case's; a search uses that engine for the current setup and every move, else the general engine, and never mixes the two. - **Broker draft.** A plan searched this way carries a `usmca-v1` trace, so its draft is asked under the Part 102 rules with the Part 102 engine's own note (as a case prediction from that engine is); the D520 note ("made by Unde's general engine") no longer appears on these plans. Its text now says it applies to a plan searched before this change, or a Part 102 engine that was off or unavailable. The textile and pharmaceutical note now says plan searches use the general engine except on Part 102 cases.

- **Actuator.** As expected, the Part 102 engine predicts Canada for the 6 moves with the motor and China for the 6 without it, so it now agrees with the rule's lean on the 3 moves the general engine sent to Canada; those 3 no longer go to the precedent check. Two plans are shown (motor, gearbox and screw drive with the housing; and with the controls), both at the bar (0.92, the second naming counter-ruling N342620), both moves the rule says shift. This is three seen development products, one run each: it shows the mechanism, not an accuracy gain, and one engine error (compressors) remains. The precedent check still reads substantial-transformation rulings; on these cases the rule, not precedent, is the marking test (D501).
- **Spend:** $0.5140 gateway-reported for this item ($0.1724 invalid attempt, $0.3416 scored), within its $2 cap.

## D531 — A revocation alert says whether the change bears on the answer (22 Nov, judge panel round 11, item 2)
- **Problem.** The alert box said "Re-check recommended" the same way whether CBP's change moved the cited ruling's holding to or from the case's answer, moved it between two other countries, or left the origin alone. On /examples/revocation-alert the cited N344694 moved from China to Taiwan (H344999), and the answer was Vietnam.
- **Built.** `domain.WithRelevance` labels each alert from three facts: the origin the changed ruling held and the origin the changing ruling holds, both from the shipped labels (`backend/data/labels.jsonl`, `labels_usmca.jsonl`; never a held-out file), and the case's predicted origin. Labels: `touches_answer` (the holding moved to or from the answer's country), `not_answer` (it moved between two other countries), `holding_unchanged` (the same origin before and after, by the labels), `unknown` (a holding or the answer is not known; the sentence says which). Each alert carries `held_before`, `held_after`, `answer`, `relevance` and `relevance_note`; the counts add `touches_answer`. It never changes the answer and never hides an alert. A re-check stays recommended in every case: the box and MCP say "Re-check still recommended" for `not_answer` and `holding_unchanged`.
- **Holdings file.** `backend/internal/domain/ruling_holdings.json`, built by `go run ./cmd/corpus holdings` (in `make reproduce`): 37 of the 308 rulings in the map have a label, 30 with one origin. A changing ruling whose label sentence opens by recounting the earlier ruling ("In NY N331974, CBP found ...") is left unknown, since that is not its own holding (H325607). A label with several origins is unknown.
- **Where.** API case read (`ruling_alerts.items[*]`) and cases-list counts, the ruling watch's lines, MCP `get_case` and `list_cases`, the site's box and cases-list badge, and /examples/revocation-alert, which now reads "H344999 modified N344694, and the origin held moved from China to Taiwan. This case's answer was Vietnam, so the change does not touch the answer directly. Re-check still recommended."
- **Recount** (`eval/supersession/alerts.json`, `relevance_final_relied`): of the 9 relied-on final changes in committed rows, 2 `not_answer` (the N356467 rows), 3 `holding_unchanged` (N345891 and H346161, both Taiwan by the labels), 4 `unknown`; none touches the answer.
- **Limits.** Most changed rulings are classification letters with no origin label, so `unknown` is common. "Holding unchanged" rests on the regex labels, which read one holding sentence; a broker should still read the letter. Tests: `TestWithRelevanceComparesHeldOriginsWithTheAnswer`, `TestRelevanceUnknownAndUnchanged`, `TestCaseAlertSaysWhetherTheChangeBearsOnTheAnswer`, `TestRulingAlertLinesSayWhetherTheChangeBearsOnTheAnswer`, frontend `ruling-alerts` and `recorded-examples`.

## D550 — Pre-registration: ground the Part 102 engine in the quoted 102.20 rule text (22 Nov, follow-up to D541)
Committed before any run of the new prompt. Nothing below changes because of a result.
- **Why:** on N344002 (hermetic compressors, D541) the Part 102 engine (`usmca-v1`) predicted China for the stator-and-rotor move by barring the 8414.90 parts from shifting to 8414.30. The 102.20 row for 8414.10 through 8414.80 allows a change "from any other subheading", so the parts shift. The prompt told the engine to "read the 102.20 rule as quoted in the facts or as you know it, including its exceptions", so it answered from memory and added an exception the text does not have.
- **Change (variant V, prompt `usmca-v2`, development until it passes):** the engine finds the tariff codes a case names (the product's own HTS when the case has a structured product, then the dotted codes in the facts and the four-digit headings named as "heading NNNN"), looks each up in the committed 102.20 table (`backend/internal/tariffshift/rules.json`, eCFR as of 18 Nov 2026, the 17 encoded chapters), and quotes the rows verbatim after the facts, with their governing notes, at most 4 rows (`engine.Part102RuleText`). The system prompt is `usmca-v1` with two edits: (a)(3) no longer says "as you know it, including its exceptions", and a paragraph tells the engine to use the quoted row that covers the good's own classification, apply it exactly as written, and add no exception, condition or carve-out the text does not contain; without a quoted row it reads the rule as it knows it. The 102.11 hierarchy is already in the system prompt and is unchanged. No model call is added; the lookup is deterministic and the cache key includes the quoted text. On the 72 development rulings, 29 name a code with a 102.20 row (counted from the facts before any run); the other 43 get no quoted text and see only the prompt edits.
- **Not run: a second variant with the deterministic rule check as a cross-check input.** From the facts the engine reads, the 102.20 check decides 0 of the 72 development rulings (`eval/tariffshift/summary.json`, source facts: the facts rarely give each material's code), so that input would say "undetermined" on every development case and the variant could not be measured; on a decided case it would also invite the engine to copy the check. Only V is run.
- **Runs (development, `splits_usmca.json` `dev`, 72 rulings):** B = `usmca-v1` re-run now, and V = `usmca-v2`, each once, same configuration as the committed Part 102 dev run (gemini-4-argon, BM25 over the labelled Part 102 rulings dated before each case, K = 5, one vote), through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini with `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, tag `d550` (`go run ./cmd/eval run -regime usmca -split dev [-usmca-prompt v2] -tag d550`). B is re-run so both runs share the day, gateway and code; the committed run (54/72, October) is reported beside it. A case that errors is re-run once by the harness's resume; any error left counts as wrong.
- **Pass rule (all three, V against B on the 72):** (1) V's correct count is not lower than B's (exact two-sided McNemar p on the discordant pairs is reported; a lower count fails whatever p is); (2) fewer rule contradictions: on the 10 development rulings where the committed 102.20 check gives an origin (`eval/tariffshift/results-dev-full_text.jsonl`, decided or decided if not de minimis; an encoding check on CBP's own text, never an engine input), V predicts a different origin on fewer rulings than B; (3) V's gateway-reported cost is at most 1.5 × B's. Reported beside it, not part of the rule: accuracy on the 29 rulings with quoted text and on the 43 without, and each changed ruling.
- **Held out, only if V passes:** V is run once, prompt frozen, on window 1 (`splits_usmca.json` `final`, 32) and window 2 (`splits_usmca_final2.json` `final2`, 13, with `-router` as its committed run) with `-confirm-final`, and compared with the committed `usmca-v1` runs (25/32 and 11/13). V becomes the production Part 102 engine (code only, no deploy change) if, pooled over the 45, its correct count is not lower than 36 and its contradictions on the held-out rulings the check decides (4 in window 1, 0 in window 2; `results-final-full_text.jsonl`) are not more than `usmca-v1`'s (0), with at least one of the two strictly better; a full tie does not ship. If V fails on dev, no held-out file is scored and `usmca-v1` stays.
- **Budget:** at most $3 for this item. Estimate from the committed rows' `cost_usd` (which tracks the gateway's charge for gemini-4-argon in earlier runs): $0.72 per dev run of `usmca-v1`, about $0.75 for V (the quoted rows add about 150 input tokens on 29 cases), about $0.45 for the 45 held-out cases: about $1.9 in all.
- **If V ships:** a plan search on a Part 102 case also passes each move's product to the engine, so its HTS selects the quoted row (plan facts do not state codes), and the D541 compressors search is re-run once as a mechanism check (about $0.05). Results in D551, EVALUATION, NUMBERS, MODEL-CARD and RESULTS, including a negative result.

## D551 — Quoting the 102.20 rule text to the Part 102 engine: did not pass on development, not adopted (22 Nov)
- **Run as pre-registered in D550** (committed and pushed as e5dfbd69 at 12:09 +08:00, before the first run at 12:10, and the `git_revision` of both runs in RUNLOG; 56a031c0 after the rebase onto main). B (`usmca-v1`) and V (`usmca-v2`) once each on the 72 development Part 102 rulings, tag `d550`. One B case failed on a gateway outage (model unavailable) and was re-run once by the harness's resume, as D550 allows; no error is left. Rows in `eval/tariffshift/ground102/runs/` (kept out of `eval/results/` so the committed-row counts of the supersession and alert checks stay as published), RUNLOG `usmca-dev-gemini-4-argon-prec-usmca-v{1,2}-litellm-d550`. Scored by `go run ./cmd/tariffshift ground102-eval` (in `make reproduce`): `eval/tariffshift/ground102/summary-d551.json`.

  | Run | Correct of 72 | With a quoted row (29) | Without (43) | Rule contradictions (10 decided) | Gateway cost |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | usmca-v1, committed (October) | 54 | 23 | 31 | 2 (N341152, N352059) | — ($0.7158 promo) |
  | B: usmca-v1, re-run | 53 | 24 | 29 | 2 (N341152, N352059) | $0.6881 |
  | V: usmca-v2, rule text quoted | 50 | 23 | 27 | 2 (N341152, N352059) | $0.7114 |

- **Pass rule: fails on two of three.** (1) Accuracy not lower: no, 50 against 53 (B right and V wrong on 5 rulings, the reverse on 2; exact McNemar p = 0.45, so the drop is within run-to-run noise, but D550 fails any lower count). (2) Fewer contradictions: no, 2 and 2, the same two rulings, where neither ruling names a code that reaches a quoted row covering the good (N341152 names none; N352059 names heading 4810, whose row allows the shift, and both engines still give Germany). (3) Cost: yes, 1.03 × B.
- **What changed on the 8 rulings where B and V differ.** With a quoted row: V lost N337260 (it read the simple-assembly exception of the 8473 row as covering soldered fins and heat pipes; the exception covers only materials of headings 8414, 8501, 8504, 8534, 8541 and 8542) and N339851, and won N340017. Without a quoted row, where only the prompt edits apply: V lost N338249, H335912 and N355835 and won N351636; on N352763 both are wrong (China and Canada; CBP held Mexico). Four of the 8 (N339851, N340017, H335912, N351636) also flip between B and the committed run, which used the same prompt: B and the committed run differ in correctness on 7 rulings in all. Much of the gap is run-to-run spread; the quoted text did not make the engine more faithful to the rule on this set.
- **Held out not scored.** V did not pass, so no held-out file was read: window 1 (32) and window 2 (13) keep their single committed `usmca-v1` scores. `usmca-v1` stays the production Part 102 engine. `usmca-v2` stays in the code for evaluation only (`eval run -regime usmca -usmca-prompt v2`), with `engine.Part102RuleText` and `tariffshift.RowsFor`; the server does not use it. The D541 compressors move is not fixed by this change, and the plan search was not re-run (D550 re-runs it only if V ships).
- **Limits.** The motivating error was on a plan move, whose facts state no code; the development rulings test the case prediction, where only 29 of 72 name a code with a row, and the deterministic check decides 10. One run per variant.
- **Spend:** $1.3995 gateway-reported (B $0.6881 including the re-run case, V $0.7114), within the $3 cap.

## D560 — The rule-check chapters re-picked without held-out data; five D460 chapters kept and the held-out figures given without them (22 Nov, #619, judge panel round 12, item 2)
- **What went wrong.** D460 said the chapters were counted on development and earlier data (labelled Part 102 rulings dated before 2024). `eval/tariffshift/chapter_counts.py` read the whole `usmca` list instead: all 72 development rulings (counted twice, once from the full text and once from the facts) and all 32 held-out `final` rulings, 14 of whose facts name a heading. So the choice of what to encode read held-out facts, which D460 rules out. Found by the team's own audit (#619).
- **The fix.** The script now reads only labelled Part 102 rulings dated before 2024 that are in no development or held-out split (dev, final, final2): 239 rulings, 84 with a code. It stops if one would be read, and lists the rulings it read; `TestChapterPoolReadsNoHeldOut` fails if any is in dev, final or final2 or dated 2024 or later. With the 69 development goods, 153 goods have a code, 75 in the D360 seven. The same threshold (4) picks 39 plastics (9), 44 wood (11), 48 paper (8), 76 aluminium (4) and 83 base metal (5). Nothing held-out was looked at to pick these; the result is what the documented rule gives.
- **Which chapters change.** 15 fats and oils, 21 food preparations, 40 rubber, 71 jewellery and 95 toys, games and sports goods are not picked by the documented rule (with it they count 2, 3, 3, 3 and 2). 40, 71 and 95 reached 4 only through held-out goods; 15 and 21 through the development rulings counted twice.
- **Decision: keep the five chapters encoded, and give the held-out figures without them.** They are the regulation's own text, applied by the same deterministic code; no parameter was tuned, and every ruling they decide agrees with CBP on development and held-out alike. Dropping them would make the product cover fewer goods for no gain in correctness. What the held-out pick biases is coverage on held-out, so those figures are now also computed with the five left out (`go run ./cmd/tariffshift eval -without 15,21,40,71,95 -out ../eval/tariffshift/d560` and the same for `parts-eval`; both in `make reproduce`), and the pages that quote held-out rule-check figures give that figure. Development figures are unchanged: development may drive the choice. `chapter-counts.json` lists the five as `chapters_kept_d460`, apart from `chapters_added`.
- **Held-out effect** (offline, no model calls, $0; computed once, used to choose nothing):

  | Held-out row | 17 chapters (as shipped) | Without 15, 21, 40, 71, 95 |
  |---|---|---|
  | D362 full text, final n = 32 | out of scope 7, decided 4 (4 agree) | out of scope 12, decided 4 (4 agree) |
  | D362 facts, final n = 32 / final2 n = 13 | out of scope 2, decided 1 / 0, 0 | out of scope 3, decided 1 / 0, 0 |
  | D382 CBP's stated codes, n = 29 | out of scope 7, decided 4 (4 agree) | out of scope 11, decided 4 (4 agree) |
  | D382 CBP's good code, top part suggestions | decided 14 (13 agree) | decided 12 (11 agree) |
  | D382 top suggestion for the good and every part | decided 15 (14 agree) | decided 13 (12 agree) |
  | D413 without the inputs that carried a code, n = 24 | 11 (10 agree) | 9 (8 agree) |
  | D430 same answer under every suggested code (CBP's good code / suggested) | 13 of 14 / 13 of 15 | 11 of 12 / 11 of 13 |

  The two held-out decisions that go are N357770 (playing cards, 9504.40, chapter 95) and N361217 (oils, chapter 15); both agreed with CBP. N356876 (chapter 71) and H351116 (chapter 40) move from undetermined to out of scope, and N361490 (chapter 95) too. The one disagreement with CBP (N358639, chapter 87) is unchanged. Of D461's 7 newly decided held-out rulings, 5 come from chapters picked without held-out data.
- **Also changed:** D460's sentence on the pool was wrong and stays as written, with this decision as the correction. EVALUATION §9, §10 and §13, NUMBERS, RESULTS, README, /method and the model card give the held-out figures without the five chapters beside the shipped ones. RUNLOG `tariffshift-chapters-heldout-d560`.

## D561 — Revocation relevance is judged for the role the ruling plays (22 Nov, #626, judge panel round 12, item 3)
- **Problem.** D531 compared every alert with the case's predicted origin. That is right for a cited ruling, but alerts are also raised for a shown plan's supporting ruling and for CBP's ruling on the current setup. A change that moved a plan's supporting ruling away from the plan's target read "does not touch the answer directly" and was left out of `touches_answer`, which is backwards for the alert a compliance lead most needs (#626, found by the team's own audit).
- **Built.** `domain.WithRelevanceBy` takes a basis per role (`store.Case.RelevanceBasis`, from the same fields as `RulingRefs`): a cited ruling, or one only read, against the predicted origin, as before; a plan's supporting ruling against the target of the plan search whose plans it supports (the plan's own predicted origin when a search has no target); the current setup's ruling against the origin given for CBP's holding there (`CurrentOrigin.Country`). Where a ruling plays several roles, each is judged and the most relevant label is kept: bears on it, then not known, then does not touch it, so a role whose country is not known never lets the alert read "does not touch". Each alert adds `relevance_role`, and the sentence names what was compared ("The plan to China rests on it, so the change bears on the plan: the ruling no longer holds China."; "It is CBP's holding on the current setup (China), so the change bears on the current setup."). `answer` stays the predicted origin.
- **Where it follows.** `touches_answer` in the counts, so the cases-list badge (now "bearing on the answer or a plan") and MCP `list_cases` ("bear on the answer, a shown plan or the current setup"); the watch line ("bears on a shown plan", "does not touch the current setup directly"); "Re-check still recommended" in the box and MCP, which follows the label. OpenAPI documents `relevance_role`.
- **Recount.** `go run ./cmd/corpus alerts` now judges committed plan rows' supporting rulings against the search's target. The counts do not change: the one relied-on plan-support change in committed rows (N322364 in the heat-gun plan, modified by H323218) has no labelled held origin, so it stays not known; 2 not touching the answer, 3 holding unchanged, 4 not known, 0 touching. The recorded alert page is a cited ruling and reads as before.
- **Tests.** `TestWithRelevanceByJudgesEachRole` (plan to the old and new holding, plans elsewhere, unknown target, current setup both ways, several roles); `TestAlertRelevanceIsJudgedForTheRoleTheRulingPlays` (the #626 reproduction through the API: plan to China supported by N344694 with the answer Vietnam bears on the plan, counts and watch line follow; current setup China bears on it); frontend `ruling-alerts`.

The ops-legacy golden takes the new scope line in place; no markup changed.

## D570 — Pre-registration: a held-out Part 102 plan set, frozen before any run (22 Nov, judge panel round 12)
Committed with the frozen set before any held-out model call. Nothing below changes because of a result.
- **Why:** the Part 102 plan pipeline (the Part 102 engine on every move, D540/D541; the 102.20 check on each move, D441; the D500 order; the precedent check) has run only on three development rulings picked by hand (D501). This is its first held-out evaluation.
- **The set (`eval/tariffshift/plans102/heldout/frozen.json`, built by `python3 -I eval/planner/part102_heldout.py freeze`, no model calls; its `inputs_sha256` pins every input file and the protocol script; `freeze --check` is in `make reproduce`).** Every ruling of the two held-out Part 102 windows (`splits_usmca.json` `final`, 32; `splits_usmca_final2.json` `final2`, 13; no Part 102 ruling has been labelled after 13 Nov 2026), in date order, kept when: (1) its committed materials extraction (D362 full text; final2 has only the facts extraction) gives CBP's code for the good and the country where the good is produced; (2) at least two materials have a country; (3) the committed held-out D381 suggestion row (`suggest-final.jsonl`, frozen and scored once in D382) covers the same materials, which gives every part's code with no new suggestion run (final2 has no row; none of it passes steps 1 and 2, so the fallback, the codes CBP states, is never used); (4) the D171 target rule, counted mechanically, names a country: CBP held China, the country where the good is produced; otherwise the country other than CBP's holding with the most work (materials made there, plus 1 for final assembly), ties to the country where the good is produced, then alphabetical. Result: **18 rulings, all from window 1**; out: 13 with no good code or no production country (8 of them final2), 13 with fewer than two materials with a country, 1 (H355020) whose only plant country is CBP's holding.
- **Leaked codes (D413).** Two frozen rulings, H351116 and N357063, had a code left in the suggester's input (5 held-out inputs did; the other 3 are not in the set). The good's code here is CBP's, so only part codes could be affected; results are reported with and without H351116 and N357063.
- **Protocol, in order, each step once.** (a) **Family:** the production family check (`familycheck`, `family-check-v1`, gemini-3.8-flash, the server's router model) on each frozen ruling's subject and facts, `go run ./cmd/eval familycov -split final -confirm-final -labels ../eval/data/labels_usmca.jsonl -splits ../eval/tariffshift/plans102/heldout/frozen.json -tag p102-heldout`; a ruling whose answer is "none" or below 0.6 (the BOM import's bar) has no plan template: the pipeline cannot plan it, and that is a reported outcome, not an exclusion. Its `product_name` is the fixture's name. (b) **Groups:** one call per ruling with a template (`part102_heldout.py groups`, gemini-4-argon, the production extractor's model, no response cache): the production extractor's rule ("use one of the operation groups given (the id), or "" if none fits", `internal/extract`) applied to each D362 material by index; a part with no group never moves. Checked once on the three D501 development products before the freeze (`groups-dev.jsonl`, $0.0172): 39 of 55 parts got D501's hand group; the 16 others are mostly hardware the call left ungrouped where the hand put it in a catch-all group. Nothing was changed after that check. (c) **Fixtures** (`part102_heldout.py build`, no model calls, `build --check` in `make reproduce`): the D501 builder with its hand steps replaced by fixed rules: one plant per country (the producing country's plant does final assembly), each material in its country's plant and its group, one operation per group and plant plus final assembly, the target plant given every movable group present (the D171 assumption), illustrative economics as D501, part codes the top D381 held-out suggestion with the next two as alternatives, the good's code CBP's. `backend/testdata/planner_part102_heldout/`. (d) **Plan search:** `go run ./cmd/eval plan -regime usmca_part102 -tag heldout` once per fixture, the D540 configuration (Part 102 engine `usmca-v1` on the current setup and every move, verifier-v2, gemini-4-argon, bar 0.92, one vote, local corpus search, no near-miss advice, at most 12 moves), through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini with `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, with the local corpus linked. A search that errors is re-run once; any failure left is reported as failed.
- **Measured, offline (`go run ./cmd/tariffshift plans102-eval -series heldout`, in `make reproduce`), per ruling:** whether a template was found and the search ran cleanly (no error); moves searched; moves the 102.20 check decides (`shifts`, `no_shift`, `other_country`) and undetermined by reason; agreement of the Part 102 engine's predicted origin with the rule on decided moves (target or not), and on moves the rule leaves undetermined only for de minimis while naming a failing part (D540); shown plans and, for each, whether its move shifts under the rule; moves flagged "precedent supports, rule gives another country"; the order before and after D500; for the current setup, the rule's status and whether it gives CBP's holding, and the engine's origin against CBP's holding; gateway-reported cost and wall time. Pooled: rulings planned end to end of 18; template coverage of 18; engine-rule agreement on decided moves (moves within a search are not independent, so the interval is optimistic); shown plans the rule says shift; current setup: rule decided and agrees, engine agrees. Exact 95% Wilson intervals where n is at least 5.
- **Backtest:** a later CBP ruling is any ruling in the committed label files dated after a frozen ruling whose facts name its number. None exists for the 18 (`later_rulings` in `frozen.json`, empty), so there is no backtest; reported as 0, not estimated.
- **Expectations stated now:** template coverage about half (furniture, vehicle parts, motors and compressors, water filters fit; plastics, waxes, emulsions and luggage likely "none"). Most frozen rulings are held Canada or Mexico, so most searches are reverse probes away from the country of final assembly: the rule should give the held country for most moves (`other_country`), shown plans should be few, and the Part 102 engine should mostly agree with the rule. Many parts carry model-suggested codes, so many moves stay undetermined.
- **Budget:** at most $8 for this item, gateway-reported. Estimate: family check about $0.05, groups about $0.10, plan searches $0.02 to $0.40 each (D541) on at most 18 fixtures, about $4 in all. If the running total passes $7 before every search has run, the rest are not run and are reported as not run.
- **Reading.** Fixtures are built by fixed rules, so plants, groups and operations are cruder than a user's product; part codes are unverified suggestions (D382); the target plant's capabilities are an assumption; one run per ruling. The precedent check reads substantial-transformation rulings; on Part 102 cases the rule, not precedent, is the marking test, so agreement with it is not accuracy. Small n: every result is reported, failures included.

## D571 — Held-out Part 102 plan set: results (22 Nov)
Run as pre-registered in D570 (the frozen set and D570 committed as 574fd5ca and pushed at 13:10 +08:00, before the first held-out call at 13:11; family check, group call and fixtures committed as 4a5d6a9d before the first plan search; both kept as branch `improve/heldout-part102-prereg`; the rebased history has new hashes). Each step ran once; no search failed and none was re-run. Scored by `go run ./cmd/tariffshift plans102-eval -series heldout` (in `make reproduce`): `eval/tariffshift/plans102/summary-heldout.json`, `moves-heldout.jsonl`.
- **Two deviations, in the fixture build, before any plan search.** (1) The family check's rows keep no `product_name`, so each name comes from the ruling's subject by the D381 rule (`productName`); N359690's subject is empty, so its name is "Product of ruling N359690". (2) A product needs a country for every part, and D570 did not say what to do with a material that has none. Such a material is left out, as the production extractor leaves out a part whose country the text does not state. Left out: N357951 1 of 8, N359145 3 of 7, N359690 14 of 19, N362414 10 of 22; the rule's answers there read only the parts with a country. The protocol script changed for both; `frozen.json` keeps its hash at the freeze, and the set did not change.
- **Funnel.** 45 held-out Part 102 rulings, 18 frozen (all window 1). Family check: 6 have a plan template (3 furniture, 3 vehicle parts), 33% (95% CI 16–56%); 12 have none (plastics, waxes, an emulsion, a rubber hose, a water purification plant, fishing tackle, wood flooring, suitcases, a dust mop, a bolt seal, a bicycle bracket kit, an insulating panel). So the pipeline planned 6 of 18 end to end; all 6 searches ran cleanly.

  | Ruling (CBP → target) | Family | Moves | Shown (rule) | Rule on the moves | Engine agrees with the rule | Current setup: rule / engine (CBP) | Parts left out | Cost, wall |
  |---|---|---:|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
  | N357951 wooden furniture (Canada → United States) | furniture | 1 | 0 | 1 another country | 1/1 | Canada / Canada (Canada) | 1 of 8 | $0.0178, 10 s |
  | N358639 pipe assembly (South Korea → Mexico) | vehicle parts | 3 | 1 (shifts) | 3 shift | 2/3 | Mexico / Mexico (South Korea) | 0 of 3 | $0.0955, 35 s |
  | N359145 wooden furniture (Canada → Thailand) | furniture | 1 | 0 | 1 another country | 0/1 | Canada / Canada (Canada) | 3 of 7 | $0.0453, 30 s |
  | N359690 truck air conditioner (Canada → China) | vehicle parts | 0 | 0 | none | – | Canada / Canada (Canada) | 14 of 19 | $0.0092, 9 s |
  | N362414 turbo thruster kit (Canada → China) | vehicle parts | 1 | 0 | 1 another country | 0/1 | Canada / Canada (Canada) | 10 of 22 | $0.0425, 32 s |
  | N364328 safety gate (Mexico → China) | furniture | 0 | 0 | none | – | Mexico / Mexico (Mexico) | 0 of 4 | $0.0092, 7 s |

- **Pooled.** 6 moves in 4 searches; the rule decides all 6 (3 shift, 3 give another country). The Part 102 engine agrees with the rule on 3 of 6 (95% CI 19–81%; moves within a search are not independent). No move is undetermined only for de minimis. 1 shown plan, and the rule says it shifts. 0 moves flagged "precedent supports, rule gives another country". Current setup: the rule decides 6 of 6 and gives CBP's holding on 5 (44–97%); the engine gives CBP's holding on 5 of 6 (44–97%). D500 order: no search showed more than one plan, so nothing to reorder. Backtests: 0 (no later ruling names a frozen one, as D570 stated). None of the 6 planned rulings had a leaked code in the suggester's input (D413), and none of the six goods is in chapters 15, 21, 40, 71 or 95 (D560), so the figures are the same without those chapters. Wall time 7 to 35 s.
- **Where the engine and the rule part.** On two reverse probes (N359145 to Thailand, N362414 to China) the Part 102 engine predicted the target, while final assembly stays in Canada and the rule gives Canada. On N358639 it kept South Korea for moving the brackets alone, which the rule says shifts (the Korean pipes and flange already change heading into 8708.99). None of the three is shown: the precedent check did not support the first two, and the third was not sent to it. On the three development products the engine agreed with the rule on 13 of 14 moves (D541); here 3 of 6.
- **The shown plan.** N358639: moving the steel pipes and the flange to Mexico, checked at 0.96 (N353124), and the rule says it shifts. Moving the pipes, flange and brackets was at 0.90, below the bar.
- **The current setup against CBP.** N358639 is the one miss for both: the rule and the engine give Mexico, where the Korean pipes, flange and brackets are welded, brazed and tested; CBP held South Korea, where the pipes are bent. D382 reported the same rule disagreement on this ruling.
- **Two searches had no move.** N359690 and N364328 are reverse probes to China where every movable group is already in China; only final assembly, which never moves, is elsewhere.
- **Against the D570 expectations.** Template coverage was lower than "about half" (6 of 18). As expected, most searches were reverse probes and most moves give the held country, shown plans were few, and nothing was flagged. Engine agreement with the rule was lower than expected.
- **Reading.** The binding limit is coverage: two thirds of the buildable held-out Part 102 rulings have no plan template, so the pipeline cannot plan them at all. Where it did plan, the one shown plan is a move the rule supports, and the rule never had to demote a shown plan. The Part 102 engine disagreed with the rule on half the decided moves, all of them moves that were not shown. Six searches, one run each, fixtures built by fixed rules with assumed plant capabilities, unverified suggested part codes and some parts left out: this is a small held-out check of the pipeline, not an accuracy figure.
- **Spend:** $0.3016 gateway-reported for the item: development group check $0.0172, family check $0.0404, group call $0.0245, plan searches $0.2195. Within the $8 cap.

## D580 — Six plan templates for Part 102 goods, chosen and written from pre-2024 Part 102 rulings; pre-registration of the held-out family check (22 Nov, follow-up to D571)
Committed and pushed before the held-out family check below. Nothing in the templates changes because of a held-out result.
- **Problem (D571):** of the 18 frozen held-out Part 102 rulings, 6 had a plan template (3 furniture, 3 vehicle parts), so 12 could not be planned. The 14 families were chosen from substantial-transformation rulings (D138, D212); Part 102 marking cases skew to goods they do not cover.
- **Pool (`eval/families/pool102.py`, no model calls):** the D560 rule (#619): labelled Part 102 rulings dated before 2024 and in no Part 102 development or held-out split (`dev`, `final`, `final2`): 239 rulings (`eval/families/part102-pool.json`). The 13 rulings dated 2024 on that are in no split are left out too. Families are chosen and written from this pool only; development rulings measure coverage; held-out rulings are read only in the step pre-registered below.
- **What lacks a template.** The production family check (`family-check-v1`, gemini-3.8-flash, bar 0.6) with the 14 templates on the pool: 83 of 239 covered (34.7%), 2 failed checks (`families-coverage-train-all-litellm-p102pool-f14.jsonl`). gemini-3.8-flash labelled each pool ruling with a product category, D138's list split finer where Part 102 goods cluster, and a regex read the good's code from the full text (`eval/families/label102.py`, `families102-pool-labels.jsonl`). Of the 156 not covered: food and drink preparations 53, metal products 13, plastic articles 11, wood articles 11, chemicals and pharmaceuticals 8, paper 7, machinery parts 7, electrical apparatus 7, vehicle parts 5 (a template exists), then 3 or fewer each.
- **Selection rule (`eval/families/select102.py`, `families102-selection.json`), written after the pool counts were seen and using pool data only:** count the pool rulings with no template by category; leave out categories that already have a template, chemicals and pharmaceuticals and textiles (regimes with their own engines, as D138) and "other"; keep those with at least 7, by count, at most 6, ties to the category with more assembled goods. Picked: food preparations, metal products, wood panels and flooring, plastic articles, electrical control apparatus, machinery parts; paper (7, none assembled) lost the tie. D138 counted assembled goods only; under Part 102 a processed good with inputs of other headings can be planned too, so this rule counts every good. The held-out product types D571 lists (plastics, waxes, wood flooring and others) were published before this rule was written; the rule reads no held-out ruling, but that knowledge existed.
- **Design for Part 102.** Each movable group is the work that makes one input whose tariff heading the 102.20 rule reads (sugar of 1701 and cocoa powder of 1805 for a cocoa blend of 1806; a plywood blank of 4412 for flooring; pre-cut sheet of 3926 for dividers), so moving a group moves where that heading's material comes from, and the rule check (D441) reads the parts' codes. The last group turns the inputs into the good (blending, extrusion, lamination, assembly) and does not move. Templates carry `"regime": "part102"`; the planner does not read it.
- **Writing, the D138 method with a Part 102 prompt (`eval/families/draft102.py`, `verify102.py`, `merge102.py`):** gemini-4-argon drafted each template from up to 45 of its pool rulings (subject, held origin, holding, start of the facts, and the 1,100 characters of CBP's reasoning ending at the holding; `families102-drafts.json`). gemini-3.8-flash checked every citation against the ruling's facts, Part 102 reasoning and holding: 81 of 151 supported. Three movable groups had no supported citation and were merged into another group of their family (cocoa and dairy inputs into sugar; fittings into pipes and hoses; precision grinding into bodies and castings, whose two citations were Section 301 rulings decided by substantial transformation); the receiving groups were checked again under their new wording, 6 of 23 supported (`families102-citation-checks.jsonl`). The agent read the holding of every citation in a movable group against its group and rewrote the notes that misstated it. Group names were shortened to sentence case by hand.
- **Guards.** `TestTemplateCitationsAreRealRulings` now also fails if a cited ruling is revoked or modified in the supersession map (D320, D400), and for a Part 102 family if a cited ruling is not a Part 102 ruling in `labels_usmca.jsonl`, is dated 2024 or later, or is in any substantial-transformation or Part 102 development or held-out split. The new check found three things: N307465 (cited by the draft machinery template) was modified by N308442, and is dropped; N331974, cited by the vehicle-parts template since D138, was revoked by H325607 on 29 Aug 2025, and is dropped from its group, sources and note (the planner does not read citations, so plans do not change and the template version is kept); and the PCBA template cites H333699, a printer ruling labelled substantial transformation that is also in the Part 102 development split. It was chosen from the substantial-transformation pool and stays; the rule that bars Part 102 splits applies to Part 102 families only. `TestTemplateSetIsPinned` pins 20 families, `TestUnionDefaultFlagPinned` gives the six union defaults (D264), and the HTS plausibility check (D471) no longer flags food chapters on a food preparations product.
- **Templates (version 1):** food and beverage preparations (45 pool rulings read; 21 citations of 18 rulings), metal semi-finished and fabricated products (13; 15 of 10), plywood, wood flooring and panels (11; 12 of 9), plastic film, compounds and moulded articles (11; 16 of 10), electrical control panels and busbars (7; 9 of 6), machinery parts and subassemblies (9; 5 of 3). 78 citations of 56 distinct rulings. Fixtures: one per family in `backend/testdata/families/`, written by hand from a cited pool ruling's facts, starting from CBP's setup and holding, target by the D171 rule, plant capabilities at the target assumed, no part codes (`eval/families/buildfx102.py`). The plywood fixture describes the Canadian work as profiling and finishing; the ruling says only that the blanks were made into a panel that is not surface covered.
- **Coverage on development (scope, not accuracy), the production family check:** Part 102 development (72): 20 (27.8%, 95% CI 18.8–39.0) with 14 families, 1 failed check; **49 (68.1%, 56.6–77.7) with 20**, none failed. On the 71 both answered: 20 → 48, 28 gained, 0 lost, 0 moved to another template. New matches: food 11, plastic 8, metal 7, wood 1, machinery 1; vehicle parts gained 1 that had failed before. A read of the 28 new matches found one stretch (a plastic doll matched to plastic articles). General development (469), a regression check: 317 of 465 answered (68.2%) against 265 of 469 with 14; on the 456 both answered 264 → 309 (48 gained, 3 lost to "none" at 0.85, 9 moved to another template, 6 of them to a new family: bearings, an idler and fluid ends to machinery parts, a busbar to electrical apparatus, a brake hose to metal products). Food preparations took 20 general development rulings (frozen seafood, tea, snacks). A plan on those is searched with the general engine and the substantial-transformation precedent check, as for any family.
- **Pre-registered, held-out family check, run once:** `go run ./cmd/eval familycov -split final -confirm-final -labels ../eval/data/labels_usmca.jsonl -splits ../eval/tariffshift/plans102/heldout/frozen.json -tag p102-heldout-f20`, through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini, at the commit that adds this decision. Measured: how many of the 18 frozen rulings now have a plan template (family not "none", confidence at least 0.6; a failed check counts as no template), against D571's 6 of 18, with a Wilson interval; which family each gets; and whether any of D571's 6 changes family. Only this step runs: the D570 group call, fixture build and plan searches are not re-run, and no second plan pass on newly covered rulings is run here, so the held-out plan results stay D571's.
- **Expectation stated now:** about half of D571's 12 get a template (the plastics and the wood flooring likely; the waxes, emulsion, purification plant, fishing tackle, suitcases, dust mop and bolt seal likely not), so about 10 to 12 of 18. The 6 already covered should keep their family.
- **Spend so far** (gateway-reported or token-priced at promo rates): family checks $0.16 (Part 102 dev, 14), $0.53 (pool), $0.19 (Part 102 dev, 20), $1.31 (general dev, 20); pool labels $0.28; drafts $0.22; citation checks $0.25; notes $0.01. $2.94. Sub-cap $6.

## D581 — Held-out family check with the Part 102 templates: results (22 Nov)
Run once as pre-registered in D580 (D580 committed and pushed as 8085a8b4 before the call at 13:55 +08:00; RUNLOG `families-coverage-final-all-litellm-p102-heldout-f20`; the RUNLOG rows of the development runs name the commit before the rebase onto #630, 9c4a3c8f, which became 4975e779). $0.0732.
- **Result.** **8 of the 18 frozen rulings now have a plan template (44.4%, 95% CI 24.6–66.3)**, against D571's 6 (33.3%, 16.3–56.3). One check failed (N364328, the safety gate that matched furniture in D571: no JSON in the reply after one retry) and counts as no template, as pre-registered; on the 17 both runs answered, 5 → 8.

## D590 — Pre-registration: two fixes for the Part 102 engine's disagreements with the 102.20 rule, from a development error analysis (22 Nov, follow-up to D571)
Committed after the development error analysis below and before any run of either variant. Nothing below changes because of a variant's result.
- **Why:** on the held-out Part 102 plan moves the Part 102 engine (`usmca-v1`) agreed with the 19 CFR 102.20 check on 3 of 6 decided moves (D571; on development, 13 of 14 in D541). D551 showed that quoting the rule text did not help. The held-out runs' details were not read to design this; only that published count was.
- **Error analysis, development only (no held-out file read).**
  - *Single setups, no model calls* (`go run ./cmd/tariffshift p102err-single`, in `make reproduce`; `eval/tariffshift/p102err/summary-single.json`): the 102.20 check on the 72 development Part 102 rulings with three committed inputs (CBP's codes from the full text, D362; CBP's good code with the top D381 suggestion for every part; the top suggestions for the good and parts, D382), first deciding input as the reference, else a de minimis lean. It decides 20 and leans on 8 (the reference gives CBP's holding on 26 of the 28). Against the committed development rows of the engine: October `usmca-v1` 14 of 20 decided and 6 of 8 leans, D550 B 15 of 20 and 6 of 8, D550 V (`usmca-v2`) 14 of 20 and 7 of 8. Eight rulings disagree in at least one run.
  - *Plan setups, one run* (`go run ./cmd/eval p102moves`, tag `d590-b`, $0.8661 gateway-reported): the production Part 102 engine alone (no precedent check) on the current setup and on every move that the check decides or leans on, with the facts a plan search renders, over three development fixture sets: the three D501 products, 13 new development fixtures built by the fixed D570 rules (`eval/planner/part102_dev.py`: 46 development rulings pass the D570 steps once the D501 three are left out; the production family check finds a template for 13, $0.0908; the D570 group call on those, $0.0457; fixtures in `backend/testdata/planner_part102_dev`), and the 23 D171 family fixtures with the top D381 codes as D442. Scored by `go run ./cmd/tariffshift p102err-moves` (in `make reproduce`; `summary-moves.json`). B agrees with the check on 43 of 57 decided rows (36 of 42 moves, 7 of 15 current setups) and on 17 of 23 leans; on the 16 current setups of the Part 102 fixtures it names CBP's holding on 8.
  - *Categories* (hand-assigned before any variant ran, `categories-dev.json`): of the 20 plan rows where B disagrees, 15 are **classification** (the engine's own reading of the good's or a material's tariff code differs from the codes the check reads; the facts a plan search renders state no code at all), 3 **assembly** (the engine says assembling or simple assembly makes a material fail, citing 102.17, which lists only end-use change, disassembly, packing, dilution and collecting GRI 2(a) parts; the rows involved do not name simple assembly), 1 **invented exception** (the engine reads the 8504.10-8504.50 row as barring 8504.90 parts), 1 **rule input** (a suggested code is the likely error). 12 of the 20 also cite simple assembly or 102.17 as a reason. Of the 8 single-setup rulings: 4 classification, 1 assembly, 1 invented exception, 2 rule input. De minimis was not a separate cause: of the 6 lean rows the engine misses, 5 are classification rows and 1 a rule-input row. The essential-character step (b) is reached in most disagreements only after one of these.
- **Variants (at most two, each one run on the same rows as B, tag `d590-va` / `d590-vb`):**
  - **Va, codes in the plan facts:** the facts a plan search renders get one more paragraph that states the codes the product gives, the finished good's and each part's that has one, labelled as the product's own and not verified by CBP (`planner.ClassificationNote`; `eval p102moves -codes-in-facts`). Prompt `usmca-v1` unchanged. This targets the classification category: the check reads these codes, the engine has never been shown them. It changes nothing for a case with no codes and nothing for single-setup cases.
  - **Vb, a structured 102.11 checklist with the codes:** Va's facts and prompt `usmca-v3` (`engine.USMCASystem3`, `engine.ChecklistSchema`): before the origin the model fills the good's classification (as given, else its reading), the rule for it, every material's origin, whether foreign, classification and whether it shifts, the de minimis question and the rule that decides; four instructions from the categories: use the codes the facts give; a material fails only when its own classification is one the row's words exclude; assembling, joining or fastening is not a reason a material fails, and simple assembly matters only where the row names it; go to (b) only when a foreign material fails; an unstated value is answered as if de minimis does not apply.
  - **Not run as a variant: a deterministic post-check.** It cannot change the engine's agreement with the rule (it does not change the answer), so it is pre-registered below as a product safety change with its own rule, not as an accuracy fix.
- **Pass rule (each variant against B, all four):** (1) agreement with the check on the 57 decided rows rises by at least 6 rows net (rows won minus rows lost) with an exact two-sided McNemar p of at most 0.05 on the discordant rows; (2) agreement on the 23 leans is not lower than B's 17; (3) no loss against CBP: on the 16 current setups of the Part 102 fixtures the variant names CBP's holding at least as often as B (8); for Vb, which changes the prompt, also on the 72 development Part 102 rulings (`eval run -regime usmca -split dev -usmca-prompt v3 -tag d590`, run only if (1), (2) and the 16-setup check pass), its correct count is not lower than D550 B's (53, the same prompt and gateway this morning, reused instead of a fourth run; McNemar reported); (4) gateway-reported cost on the same calls at most 1.5 × B's (for Vb's 72-ruling run, at most 1.5 × D550 B's $0.6881). A failed engine call counts as a disagreement and as wrong. If both pass, the one with more decided agreement is adopted; a tie goes to Va (no prompt change).
- **Held out, only for a variant that passes, each scored once, frozen:** (a) the held-out plan fixtures of D570 (`testdata/planner_part102_heldout`), with `eval p102moves` on the current setups and the moves the check decides or leans on, against the published D571 aggregate (3 of 6 decided moves agree; that figure came from the plan-search runs on another run of the same engine, so the comparison is across runs and disclosed as such). (b) For Vb only, the single-setup held-out windows (`eval run -regime usmca -usmca-prompt v3 -confirm-final`, window 1 `final` 32, window 2 `final2` 13 with `-router` as its committed run), against the committed `usmca-v1` runs (25 of 32, 11 of 13), which were scored before; this is a candidate comparison and disclosed. Va changes no single-setup input, so (b) does not apply to it. **Adopted** (the Part 102 engine in plan searches, code only, no deploy change) only if it wins: on (a) more decided held-out moves agree than 3 of 6, and its held-out current setups name CBP's holding at least as often as the published D571 pooled figure; for Vb also on (b) a pooled correct count of at least 36 of 45. Otherwise `usmca-v1` with plain facts stays, and the result is reported as negative.
- **Safety change S, pre-registered separately (no accuracy claim):** on a Part 102 case, the plan's 102.20 check also flags for a broker's look (`review`, with a note; the answer, the ranking and what is shown are unchanged) (i) the current setup when the check decides a country other than the engine's, and (ii) a move the check says shifts to the target while the engine predicts another country, which the search therefore never sent to the precedent check. Moves where the engine predicts the target and the check does not already carry the D441 precedent note when shown. S ships if, on the development rows of the engine that is adopted (B unless a variant is), it flags at most one in three of the decided rows, so that it stays a signal; it is disclosed as not changing accuracy.
- **Budget:** at most $5 for this item, gateway-reported, including the error analysis. Estimate: done so far $1.0; Va about $0.9, Vb about $1.1 on the moves and $0.8 on the 72 rulings; held out about $0.1 per variant on the plan fixtures and $0.5 for Vb's windows. If the running total would pass $5, the remaining runs are not made and are reported as not run.
- **Reading.** Agreement with the rule is not accuracy: the rule reads unverified suggested part codes (D382), and on 2 of the 28 single-setup rows the rule's input is the likely error. The plan rows are not independent (moves within a fixture share facts). One run per variant.
