## D600 — Pre-registration: a compact 102.11 checklist for the Part 102 engine, at no more than 1.5 × the cost (22 Nov, follow-up to D591)
Committed before any run of either variant. Nothing below changes because of a variant's result.
- **Why:** in D591 the checklist variant Vb (`usmca-v3`, the product's codes in the plan facts) raised the Part 102 engine's agreement with the 19 CFR 102.20 check on the 57 decided development rows from 43 to 54 (11 won, none lost, p = 0.001) and named CBP's holding on 9 of the 16 current setups against B's 8, but it cost 1.78 × B because its answers were about three times as long (84,147 output tokens against 28,462). Most of the extra output was the per-material list (about 1,000 characters a row, every material with free-text fields), the free-text rule and de minimis fields, and a flip on every row; its reasoning was as long as B's. Only the D590 development rows and the D591 figures were read to design this; no held-out file.
- **Variants (at most two, each one run on the same 97 development rows as B, Va and Vb, tags `d600-vc` and `d600-vd`):** both keep Va's change (the facts a plan search renders get the product's own codes, `planner.ClassificationNote`; `eval p102moves -codes-in-facts`) and Vb's four instructions, written tersely, after the usmca-v1 hierarchy unchanged. The answer is fixed short fields through the existing JSON-schema output path, with no free-text essay: word limits on every text field (the essential-character step at most 12 words, the decisive step and the flip at most 15, the reasoning at most 40 against usmca-v1's 80) and enumerated values where the answer is a choice. `LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` is not changed, so a long answer is not cut off.
  - **Vc, compact checklist (`usmca-v4`, `engine.USMCASystem4`, `engine.CompactChecklistSchema`):** `good_hts` (as given, else the engine's reading); `foreign_materials`, one entry per foreign material only, each `{part (at most 3 words), hts, origin, shift: yes | no | unknown}`; `de_minimis`: not needed | applies | does not apply | value not given; `rule_step`: (a)(1) | (a)(2) | (a)(3) | (b) | (c) | (d); then the standard answer fields.
  - **Vd, failing materials only (`usmca-v5`, `engine.USMCASystem5`, `engine.FailingChecklistSchema`):** as Vc, with `foreign_materials` replaced by `failing_materials`, the names (at most 3 words) of the foreign materials that do not make the required change ([] if none). This is the "fewer fields, no per-material list" candidate D591 named.
- **Development runs:** gemini-4-argon, BM25 precedents K = 5, through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini with `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`. (i) Plan rows: `go run ./cmd/eval p102moves -tag d600-vc -usmca-prompt v4 -codes-in-facts` and the same with `-tag d600-vd -usmca-prompt v5`, scored by `go run ./cmd/tariffshift p102err-moves` (series `vc`, `vd`) against B's committed rows. (ii) The 72 development Part 102 rulings, run this time for both variants whatever (i) gives: `go run ./cmd/eval run -regime usmca -split dev -usmca-prompt v4 -tag d600` and `-usmca-prompt v5`, rows moved to `eval/tariffshift/p102ck/runs/` (as D550's), scored by `go run ./cmd/tariffshift p102ck-eval` against D550's usmca-v1 re-run (53 of 72, $0.6881). Single setups get no codes paragraph (their facts are CBP's own text), so (ii) tests the prompt alone. A failed engine call is re-run once (the runner's re-run, or the harness's resume); a call still failed counts as a disagreement and as wrong.
- **Pass rule (each variant against B, all four, the same as D590's):** (1) agreement with the check on the 57 decided rows rises by at least 6 rows net (won minus lost) with an exact two-sided McNemar p below 0.05 on the discordant rows; (2) agreement on the 23 leans is not lower than B's 17; (3) no loss against CBP: on the 16 current setups of the Part 102 fixtures the variant names CBP's holding at least as often as B (8), and on the 72 development rulings its correct count is not lower than D550 B's 53 (McNemar reported); (4) gateway-reported cost at most 1.5 × B's on the same calls, on the plan rows (B $0.8661, so at most $1.2992) and on the 72 rulings (D550 B $0.6881, so at most $1.0322). If both pass, the one with more decided agreement is selected; a tie goes to the cheaper on the plan rows.
- **Held out, only for the selected variant, each window scored once, frozen:** the single-setup held-out windows only, window 1 (`splits_usmca.json` `final`, 32) and window 2 (`splits_usmca_final2.json` `final2`, 13, with `-router` as its committed run), `go run ./cmd/eval run -regime usmca -split final|final2 -usmca-prompt v4|v5 -confirm-final -tag d600`, rows to `eval/tariffshift/p102ck/runs/`. They are compared with the committed `usmca-v1` runs (25 of 32 and 11 of 13, 36 of 45 pooled). Both windows were scored before with `usmca-v1`, once each; this is a candidate comparison and is disclosed as one. The D570 held-out plan set (`testdata/planner_part102_heldout`) is not touched. **Adopted** only if the pooled correct count is at least 36 of 45 (D590's held-out bar, not below `usmca-v1`): the variant's prompt becomes the production Part 102 engine by code default (new prompt version, prompt snapshot updated, model id and prompt registered in the log policy), and a plan search on a Part 102 case renders the product's codes into the facts the engine reads. No deploy change. Safety flag S (D591) stays, and its rate under the adopted engine on the development rows is reported. Otherwise `usmca-v1` with plain facts stays, the variants stay in the code for evaluation only, and the result is reported as negative.

Estimate from the D590 rows: the plan rows cost about $0.9 to $1.2 per variant (input about 340,000 tokens with the codes and the longer prompt; output near B's 28,462 if the limits hold), the 72 rulings about $0.75 to $0.9 per variant, the held-out windows about $0.5: about $3.8 in all. If the running total would pass $6, the remaining runs are not made and are reported as not run.

## D610 — Pre-registration: the auto-accept bar for `usmca-v5` Part 102 answers, set from development rows only (22 Nov, follow-up to D602)
Committed before any bar or map is computed by code and before anything is applied to a held-out row. Nothing below changes because of a held-out result.
- **Problem (D602):** fewer held-out Part 102 answers reach stated confidence 0.95 under `usmca-v5` (17 of 45) than under `usmca-v1` (22 of 45), so with the bar unchanged more Part 102 cases go to review. The 0.95 bar (D61, 17 Oct) was set on the first held-out window for `usmca-v1` and is disclosed as such on /method. The question is whether a bar or a calibration map fitted on development rows lets `usmca-v5` auto-accept more cases without lowering precision.
- **What was read before this entry, disclosed.** The confidence and correctness of the 72 development `usmca-v5` rows and of D550's `usmca-v1` re-run, so the development outcome below is foreseeable. While surveying the files, the per-confidence counts of the committed held-out rows (`usmca-v1` and `usmca-v5`, both windows) were also printed; those rows were all scored and published in D602. The rule is written from the development rows and the earlier bar rule (D61, D160) only.
- **Data:** the 72 development Part 102 rulings answered by `usmca-v5` (`eval/tariffshift/p102ck/runs/usmca-dev-gemini-4-argon-prec-usmca-v5-litellm-d600.jsonl`, no failed call), right or wrong as `p102ck-eval` scores them. The Part 102 triage does not read the router's scope (`triage.USMCA`), so every row counts.
- **Target:** at least 95% right among the development cases auto-accepted, on at least 20 of them (about a quarter of 72; cal-v2 asked for 100 of 463, D160).
- **Rule (one map, the cal-v2 procedure):** `cal-p102-v1`, isotonic regression (pool-adjacent-violators) on stated confidence after pooling adjacent confidence values, lowest first, into blocks of at least 20 cases, a short last block joining the one below, capped at 0.99; a value between steps takes the step at or below it. Its bar is the lowest calibrated step whose development cases at or above it are at least 95% right, with at least 20 of them. With the map, triage would compare the calibrated value with `USMCA_FAST_PATH` (0.95 as deployed), so the deployed bar would mean the target precision; the calibrated value would also be the one shown for Part 102 answers.
- **Reported beside it, not deciding:** the stated-confidence curve, every stated value `usmca-v5` emitted on development as a bar, with cases accepted and right (the same rule on stated values: the lowest stated bar at least 95% right on at least 20 cases).
- **Coverage gain needed on development:** the map is a candidate only if it auto-accepts at least 20 development cases and more than stated 0.95 does on the same rows. If not, nothing is applied as a candidate: the bar stays stated 0.95 and the map is not shipped.
- **Held out, once, no model calls:** a candidate map is applied unchanged to the committed `usmca-v5` held-out rows (window 1, 32, and window 2, 13, from D601). **Adopted** only if, pooled over the 45, it auto-accepts more than stated 0.95 does (17) and at least 95% of what it accepts is right. Adoption is a code default: the map is embedded for `usmca-v5` on the primary model, Part 102 triage reads it, and calibrated confidence is shown for Part 102 answers. Otherwise the bar stays stated 0.95 and is documented. Either way the held-out coverage and precision at stated 0.95 (before) and under the rule's outcome (after) are reported, with the stated bar table on both windows for `usmca-v1` and `usmca-v5`, and the map's held-out ECE beside stated confidence's, computed once.
- **Tool:** `go run ./cmd/tariffshift p102bar` writes `eval/tariffshift/p102bar/summary.json` from committed rows (in `make reproduce`). No model calls, no cost.

## D611 — Pre-registration: why the Part 102 window-1 95th-percentile latency rose, and one tail fix measured on development (22 Nov, follow-up to D602)
Committed before the development re-run below.
- **Problem (D602):** window 1's 95th-percentile per-call latency rose from 9.2 s (`usmca-v1`, October) to 27.8 s (`usmca-v5`). With 32 rows the 95th percentile is the second-slowest call.
- **From committed rows first, no calls:** for each Part 102 run in `p102ck-eval`, the slowest calls with their output and input tokens, and the rank correlation of latency with output tokens. `latency_ms` is one HTTP attempt (the engine records the answering response's latency; a retried attempt is not in it), and no row carries an error. Three causes are named: long outputs (then output tokens track latency), retries (then wall time exceeds `latency_ms`; not measurable from the committed rows), or the gateway and provider (slow calls with ordinary output).
- **Candidate fix, a hedged request (`llm.WithHedge`, eval flag `-hedge-after`, default off):** if a call has not answered after T, the same request is sent once more and the first answer is used; the other is cancelled. T = 12 s (about the 85th percentile of `usmca-v5` on the 72 development rulings). Output limits are not a candidate if the slow calls have ordinary output. A shorter timeout with a retry is not a candidate: a retry starts only after the timeout and a backoff, so calls a little over the timeout would get slower.
- **Run:** two arms started at the same time on the 72 development Part 102 rulings, `usmca-v5`, gemini-4-argon, BM25 K = 5, through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini, `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, 8 workers each: A `go run ./cmd/eval run -regime usmca -split dev -usmca-prompt v5 -tag d611-a`, B the same with `-hedge-after 12s -tag d611-b`. Each row records a new `wall_ms`, the time of the whole engine call (retries and hedges included). A failed call is re-run once by resume; a call still failed counts as wrong.
- **Reported:** per arm, `wall_ms` median and 95th percentile, `latency_ms` the same, correct of 72, output tokens, gateway cost, hedges sent (B rows with `wall_ms` at or above 12 s). Whether the slow rulings of A are slow in D600's run too (if the same rulings are slow, the cause is the input, not the gateway).
- **Rule for proposing the hedge:** B's 95th-percentile wall time at least 20% below A's, B's correct count not below A's minus 3 (run-to-run noise, D551), and B's gateway cost at most 1.3 × A's. If it passes, the hedge is proposed with its tests for the owner to turn on; the server is not changed in this PR (production calls Vertex AI, not the gateway, so a gateway result does not carry over). If it fails, it is reported as negative and stays an eval option.
- **Budget:** at most $2 gateway-reported for both arms (estimate: A about $0.73, as D600's Vd run; B about $0.73 plus the hedged calls, about $0.10). A cancelled hedge may be billed without its cost reaching us; such calls are counted at the arm's mean cost per call and added to the reported spend.

## D612 — Window 2's Part 102 runs had almost no precedents; `eval run` now stops on a missing facts directory (22 Nov, follow-up to D602)
- **Found (D602):** the committed window-2 Part 102 command (D210) and the `usmca-v5` run that repeated it pass `-facts ../data/facts,../eval/data/facts_final2`. From `backend/`, `../data/facts` does not exist, and the corpus loader skipped a missing directory in silence. Of the 488 labelled Part 102 rulings (473 in `labels_usmca.jsonl`, 15 in `labels_usmca_final2.jsonl`), only the 15 window-2 rulings had facts, so each window-2 case could use only earlier window-2 rulings as precedents (N365110 had none in the `usmca-v5` run). The textile and pharmaceutical window-2 commands name `../data/corpus/facts` and are not affected.
- **Fix:** `eval run` checks every `-facts` directory and stops with an error naming a missing one (`existingDirs`, `TestExistingDirsRejectsAMissingFactsDirectory`). The corrected window-2 command uses `-facts ../data/corpus/facts,../eval/data/facts_final2` (a local corpus build), or the committed bundle `data/facts,../eval/data/facts_final2`, which has the facts of all 473 first-pool rulings (`TestWindow2FactsPathsExist`). D210's command carries a note.
- **Not done:** window 2 is not re-scored, for `usmca-v1` or `usmca-v5`. Its published counts (11 of 13 each) stand as measured with the 15-ruling pool and say so; a future window-2 run with the full pool would be a new candidate comparison and would be logged as one.

## D613 — The `usmca-v5` auto-accept bar: no development rule gains coverage; the bar stays stated 0.95 (22 Nov, results of D610)
- **Run as pre-registered in D610** (pushed as b7cbefb9 before `p102bar` was written; fe0d0f22 after the rebase onto main), from committed rows, no model calls: `cd backend && go run ./cmd/tariffshift p102bar -check` (in `make reproduce`), `eval/tariffshift/p102bar/summary.json`.
- **Development, `usmca-v5`, 72 rulings, 53 right.** The map `cal-p102-v1` has two steps: stated 0.45 to 0.90 maps to 0.4483 (29 cases, 13 right) and stated 0.92 to 0.98 to 0.9302 (43 cases, 40 right). Pooling into blocks of 20 joins the 10 cases at 0.96 and 0.98 (all right) with the 33 at 0.92 and 0.95. No step is at least 95% right, so the map has no bar and is **not a candidate**. Nothing was applied to a held-out row as a candidate; the map is not shipped and Part 102 answers still show no calibrated value.
- **Stated bars on development** (reported, not deciding):

  | Stated bar | `usmca-v5`: accepted, right | `usmca-v1` (D550 re-run): accepted, right |
  |---|---|---|
  | 0.98 | 8, 8 | 12, 12 |
  | 0.96 | 10, 10 | 19, 19 |
  | 0.95 | 38, 36 (94.7%, 95% CI 82.7–98.5) | 38, 36 (94.7%) |
  | 0.92 | 43, 40 (93.0%) | 50, 45 (90.0%) |
  | 0.90 | 54, 45 (83.3%) | 58, 46 (79.3%) |

  The same rule on stated values finds no bar either: 0.96 is 10 of 10 but under 20 cases, and 0.95 is just under 95% for both engines.
- **Held out, the committed rows, before and after.** The rule's outcome is the unchanged stated 0.95, so before and after are the same: `usmca-v5` auto-accepts 11 of 32 on window 1 (11 right) and 6 of 13 on window 2 (5 right), 17 of 45 pooled, 16 right (94.1%, 95% CI 73.0–99.0); `usmca-v1` 22 of 45, 21 right (95.5%). The stated table on both windows (reported once, no decision taken from it):

  | Stated bar | `usmca-v1` pooled: accepted, right | `usmca-v5` pooled: accepted, right |
  |---|---|---|
  | 0.96 | 12, 12 | 6, 6 |
  | 0.95 | 22, 21 | 17, 16 |
  | 0.92 | 28, 26 (92.9%) | 19, 18 (94.7%) |
  | 0.90 | 32, 29 (90.6%) | 32, 29 (90.6%) |

  Held-out calibration, computed once on the 45 `usmca-v5` rows, one bin per value: ECE 0.0916 for stated confidence and 0.2371 for the map (its low step puts the six held-out answers at 0.75, all right, at 0.45). The map would make the shown value worse.
- **What this means.** Lowering the bar does not hold the 95% target on development (0.92 is 93.0%) and the held-out rows agree (0.92 is 94.7%). The fall in coverage under `usmca-v5` (17 of 45 against 22) is the cost of the engine change at the same bar; no bar picked from development recovers it at 95% precision. A finding outside D610's question, flagged for the owner and not acted on: on development neither engine reaches 95% at stated 0.95 (36 of 38 each), and `usmca-v5` is 16 of 17 held out at 0.95. Only 0.96 and above are error-free on development, on 10 cases for `usmca-v5`. The deployed bar (`USMCA_FAST_PATH`, set in the deployment, which this work does not touch) is unchanged.
- **Not done:** no new held-out model call. The map and table are on one development run; run-to-run noise on the 72 is about 1 to 3 rulings (D551), and on the D611 re-run arm A `usmca-v5` was 57 of 72 with 36 auto-accepted at 0.95, 35 right, which shows how much a 38-case block moves between runs.

## D614 — The Part 102 latency tail is the gateway, not the prompt; the hedged request helps only under load and is not proposed as a default (22 Nov, results of D611)
- **Run as pre-registered in D611** (pushed as b7cbefb9; the tooling as e67c15a4, both before the first call; fe0d0f22 and 25c1ba93 after the rebase onto main, and the re-run rows record e67c15a4). `p102bar` reads the committed rows and the two arms (`eval/tariffshift/p102bar/summary.json`, rows in `eval/tariffshift/p102bar/runs/`).
- **From the committed rows, no calls.** Window 1's two slowest `usmca-v5` calls took 28.4 s and 27.8 s with 200 and 274 output tokens, below the run's median of 256; with 32 rows the 95th percentile is the second of them. Neither carries an error, and `latency_ms` is one attempt, so they are single slow responses, not retries and not long answers. Latency follows output tokens only weakly in every run (rank correlation 0.32 to 0.51). The slow tail is not new: `usmca-v1`'s development re-run had calls of 27.3, 26.1 and 25.5 s with ordinary output, and on the 72 development rulings `usmca-v5`'s 95th percentile (18.3 s) is below `usmca-v1`'s (21.8 s).

  | Run | Median / 95th percentile per call, `usmca-v1` | Same, `usmca-v5` |
  |---|---|---|
  | 72 development rulings | 8.4 s / 21.8 s | 7.9 s / 18.3 s |
  | Window 1 (32) | 7.1 s / 9.2 s | 7.7 s / 27.8 s |
  | Window 2 (13) | 8.5 s / 16.4 s | 7.4 s / 17.5 s |

- **The development re-run, two arms at once** (`usmca-dev-gemini-4-argon-prec-usmca-v5-litellm-d611-a` and `-d611-b`). The gateway was slower than in D600: the median call took 12.6 s against 7.9 s for the same prompt on the same rulings, and 8 of arm A's 72 calls hit the 30 s per-attempt timeout and were retried. Arm A's per-ruling latency does not follow D600's (rank correlation −0.07; its four slowest rulings ranked 2, 34, 48 and 66 of 72 there), so which call is slow depends on the moment, not the input.

  | Arm | Wall time per case, median / 95th percentile | Answering call, median / 95th percentile | Correct of 72 | Output tokens | Gateway-reported cost |
  |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
  | A: no hedge | 13.1 s / 51.4 s | 12.6 s / 27.5 s | 57 | 19,969 | $0.5834 |
  | B: hedge after 12 s | 13.0 s / 40.2 s | 12.8 s / 28.2 s | 54 | 19,086 | $0.7079 |

- **D611's rule:** (1) B's 95th-percentile wall time is 22% below A's (40.2 s against 51.4 s; at least 20% needed): passes. (2) 54 against 57, within the 3 allowed: passes. (3) Cost: 1.21 × A on gateway-reported cost, which passes, but a hedge was sent on 38 of 72 calls (estimated from wall time) and the gateway reports no cost for the cancelled one; counted at the mean cost per call, as D611's spend clause counts them, B is about $1.0815, 1.85 × A, which fails. The cost condition should not have been in D611: under the owner's decision of 22 Nov cost is reported, not a pass condition. Disclosed rather than re-read after the result.
- **Decision: not proposed as a default.** The gain shows only at the 95th percentile, under a gateway slow enough that about half the calls passed 12 s, and the hedge then doubles those calls; the median did not move, and B answered three fewer rulings right (within noise). With the gateway as it was in D600 (median 7.9 s) a 12 s hedge would fire on 9 of 72 calls. Production calls Vertex AI, not the gateway, and tries the primary model once before the fallback model (deployment settings, not changed here), so a gateway result does not carry over. `llm.WithHedge` and `eval run -hedge-after` stay as an evaluation option, off by default, with tests (`TestHedge*`); the server does not use them. Output limits are not a fix: the slow calls have ordinary output, and `usmca-v5`'s answers are already shorter than `usmca-v1`'s.
- **Spend:** $1.6649 counted (A $0.5834, B $0.7079 reported, plus $0.3736 estimated for cancelled hedges), within the $2 set in D611.

  | Same, on the four fixtures both runs share | 1 of 3 | 3 of 3 |
  | Shown plans; the rule says they shift | 1; 1 | 1; 1 |
  | Moves precedent supports while the rule gives another country | 0 | 0 |
  | Rows marked for review (D441 or D591, scored by today's code) | 1 (N358639, the brackets move) | 0 |
  | Current setup: rule decides; gives CBP's holding | 6 of 6; 5 | 7 of 8; 6 |
  | Current setup: engine gives CBP's holding | 5 of 6 | 6 of 8 |
  | Backtests | 0 | 0 |
  | Plan-search cost, total; a search | $0.2195; $0.037 | $0.1757; $0.022 |
  | Search wall time, median / 95th percentile | 20.0 s / 35.0 s | 12.5 s / 40.2 s |

- **Against the D630 expectations.** Agreement rose, as expected, to 6 of 6; on the four shared fixtures 3 of 3, at the top of the expected 2 to 3. Shown plans stayed few (1), and coverage is D581's 8 of 18.
- **Where it changed.** The two D571 misses on shared fixtures were reverse probes (N359145 to Thailand, N362414 to China), where `usmca-v1` predicted the target although final assembly stays in Canada; `usmca-v5` keeps Canada on both, as the rule does. N358639 is not like for like: the metal-products fixture puts all three Korean parts in one group, so its one move is the pipes, flange and brackets together, which the rule says shifts, the engine predicts Mexico, and the precedent check supports at 0.95 (N353124); it is the one shown plan. D571's lone disagreement there (the brackets alone) is not a move in this fixture.
- **Reading.** Five of the six decided moves are moves where the rule keeps the country CBP held, so an engine that never predicted the target would also agree on 5 of 6; the figure says `usmca-v5` no longer reads reverse probes as shifts, and agrees on the one move that does shift. On the current setup the engine missed one more ruling than before: N363381, where it gives the United States (the dust mop is made there) and CBP held Canada; the rule cannot decide that good (chapter 96 is not encoded). N358639 is still missed by both, as in D571. Moves within a search are not independent, 6 is small, and each search ran once. Agreement with the rule is not accuracy. This is the first held-out evidence that the D602 change carries over to plan searches, not only to single setups.
- **The actuator page (development, D630).** One search, `eval plan -regime usmca_part102 -fixture testdata/planner_part102/n348465.json -tag d630`, at 16:15, $0.2923, 47 s. `usmca-v5` agrees with the rule on 12 of 12 moves; `usmca-v1` in D541 also 12 of 12, the general engine 9 of 12. Two shown plans, both motor moves the rule says shift (motor with controls, and motor with gearbox and controls, precedent check 0.92 citing H322161); the D541 run showed two others citing N346297. `/examples/part102-plan` now shows this run, with the `usmca-v1` and general-engine predictions beside each move, and says which run and engine each is (`plans102-example -check` in `make reproduce`). The other two development searches were not re-run, so the compressors move (wrong under `usmca-v1`, D541) is not re-measured.
- **Spend:** $0.4806 gateway-reported: group calls $0.0126, held-out plan searches $0.1757, actuator search $0.2923. Within D630's $2.5 and $0.3.

## D642 — Part 102 copy after D602 and D612: the engine's version, no clean check for `usmca-v5`, the window-2 pool note, the plan base rate on /accuracy (22 Nov, #643, judge panel round 14 item 2)
- **What changed (wording only, no figure changes).** `docs/claims-reconciliation.md` names `engine.USMCAProduction` (`USMCASystem5`, `usmca-v5` since D602) as the Part 102 engine, with `usmca-v1` as the engine before it. /method's shortfall list keeps the second window as the clean check for the textile and pharmaceutical engines, and says the Part 102 engine in use has none: `usmca-v5` was picked on development rulings and then scored once on both windows, which `usmca-v1` had already been scored on (a candidate comparison, D602), and window 2's runs had only the 15 window-2 rulings as precedents (D612). The window-2 Part 102 figures now carry that pool note where they are shown: /accuracy's Part 102 card, the served `usmca_final2_accuracy` and `usmca_v5_final2_*` labels (`go run ./cmd/eval summary`), claims-reconciliation's `regimes.w2.part102` rows, NUMBERS, EVALUATION §8 and §16.1 and the model card. /accuracy's held-out plan sentence adds that five of the six decided moves keep the country CBP held (D631), as README, /method and NUMBERS already say.

## D643 — Delete-case focus restore keyed by case id (22 Nov, #622)
- The cases table remembered the row's display name when **Delete case…** opened and focused the first `Actions for <name>` trigger on cancel. Two cases can share a name (it defaults to the product name), so cancelling on the second focused the first. The trigger now carries `data-row-menu-trigger={case id}` and the restore looks it up by id. `ui-check` stubs two writable cases with the same name, opens Delete from the second, and checks that Escape and Cancel both return focus to the second row's trigger.

## D640 — The product's codes reach the Part 102 engine only, not the precedent check, near-miss advice or the broker draft (22 Nov, #642, judge panel round 14 item 1)
- **What was wrong.** D602 shipped `Options.CodesInFacts` to state the product's own codes "in the facts the engine reads". The planner rendered one string, so the codes paragraph ("the product's own codes, not verified by CBP") also went to the precedent check (`verifier.Task` FactsA and FactsB), near-miss advice (`nearmiss.Task`) and the stored `VariantFacts`, which become the drafted ruling request's facts. D600 to D602 measured the paragraph on the engine only (`eval p102moves -codes-in-facts`); the 0.92 plan bar was set on plain facts.
- **What ships.** `Planner.render` returns two strings: the engine's facts (Render plus `ClassificationNote` when the regime is in `CodesInFacts`) and the plain facts (Render). Only the engine's prediction and its cache key read the first. The precedent check, near-miss advice, `VariantFacts` (the broker draft) and `Estimate`'s verdict and advice peeks read the plain facts, as before D602. This restores what D602 pre-registered; it is not a new change to any gate, so nothing is re-measured. Verdicts cached before D602 match again.
- **Tests.** `TestAudit638CodesReachOnlyTheEngine` (planner: engine facts carry the paragraph; verifier tasks, near-miss tasks and every plan's `VariantFacts` do not, and the baseline's equal Render), `TestEstimatePeeksTheRegimeEngine` (the estimate finds every check the search stored), and `TestPart102PlanDraftHasNoCodesParagraph` (httpapi: a Part 102 plan search through the handlers; the engine read the paragraph, the stored plan and both draft formats do not). Both new tests fail on the code before this change.
- **Committed runs not re-run.** The plan searches recorded since D602 ran with the paragraph in the precedent check's and near-miss inputs and in `VariantFacts`: the D630 held-out pass and the D630 actuator search (D631), whose files stay as committed. Their precedent verdicts, including the shown plans' confidences (N358639 at 0.95, the actuator's at 0.92), were made with the paragraph present and should be read that way. The engine predictions and the engine–rule agreement figures (6 of 6 held out, 12 of 12 on the actuator) do not depend on it. The D630 run files still carry the paragraph in their stored facts; the recorded page does not show those facts. No model call.

## D641 — Plan sentences name one leftover part, and join several groups once (22 Nov, judge panel round 14 item 3, #633 residue)
- **What was wrong.** D622's shorter group names counted the parts they did not cover, so one leftover read "1 other part", and Describe joined each group's own "A and B" phrase with another "and": "Move the motor stator and the control boards and 1 other part to Canada", while the "Moves:" line beneath named the part.
- **What ships.** A single leftover part is named ("the control boards and the electrical apparatus"); two or more stay a count ("4 other parts"). On a move to one country the items of every group are joined once, with commas and a final "and": "Move the motor stator, the control boards and the electrical apparatus to Canada". A template name that fits stays one item, so a name that contains "and" ("PCBA and sensors") can still meet another "and". Moves to several countries are worded as before.
- **Recorded page.** `/examples/part102-plan` takes its plan sentences from a recorded run. `plans102-example` now rebuilds them from the recorded moves with `planner.Redescribe`, as the server does for a stored search; moves, predictions and verdicts are as recorded, and the page note says so. Besides the D641 wording, this also applies D622 to that run: "the housing and machined block" reads "the housing" (the product has housings and no machined block).
- **Tests.** `TestDescribeNamesOneLeftoverAndJoinsOnce` (the N348465 actuator); one intended expectation change in `TestGroupPhraseNamesThePartsWhenTheTemplateNameDoesNotFit` ("the PCBA and the temperature control module"). No other golden changed.

## D650 — Pre-registration: a compact component checklist for the substantial-transformation engine (22 Nov, follow-up to D157, D164 and D602)
Committed before any run of either variant. Nothing below changes because of a variant's result.
- **Why:** the largest error group of the production engine (engine-v1 on Gemini 4 Argon) is CBP holding China, where the components or sub-assemblies were made, while the engine named the assembling country (13 of 37 misses on the 377-ruling held-out split, 4 of 6 on final2; D154, D163). Two fixes failed on development: a written rule (rules-v2, D157: 90.9% against 91.8%) and a second-stage adjudicator (D164: no variant passed). For the Part 102 engine a short structured checklist in the answer worked (usmca-v5, D600 to D602). This tries the same idea for the general engine.
- **What was read to design it:** the engine-v1 prompt, D150 to D164, D600 to D602, and the development rows of engine-v1 through the gateway (`eval/results/dev-gemini-4-argon-prec-engine-v1-litellm-gw.jsonl`). On those rows (463 after the D23 adjustments) 12 of the 78 China-held rulings are wrong, each naming the assembling or processing country, and 18 rulings held elsewhere are wrong with China named: the errors go both ways, as D157 found. No held-out failure was read; only the published held-out counts (D39, D154) are used, in the adoption rule below.
- **Variants (at most two, `internal/engine/st_checklist.go`, eval only):** both keep engine-v1's task and test word for word (`stHead`) and add a checklist the engine fills before it answers, through the JSON-schema output path, with word limits on every text field and no rule about which way a case goes.
  - **Va, `st-checklist-v1` (`-st-prompt ck1`):** `assembly_country`; `components`, at most 5 major components or sub-assemblies, each `{part (at most 4 words), origin, essential (true | false), processing in the assembly country (at most 10 words), transforms: yes | no | unclear (new name, character or use), precedents (ruling numbers shown, [] if none)}`; then engine-v1's answer fields with limits (essential character 12 words, decisive step 15, flip 15, reasoning 50 against engine-v1's 80).
  - **Vb, `st-checklist-v2` (`-st-prompt ck2`):** Va plus a precedent comparison: the closest earlier ruling shown in which CBP held a component's or sub-assembly's country although the article was assembled elsewhere, and the closest in which CBP held the assembling country (`{ruling or null, differs (at most 12 words)}` each), `closer: component | assembly | neither`, and the instruction to follow the closer one. The comparison names both directions, not only the component-country one, because the development errors go both ways (D157).
  - Fingerprinted in `internal/promptsnap` (`engine.st_checklist1`, `engine.st_checklist2`). The eval row keeps the whole answer (`answer`).
- **Runs:** Gemini 4 Argon, BM25, K = 5, temperature 0, through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini, `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, the local corpus (`../data/corpus/facts`, the same pool as the baseline), no `-router` (as the baseline). First a format check: 5 development cases per variant (`-limit 5 -tag smoke`), to see that answers parse and to measure tokens and cost; it is not scored for selection, and its rows are committed. If it shows a format fault, the prompt is fixed before the full run, under a new version name, and the fix is disclosed. Then one full run per variant on the 469 development rulings: `go run ./cmd/eval run -split dev -st-prompt ck1 -tag d650` and the same with `ck2`. A call still failed after one resume counts as wrong.
- **Baseline:** engine-v1 on Argon through the gateway, run 1 of D190 (`...-litellm-gw.jsonl`): 425 of 463 = 91.8%; China-held (CBP held China) 66 of 78; the other 385 rulings 359. Run-to-run noise: three engine-v1 runs gave 425, 422 and 422 (spread 0.7 points, 4 answer flips; D190).
- **Pass rule, each variant against the baseline on the 463 adjusted development rulings, all four:** (1) accuracy at least 425 of 463 (91.8%); (2) net fixed minus broke at least +5, above the 4-flip run-to-run noise; (3) China-held: more right than 66 of 78; (4) the other 385: at most 2 fewer right than 359 (no net loss of 3 or more). The exact two-sided McNemar p against the baseline is reported, not gated, and so are McNemar against runs 2 and 3 of D190. Cost is not a condition (owner decision, D601 and the programme rule); gateway cost per case, output tokens and per-call latency p50 / p95 are reported, and a cost above 3 times the baseline's is flagged. If both pass, one winner: higher development accuracy, then more China-held right, then lower p50 latency.
- **Held out, only for the winner, each split scored once:** the 377-ruling split (`-split final -confirm-final -st-prompt ckN -tag d650`, no router; fast path on the fixed Vertex scope file, as the D240 repeats) and final2 (83; `-split final2 -confirm-final -router -splits ../eval/splits/splits_final2.json -labels ../eval/data/labels.jsonl,../eval/data/labels_final2.jsonl -facts ../data/corpus/facts,../eval/data/facts_final2 -st-prompt ckN -tag d650`, as D241). Both splits were scored before by engine-v1 (official: 340 of 377 on Vertex AI, 77 of 83 through the gateway); this is a candidate comparison and is disclosed as one. Reported: accuracy with Wilson 95% intervals, exact McNemar against the official engine-v1 rows, China-held accuracy, ECE and Brier of stated confidence, and auto-accept coverage and accuracy at the cal-v2 bar. cal-v2 is fitted to engine-v1's confidences (D160), so it is applied only as a reading of the raw numbers; a new engine needs its own map.
- **Adopted** as the production engine only if, on held out, accuracy is not lower than engine-v1's on either split (at least 340 of 377 and 77 of 83) and the China-held count, pooled over both splits, is higher than engine-v1's. Then: the checklist prompt becomes the code default under a new prompt version, the prompt snapshot and the log policy are updated, and a new calibration map is fitted on the variant's development rows by the D160 rules before any calibrated value is shown for it (until then the product shows stated confidence for it). Otherwise engine-v1 stays, the variants stay eval only, and the result is reported as negative.
- **Budget:** at most $15 gateway-reported for this item. Estimate from the baseline rows (2,836 input and 226 output tokens a case, $0.0079): about 300 more input tokens and 200 to 400 more output tokens give about $0.010 to $0.012 a case, about $5 to $5.6 per development run and $4.8 to $5.6 for both held-out splits. Before each full run, the spend so far plus that run's estimate plus a held-out reserve (460 cases at the highest per-case cost measured so far) must stay within $15; a run that would not fit is not made and is reported as not run.

- **Run as pre-registered in D650** (committed and pushed as 91225141 at 17:07 +08:00, before the first variant call; that is the `git_revision` RUNLOG records for the runs below, and the hash is from before the rebase onto main). - **Va, `st-checklist-v1`, development set (463 after the D23 adjustments), one run, no failed calls** (`eval/results/st-checklist-metrics.json`, `python3 -I eval/charts/build_st_checklist.py .`):

  | Run | Accuracy (95% CI) | China-held (78) | Not China-held (385) | Fixed / broke vs engine-v1, exact McNemar p | Fast path (stated ≥ 0.92, in scope) | Output tokens | Cost / case | p50 / p95 |
  |---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---:|---|---|
  | engine-v1, gateway (D190 run 1) | 91.8% (88.9–94.0) | 66 | 359 | | 375 at 95.7% | 226 | $0.0079 | 6.8 s / 10.8 s |
  | Va: st-checklist-v1 | 91.1% (88.2–93.4) | 67 | 355 | 5 / 8, p = 0.58 | 359 at 96.9% | 420 | $0.0109 (1.38 ×) | 9.5 s / 15.4 s |

It is reported as not run. Running it would need about $2 more for this item.

- **Spend:** $5.1544 gateway-reported for D650 and D651 ($0.1288 for the format check, $5.0256 for the Va run), within D650's $15.

## D660 — Six more plan templates, chosen from development and pool rulings with no template in either regime; pre-registration of one held-out family check (22 Nov, follow-up to D580)
Committed and pushed before the held-out family check below. Nothing in the templates changes because of a held-out result.
- **Problem.** With 20 families, the production family check (`family-check-v1`, gemini-3.8-flash, bar 0.6) found a template for 317 of 469 general development rulings (67.6%) and 49 of 72 Part 102 development rulings (68.1%). A product with no template gets an origin and no plan.
- **Selection set (no held-out ruling is read).** Substantial transformation: the 469 development rulings and a new pool (`eval/families/pool_r3.py`, `r3-st-pool.json`): labelled substantial-transformation rulings with facts, dated before 2026, in no `final`, `final2`, `pilot` or `tune_check` list of any split file and not in dev, 754 rulings, of which `familycov` reads the 661 with one held origin. Part 102: the 72 development rulings and D580's pool (239). `select_r3.py` stops if any of these lists holds a held-out ruling. The family check with 20 templates was run on both pools (`families-coverage-train-all-litellm-{r3stpool,p102pool}-f20.jsonl`, $2.41); development already had its 20-template runs (D580). A ruling in two sets is counted once: 1,436 rulings, 996 with a template, 440 without.
- **What lacks a template.** gemini-3.8-flash gave each of the 440 a product category (D580's list), a product noun and, from the full text by regex, the good's code (`label_r3.py`, `families-r3-labels.jsonl`, $0.51). The code was found for few substantial-transformation rulings, so product nouns carry the grouping. By product type (step 2 below), with no template, then pool rulings of the type in its regime:

  | Product type | No template (dev + pool) | Pool rulings in regime | Picked |
  |---|---:|---:|---|
  | Paper, tissue and paperboard (napkins, toilet tissue, towels, folders) | 73 | 55 | yes |
  | Automotive air, oil and cabin filters | 23 | 0 | no: no pool ruling to write from |
  | Off-road vehicles and mobile machinery (UTVs, AGVs, excavators, telehandlers) | 20 | 13 | yes |
  | Semiconductor devices (integrated circuits, transistors, diodes) | 16 | 10 | yes |
  | Bicycles, e-bikes and scooters | 13 | 4 | no: 4 pool rulings |
  | Golf clubs and sporting goods | 13 | 6 | yes |
  | Toys and build kits | 12 | 13 | yes |
  | Heat pumps, furnaces, gas heaters and air conditioners | 11 | 5 | yes |
  | Lifting jacks 9, batteries 8, solar 7, pens and pencils 6 | under 10 | | no |

  229 rulings with no template fit no type: chemicals and pharmaceuticals 67 (own engine), household goods 23, machinery parts 12, electrical apparatus 10, then 9 or fewer each.
- **Selection rule (`eval/families/select_r3.py`, `families-r3-selection.json`), in two steps, disclosed as run.** Step 1, written before the counts were seen, counted by category as D580 did (leave out categories with a template, the two regimes with their own engines and "other"; at least 10 with no template, 6 in a pool; at most 8). It kept 5 categories, two of them unrelated goods under one label (household goods; toys and sporting goods), and missed types filed under a category that has a template (integrated circuits under PCBA devices, car air filters under filters). Step 2, written after step 1's counts and nouns were seen, groups by product type: a fixed pattern over each ruling's product noun and subject. Keep types with at least 10 rulings with no template and at least 5 pool rulings of the type in one regime (a template cites one regime's pool and never a development ruling); by count, at most 8. Six types pass, all substantial transformation by majority of their pool rulings. The first semiconductor pattern also caught four thin-film transistor LCD modules; a display pattern now comes first, and that family was drafted again from its 10 pool rulings (the first draft and its checks are kept: `families-r3-draft-semiconductors-first.json`, the first 28 semiconductor rows of the check file).
- **Writing, the D138 method.** gemini-4-argon drafted each template from its pool rulings with D138's prompt (`draft_r3.py`, `families-r3-drafts.json`); gemini-3.8-flash checked every citation against the ruling's facts and holding with D138's check (`verify_r3.py`, `families-r3-citation-checks.jsonl`). Two movable groups had no supported citation and were merged (`merge_r3.py`): golf ball forming into club head forming, and build-kit wood and acrylic parts into motors and electronics; both receiving groups were checked again under the new wording, 9 of 9 supported. Unsupported citations were dropped and notes that cited them rewritten (`finalize_r3.py`). The agent read the holding and facts of every citation in a movable group: the semiconductor bare-wafer citations are rulings where the wafer was made in the country of the front-end work CBP held decisive, and the note says so; two notes the rewrite got wrong were rewritten by hand (`write_r3.py`: the ski binding group, and the HVAC heat exchanger group, whose note misread N347271). ## D670 — Amendment to D631: the second held-out plan pass is a candidate comparison, not new held-out evidence (22 Nov, #649, judge panel round 15 item 1)
- **What was wrong.** D631 read its result as "the first held-out evidence that the D602 change carries over to plan searches". All 8 rulings it planned are window-1 rulings (`eval/tariffshift/plans102/heldout/frozen.json`, `window: final`). `usmca-v5` was scored on that window in the held-out run D601 set out (tag `d601`, 15:21 +08:00, results in D602), and its adoption was gated on that result (D602). So the engine under test in D630 had been chosen partly on its held-out answers for these same rulings. D600 and D630 said the D570 plan set was "not touched"; that holds for plan searches, not for the rulings' current setups.
- **The current-setup figure is D601's.** The engine gives CBP's holding on 6 of 8 current setups in D631, the same 6 as in the D601 window-1 rows, with the same two misses and the same wrong countries (N358639: Mexico, CBP South Korea; N363381: the United States, CBP Canada). `eval/tariffshift/p102ck/runs/usmca-final-gemini-4-argon-prec-usmca-v5-litellm-d601.jsonl` against `eval/tariffshift/plans102/summary-heldout2.json`, ruling for ruling. N363381 is not a new miss: D571 did not plan it (no template then), and D601 had already scored it wrong.
- **How D631 now reads.** The D631 figures stand as measured (8 of 18 planned, 6 of 6 decided moves agree with the rule, 1 shown plan). The move-level agreement is a different quantity from D601's single-setup accuracy, and the move facts differ from the window facts, but the pass is a candidate comparison like D602's, not a clean held-out check of `usmca-v5`. Its "Reading" sentence on N363381 ("missed one more ruling than before") and its last sentence ("the first held-out evidence ...") are superseded by this entry. The `usmca-v5` Part 102 engine has no clean held-out check of plan searches; a fresh one needs Part 102 rulings published after the D601 windows.
- **D640 caveat carried with it.** The D631 precedent verdicts (N358639 at 0.95, the actuator's shown plans at 0.92) were made while the codes paragraph was still in the precedent check's facts (D640). That note now sits beside those verdicts in NUMBERS, EVALUATION §15.2 and the recorded actuator page note, not only in D640.
- **Where it changed (wording only, no figure changes).** EVALUATION §15.2, NUMBERS (the D630/D631 rows), /method, /accuracy, README and MODEL-CARD now call the pass a candidate comparison on window-1 rulings scored in D601 and say the 6 of 8 current-setup result is D601's. claimscheck fails on "first held-out evidence" in the public text it reads — the README, `docs` except this log, `eval/RESULTS.md` (added by the #658 amendment), the site, the MCP server and backend strings — and on "held-out evidence" beside `usmca-v5` unless the line says it is not, or calls it a candidate comparison (`TestStaleRound15PhrasesFail`). It also fails on the superseded "one more current setup" / "new miss" reading of N363381 (`TestStaleN363381ReadingFails`).

## D690 — RCEP preferential-origin calculator: official Annex 3A rules (HS 2022) in tested Go code, its own route, MCP tool and case panel (22 Nov, #662, J4)
- **Problem.** Every answer the product gives is U.S. non-preferential or marking origin. A manufacturer moving final assembly out of China into an RCEP country also asks whether the good can claim the RCEP preferential tariff. That is a different question with published, mostly mechanical rules, so it belongs in code, not in a prompt.
- **Rule data.** The RCEP Agreement's Annex 3A product-specific rules transposed to HS 2022 (adopted by the RCEP Joint Committee 30 June 2022, editorial revision 20 August 2022, applied from 1 January 2023), from the RCEP Secretariat PDF; cross-checked against the Australian Border Force copy. URLs, retrieval date (22 Nov 2026), page counts and SHA-256 of both files are in `eval/rcep/source.json`; the two Secretariat URLs served byte-identical files. Neither PDF states a reuse licence; the rules are the text of a public international agreement, the parsed table is committed with attribution (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES) and the PDFs are not redistributed.
- **Parse (`eval/rcep/parse_psr.py`, pdfplumber table cells, no model).** Rule cells split across a page break are joined to the row above; section banners and dash-only description rows are dropped. 2,452 rows: 96 chapters (01 to 97; there is no chapter 77), 263 chapter or heading rows with no rule of their own (their subheadings carry it), 2,189 rows with a rule. A small grammar reads 2,181 of them: WO, CC, CTH, CTSH, RVC40 (one row writes "RVC 40"), CR, "or" between alternatives, and "except from" chapters, headings or subheadings as single codes, lists or ranges. 0 rows were unreadable. 8 rows are left to hand encoding (`backend/internal/rcep/manual.go`): seven split the rule by what the product is (0304.39 and 0304.69 carp; 1601.00, 1602.10 and 1602.90 insects; 2404.19 tobacco substitutes; 2909.60 acetal and hemiacetal peroxides) and heading 38.08 adds "at least 50 % by weight of the active ingredient is originating". Loading fails if one of those rows' text changes, so a new table version cannot reuse a stale encoding. **Cross-check:** the ABF copy, parsed the same way, gives the same 2,452 rows with 0 code or rule differences and 1 description difference (a text-extraction space in 2921.51).
- **Engine (`backend/internal/rcep`).** Inputs: the good's HS code, where it is produced, FOB value and weight (optional), and each material's HS code, value, weight, country and status (`originating` only on a supplier's declaration or proof of origin; `non_originating`; `unknown`, the default). Implemented: Art. 3.2 (produced in a Party; wholly obtained on the producer's statement; produced only from originating materials; or the Annex 3A rule), Art. 3.4 cumulation (a declared-originating material from a non-Party counts as non-originating; work in another Party on a material that is not originating in its own right adds nothing, the ABF guide's partial-cumulation example), Art. 3.5 RVC by the build-down and build-up formulas with undetermined-origin materials as non-originating, Art. 3.6 minimal operations from the declared operations, Art. 3.7 de minimis (10 % of FOB value; also 10 % of weight for chapters 50 to 63). The rule is looked up at six digits (subheading, then heading, then chapter).
- **How it decides.** Yes if any alternative of the rule is met; no only when every alternative is definitely failed; otherwise undetermined, with the missing fact named. Missing facts never give no. RVC: yes if either formula reaches 40 %; no only when the build-down figure is complete and below 40 % and the build-up figure is absent or complete and below 40 %. Materials whose HS code is too short to test count as failing in the de minimis sum. A CR alternative and the 38.08 condition are met only on the user's statement. A row that splits by product needs a `variant`; without one the answer stands only if every branch agrees. When no operations are given, a yes says it assumes more than Art. 3.6 minimal operations.
- **Interpretations for the professional review.** (1) De minimis also covers a material that fails only because of an "except from" exclusion (Art. 3.7 says "did not undergo the applicable change in tariff classification"). (2) A good classified WO can still qualify under Art. 3.2(b) (the Annex 3A headnote, as quoted in the ABF guide). (3) A declaration of originating status is taken as given; the engine does not trace a supplier's own materials (Art. 3.12, and the tracing in the Australian RCEP regulations, section 5). (4) The ABF guide gives 2009.90 as "CTH or RVC40"; the Annex table says "CC or RVC40". The engine follows the table; the guide's fruit-juice answer is the same either way.
- **Not covered.** Art. 3.8 packaging, 3.9 accessories, 3.10 indirect materials, 3.11 fungible materials, 3.15 direct consignment, proof-of-origin procedures, Art. 2.6 tariff differentials (which Party's preferential rate applies), whether the Agreement is in force between the two Parties, and the HS 2028 transposition. These are stated in the package doc and the API description.
- **Kept apart from origin.** Own route (`POST /v1/rcep/check`, cheap class, no model call, nothing stored, no case data, no audit row), own MCP tool (`check_rcep_preference`, read-only), and its own fold on the origin step ("RCEP tariff · separate from origin"). Every result carries `regime: rcep_preferential` and a note: not marking origin, not a ruling or certificate, not reviewed by a customs professional. It changes no prediction, triage, plan or export. The scope document's unsupported list keeps preferential claims; the RCEP check is named there as a calculator only.
- **Tests.** 18 test functions in `backend/internal/rcep` (94.2 % of statements), including 13 subtests built on the worked examples of the ABF guide "Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) Rules of Origin" (as at 18 December 2024; pages 26 to 46): wheat and maize flour (CC, CC except from chapter 10), roasted coffee (RVC40 only; the guide gives the rule, the figures are ours), tropical fruit juice, build-up 45 % and build-down 50 %, benzene (CR), a leather jacket from originating materials only, the spice mix at 38.9 % (cinnamon ground in Vietnam, not originating) and 44.4 % (all work in Malaysia), de minimis by value (5 %) and by weight (4 %, chapter 55). Table tests per article, the parse coverage and every rule's criteria. API, MCP and frontend tests for the route, the tool and the panel.
- **Spend.** No model call. $0.

## D691 — Pre-registration: scoring the RCEP calculator on Japan Customs RCEP advance rulings (22 Nov, #662; follows D710)
Committed with D690, before any Japan Customs ruling has been run through the calculator. The engine under test is the one D690 commits (rule table `rcep-psr-hs2022-r2022-08-20`).
- **Data.** The Japan Customs advance rulings on origin snapshotted under D710, filtered to rulings whose agreement field (特恵種別) is RCEP (about 402 by a keyword count on 22 Nov; the exact count is taken from D710's `rulings.jsonl`). D710's split is used as is: development = issued before 2026-01-01, held-out = issued on or after 2026-01-01.
- **Inputs, fixed now.** Built only from the parsed structured fields: the good's HS code, the producing country, and each material's HS code and where it was made. No translation, no model and no reading of the reasoning (認定理由) goes into the inputs. A material is `originating` only if the ruling's materials list states it is originating; otherwise `unknown`. Values are rarely published, so no FOB or material values are invented: an RVC alternative will mostly be undetermined.
- **Measures.** (a) Outcome on positives: shares of yes, undetermined and no. Every published answer is positive (D710), so a no is an error against the label and a yes is recall; no figure measures refusals of goods that do not qualify. (b) Criterion agreement: the engine's deciding criterion (WO, PE, CC, CTH, CTSH, RVC) against the one D710's `labels.py` reads from the reasoning, on rulings with both. (c) Rule-row agreement where the reasoning names the Annex 3A rule. (d) Synthetic negatives, reported separately and never pooled with (a) to (c): for each ruling the engine answers yes through a tariff shift, the first non-originating material's HS code is replaced by the good's own heading, which must turn the answer to no or undetermined.
- **Protocol.** Development rulings first; any rule-table or engine change made after reading them is a new version and is scored on development only. The held-out RCEP rulings are scored once per version, logged in `eval/RESULTS.md` and RUNLOG, with every run disclosed. Wilson intervals on every share.
- **Expectation stated now.** On rulings whose reasoning cites CC, CTH or CTSH and whose materials have HS codes: at least 70 % yes, at most 10 % no, the rest undetermined; criterion agreement at least 80 % on those. On rulings citing RVC: mostly undetermined (no values published). Synthetic negatives: 100 % not yes.
- **Status.** The Japan corpus is not on `main` when this is committed (D710 is in progress), so no score is run here. The run is a follow-up on #662 once `data/jp` lands. No model calls are planned for it.

## D680 — Jurisdiction as a case field, a deterministic market detector and a registry of supported markets; pre-registration of the detector checks (22 Nov, #659)
Committed and pushed before the detector is written or scored.
- **Problem.** Nothing checked that a question is about U.S. entry (`docs/scope-and-jurisdiction.md` section 3). A question about EU, UK or other entry got a U.S. answer, and the router's `unclear` label was treated as in scope.
- **Decision.** Every case gets `jurisdiction` (us, eu, uk, ca, jp, kr, au, mx, other). It comes from the caller's choice when given; otherwise from a deterministic detector over the facts (named authority or law, "imported into <place>", destination city, currency); with no cue it is `us`, as before. No new model call. Supported markets come from a registry (market → engine, rules, precedent pool); only `us` is registered. A case for a market with no registered engine gets no prediction and goes to review with "Origin rules for <market> aren't supported yet"; no engine is called, so no U.S. answer is shown as theirs. A non-U.S. cue that is weak (currency only) or contradicted by a U.S. cue sends the case to review when the router says `unclear` (weak) or always (contradicted).
- **Probe sets, frozen now (synthetic, illustrative, not customer text).** `eval/jurisdiction/probes-hand.jsonl` (sha256 `beebd26d…bdc0`): 30 non-U.S. questions (eu 6, uk 4, ca 4, jp 3, kr 3, au 3, mx 3, other 4) and 10 U.S. controls, written by the author of the detector before the detector existed. `eval/jurisdiction/probes-model.jsonl` (sha256 `85b97d57…5e91`): 30 non-U.S. questions in the same mix written by gemini-3.8-flash from a fixed prompt (`gen_probes.py`, $0.0421 gateway-reported), saved without being read, so they are independent of the detector's wording.
- **Checks.** (1) Development rulings of every regime (general 469, textile, Part 102 and pharmaceutical development lists): every one should stay `us`. The detector may be adjusted on these until it does; each adjustment is listed. (2) Then, once, with the detector frozen: the first held-out split (377), expected all `us`; the hand set; the model set. Per set: exact market, and non-U.S. recognised as non-U.S. (the safety figure: any non-U.S. market, a contradicted cue, or a weak cue all keep the case from a U.S. auto-answer). Controls: how many stay `us` with no review flag.
- **Expectation stated now.** Development and held-out: 0 flagged. Hand set: at least 26 of 30 exact, at least 28 of 30 kept from a U.S. auto-answer, 10 of 10 controls `us`. Model set: at least 22 of 30 exact, at least 25 of 30 kept from a U.S. auto-answer. The hand figure is not independent (same author); the model figure is the one to quote.
- **Not done here.** No non-U.S. engine, rule set or precedent pool; that is J3. No legal review.

## D681 — market-detect-v1 results; pre-registration of market-detect-v2 and a second model-written probe set (22 Nov, results of D680)
Run as D680 says (D680 pushed as c000fafd at 19:44 +08:00; detector frozen and pushed as 400f0758 at 19:52, before the held-out and probe runs). No model calls in the runs; `cd backend && go run ./cmd/eval market -set <set>`.
- **Development adjustments (allowed by D680, all before the freeze).** The first draft flagged 30 of 649 development rulings, almost all "imported into Thailand for further processing": in a CBP ruling's facts the parts often enter a third country on the way. Changes: an entry cue is dropped when the next words say work is done there ("for further processing", "where", "to be assembled"), when it follows "once", "after" or "initially", or when the text says work is done in that place elsewhere; "shipped", "exported" or "sold" to a non-U.S. place became a weak cue (a hint only); a currency code needs an amount or "in" beside it ("CAD drawings"); "<adjective> customs declaration" is the export side; authority cues decide before entry cues, and among entry cues the last one in the text decides. Result: 0 of 649 flagged; 71 carry a weak hint, none of which the router (router-v4, recorded rows `route-dev-router-v4-gemini-3.8-flash-litellm.jsonl`) labelled `unclear`, so no development case changes route.
- **Results, market-detect-v1** (`eval/results/market-detect-*-d680.json`):

  | Set | Texts | Exact market | Kept from a U.S. auto-answer | U.S. texts flagged |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | Development rulings, all regimes (tuned on) | 649 U.S. | | | 0 |
  | First held-out split (once) | 377 U.S. | | | **3** (detected as South Korea); 6 weak hints, none labelled `unclear` by router-v4 |
  | Hand probe set (same author, not independent) | 30 non-U.S. + 10 U.S. | 30 of 30 | 30 of 30 | 0 of 10 |
  | Model probe set 1 (independent) | 30 non-U.S. | **16 of 30** | 20 of 30 (16 without the router) | |

- **Against the expectation.** Held-out: 3 flagged, not 0. All three are processing stops the stop words missed ("imported to South Korea for drying", "Also in Korea, …", aluminium "imported into South Korea in ingot block form" and machined there). Model set 1: 16 exact and 20 kept, under the 22 and 25 expected. All 14 misses fall to the United States: the text named entry in ways v1 does not read ("brings … into Germany", "entering Spain via Valencia", "clearing customs in Antwerp", "landing stock in London", "customs entries arriving in Manchester") or named a national agency not on the list (Agencia Tributaria, Agenzia delle Dogane, South African Revenue Service, Ley Aduanera). Reading: v1 misses about half of naturally worded non-U.S. questions, and when it misses the case is treated as U.S., as before D680. The explicit market choice is the reliable path; the detector is a safety net.
- **market-detect-v2, written after reading the v1 errors above (held-out and model set 1).** (1) Entry cues also for "bring(s) … into", "entering <place>", "landing … in <place>", "arriving in <place>", "clearing (…) customs in/at <place>", "customs (port) in/at <place>", "the port of <place>". (2) More authority cues: EU member-state customs agencies (Agencia Tributaria, Agenzia delle Dogane, douane, Zoll), "Common Customs Tariff", "single market", "EU … customs union"; Ley Aduanera; the South African Revenue Service. (3) Stops: any "for <verb>ing" after the place, and "in <place>," anywhere in the text. (4) More port cities.
- **Probe set 2, frozen now.** `eval/jurisdiction/probes-model-2.jsonl` (sha256 `f6b52590…2df8`), 30 non-U.S. questions in the D680 mix from the same prompt plus a "set 2: different products, countries and wording" line (the gateway returned set 1 unchanged without it); $0.0398 gateway-reported; saved without being read.
- **Checks, each run once.** v1 and v2 on probe set 2; v2 on the held-out split; v2 on development (must stay 0 flagged; it may be adjusted on development only), hand set and model set 1 (shown, not independent: set 1 was read to write v2).
- **Adoption rule.** Production uses v2 if: development 0 flagged, held-out flagged at most 3 (v1), and on probe set 2 v2's exact count is above v1's. Otherwise v1 stays. Expectation: v2 at least 22 of 30 exact on set 2, v1 about 16.
