## D785 — Family-check run on development rulings for #772, main's templates against #772's, pre-registered (24 Nov)
Committed and pushed before either run. Budget: up to $100 for this lane, granted by the user for this run.
- **Runs.** Two, on the development split only (469 rulings); the held-out split is not run (no `-confirm-final`). Same model and settings as the committed 26-template development run (`families-coverage-dev-all-litellm-f26`): `family-check-v1`, gemini-3.8-flash, match bar 0.6, 6 workers, subject plus the first 1,500 characters of the facts, through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini, with `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1` so neither run reads cached answers. **Baseline** `-tag f26-b2-base`: main's code and templates at `1c1a63f0` plus the familycov commit below, so no guard and version 1 templates. **#772** `-tag f26-b2`: this branch, version 2 templates and `family-guard-v1`. `familycov` now records each check's latency and scrubs the gateway's address from error text (b4b4f1ca); nothing else in the command changes.
- **Measured (`eval/families/familycov_b2.py`, written now, writes `b2-familycov.json`).** Per run, with Wilson 95% intervals; a failed check counts as no match:
  - D781's frozen development cases matched to their family's template: batteries (7) → `power_supplies_chargers`, machinery (11) → `motors_pumps_compressors`, furniture (1) → `furniture`, medical (10) → `medical_devices`, optical (2) → `display_camera_modules`.
  - Look-alikes: the development rulings the D781 screen marked ambiguous (33 distinct), right when not matched to the family they share a cue with.
  - All 469: matched to any template; on rulings both runs answered, gained, lost and moved.
  - The guard: rows of the #772 run whose match it took away, each with the model's family, the rule and the baseline family, read by hand.
  - Cost (token-priced at promo rates, gateway-reported where available) and p50/p95 latency per run.
- **Expectation stated now.** The baseline should land near the committed f26 run (349 of 469); #772 within a few rulings of it. Batteries should mostly match the renamed template in both runs (the power-supply template already took power banks); the guard should take away few matches (1 of 349 on the recorded run, D784). No claim of accuracy follows from either run: matching is template scope.

## D786 — Review fixes to the guard and two notes before the #772 family-check run; D785 amended (24 Nov)
An independent review of fd4b2478 found the D783 guard rejecting genuine battery products. Fixed here, committed and pushed before the `f26-b2` run, which had not been run. The baseline run (`f26-b2-base`, main's code, no guard) had already finished when this was written; its summary line (350 of 465 answered checks matched, 4 failed) was seen, and none of D785's per-family figures had been computed.
- **Guard, now `family-guard-v2`.** (1) The product word skips words with digits and unit words (`12V 100Ah`, `10000mAh`), stops before "in" clauses ("… packs in Vietnam"), and battery products now include boards, backups and UPS units. (2) The guard reads only the "Typed:", "Product name:" and "Product:" lines and the model's product name; a parts list never names the product, and with no such line it does nothing (an import with only "Parts: housing, lithium cells, BMS board" was wrongly refused). (3) The pet rule fires only when a pet word is right before the product word, or the product is a bed, house, tree, crate or kennel with a pet word ("pet-friendly sofa" now passes). (4) The toy rule fires only on "toy" or "novelty" (a children's thermometer, a kids' nebulizer and a plug-and-play camera module now pass). (5) Gel is no longer a drug word (ultrasound gel), trucks and carts are no longer vehicles (a hydraulic pallet truck or forklift is a machine), and the hand-tool rule spares industrial and commercial goods (an industrial blender). (6) A guarded answer has confidence 0 and a plain reason naming the family's display name ("Not planned as Furniture and mattresses: a lamp or light fitting is lighting, not furniture."); the model's family, reason and the rule are kept off the API response and logged with the guard version (`httpapi/family.go`). All of these are in `guard_test.go`, the parts-only path included. With v2 the recorded development rows still change in 1 of 349 matches (the pet bed); the v1 file is kept in the proof directory.
- **`familycov`** records, per row, the model's family and the rule when the guard took a match away, and the guard version in RUNLOG (`model_family`, `guard_rule`, `guard_version`).
- **Template notes.** N348871: the portable power station's origin followed where its PCBAs were made across the four scenarios, with Chinese batteries in all; CBP did not rank the parts. N333849: France assembled the generator's rotor and stator into drivetrain subassemblies made in China, and CBP weighed the French work collectively. D782's wording of both is superseded by this.
- **Citations.** N361712 (dated 2026, cited by version 1) is no longer cited in the new sterile packing group: D780's pool stops before 2026. `depth_b2.py check` now checks every group/outcome pairing new in version 2, new or reused rulings (17), not only new rulings; H322967 is the one reused pairing and is recorded. N349313's pairings are unchanged from version 1.
- **Counts restated (D784).** After N354279 moved, furniture has 10 pool and 1 development ruling kept and 5 ambiguous; M1's furniture line is 0 → 0 of 1.
- **D785 amended.** The #772 run (`-tag f26-b2`, not yet run) uses `family-guard-v2`; guarded rows are read from `guard_rule`. Everything else in D785 stands.

## D787 — Development family-check run for #772: results of D785 as amended by D786 (24 Nov)
Run once each, development split only (no held-out split), through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini with the gateway cache off. Baseline `families-coverage-dev-all-litellm-f26-b2-base` (main's code and templates plus the familycov commit, revision 25af1566, never pushed: main 1c1a63f0 with b4b4f1ca cherry-picked); #772 `families-coverage-dev-all-litellm-f26-b2` (revision 10691215, `family-guard-v2`). Machinery (motors, pumps, compressors and machines) 7 → 7 of 11 (64%, 35–85); the other four go to the Part 102 machinery parts template in both runs. Medical 9 → 9 of 10 (90%, 60–98; the electrosurgical return electrode is "none" in both). Optical (displays, cameras and lenses) 0 → **1 of 2** (0%, 0–66 → 50%, 9–91): the optical window now matches; the sight carrier plate stays "none". Furniture 1 → 1 of 1.

The vein finder failed in the #772 run and so counts as right; on answered checks only, 31 of 32 in both runs.

On the 456 both runs answered, 343 → 345: gained 5 (the two cells, the optical window, an oil filter to vehicle parts, and a laser marking and engraving machine to motors and machines), lost 3 (the pet bed, by the guard; a microwave hood combination and a thermal print head, both to "none" at 0.85 with no guard involved), moved 1 (the 3D printer). The two non-guard losses and the oil-filter gain look like run-to-run variation; no repeat was run.

## D788 — The guard's rule is not logged by the HTTP route (24 Nov, follow-up to D786)
D786 logged the guard's rule, version and the model's family from `POST /v1/products/family-check`. The log-safety allowlist (`internal/logsafe`) admits only known messages and closed-value keys, and `TestASTGuardRealPackages` rejected the new message. Rather than widen that allowlist in this PR, the route logs nothing new: the model's family, reason and the rule stay on the check result (`ModelFamily`, `ModelReason`, `GuardRule`, kept out of the JSON), and `familycov` records them per row with `guard_version` in RUNLOG. A log line can follow with an allowlist change reviewed on its own.

## D789 — Guard v3: the product word is the rule's own known word, before any clause; a new #772 run pre-registered (24 Nov, re-review of d61a1069)
Committed and pushed before the new run. The `f26-b2` run (D787) measured `family-guard-v2` and is **superseded**; its files and RUNLOG row stay as they are.
- **Problem.** Guard v2 still read a word after the product as the product: it cut at " in " before " made ", so "Lithium battery made in Vietnam" read "made", and "Battery pack imported from China", "Battery pack that we assemble in Mexico", "Lithium battery 12V 100Ah deep cycle" and "Lithium battery storage cabinet" were refused as battery-powered devices; "Floor lamp made in China" and "Pet bed made in Vietnam" slipped through.
- **Rule (`family-guard-v3`).** A phrase is cut at a comma or bracket, read after the last "of", and stopped at the first clause word (for, with, from, in, made, assembled, manufactured, produced, imported, sold, sell, that, which, we, by, to, at, using); words with digits and unit or chemistry words (V, Ah, volt, amp, hour, LFP, SLA…) are dropped. Each rule then takes as the product the **last word it knows** (its own vocabulary, singular, a hyphenated word also by its last part), not the last word of the phrase; with no known word it does nothing. Battery products now include assembly, circuit, protection, cabinet and rack ("battery protection circuit", "battery pack assembly"). The drug rule fires on words that name a drug on their own (supplement, vitamin, pill, ointment…) and on dosage forms (tablet, capsule, cream) only with drug context (pills, dosage, mg, supplement, vitamin, pharmaceutical, drug, medicine) and never next to android, medical, computer, display, endoscopy, camera or coffee; "Ibuprofen tablets" with no context is now left to the model. The pet rule ignores "pet-friendly" and "dog-proof". The hand-tool rule also spares floor, pneumatic, hydraulic, rock, ride-on, riding, stationary, bench and press machines (a floor sander, a rock drill, a ride-on mower); a walk-behind mower is still refused from industrial machines. Every case from the re-review is in `guard_test.go`. The recorded development rows still change in 1 of 349 matches (the pet bed).
- **Wording fix.** D788 and the PR body said `familycov` records the model's reason; it did not. It now does (`model_reason`), with `model_family` and `guard_rule`.
- **Baseline revision.** 25af1566 (main 1c1a63f0 with b4b4f1ca cherry-picked) was not pushed; the commit is identical to main plus a commit on this branch. D787's disclosure stands, and the baseline run `f26-b2-base` is reused unchanged.
- **Run, pre-registered.** One `familycov` run of this branch (version 2 templates, `family-guard-v3`), development split only (no `-confirm-final`), `-tag f26-b2-g3`, same model and settings as D785 (gemini-3.8-flash, `family-check-v1`, bar 0.6, 6 workers, gateway cache off), through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini. Measured by `eval/families/familycov_b2.py` exactly as D785 (now also writing `b2-familycov-g3.json` against the same baseline): frozen cases per family with Wilson intervals, the 33 look-alikes, all 469 with gained, lost and moved, the guard's removals, cost and p50/p95 latency. Expectation: within run-to-run variation of D787's figures; the guard takes away at most the pet bed among recorded development matches.

## D800 — EU and UK intake: missing information is asked, with the document that settles it (24 Nov, #770)
- **What is asked.** Every need of the EU or UK check now names the document or input that would settle it (`need.evidence`, `nporigin.EvidenceFor`): a row choice, "the product specification or catalogue description"; a value share, "the supplier's bill of materials with values, and the good's ex-works price"; a weight share, the bill of materials with net weights; a process or condition fact, "a production record from the plant showing where this work was done" (the formula sheet for a mixture, a production record for goods made from blanks); a material code, "the HS code on the supplier's invoice or the supplier's declaration"; a material origin, the supplier's declaration or certificate of origin. The wording reads only the need's kind and key, so the API, the MCP text ("settled by: ...") and the page say the same.
- **Controls.** On the origin page of an EU or UK case, and on the EU and UK cards of All checks for any case, each such need is asked in place: a choice for a row, yes or no for a fact, a percentage for a share, a code or a country for a part that lacks one. "Re-check" saves the answers and re-runs the check on the committed tables, and the next missing fact, if any, is asked. A chain on the real EU table: a radio of 8527 from a Chinese tuner of 8529 asks the tuner's value share (10% tolerance), then the chapter rule for goods made from blanks, then the case's value share (residual rule by value), then decides China. A UK pair of trainers (6404) from Vietnamese uppers asks whether the work is more than assembling uppers onto soles and decides Cambodia on yes. A shirt of 6205 asks which split it is.
- **Never fake.** The controls only send what the committed rules ask: answer keys the rules read (`ValidAnswer`), rows the table has (`ValidRow`), parts that exist, codes that fill or lengthen, shares that add up to at most 1. Anything else is a 400; the tests run against `euorigin.Rules()` and `ukorigin.Rules()` only, no injected table.
- **Canada.** The Canada guidance (D735) is unchanged and not duplicated: the EU and UK engines share `tariffshift` only for code ranges, not its `Guide`. The evidence report reuses `tariffshift.Guide` as it is for Canada's missing facts and only adds the same evidence wording.

## D801 — Supplied answers are kept per case, beside the product, attributed and timestamped (24 Nov, #770)
- **Choice.** Answers are saved on the case (`origin_facts` by market), not kept in the browser: the evidence report, the MCP tool and a reload must see what the check read, and a reviewer must see who supplied it and when. Client-side answers would vanish on reload and make the report disagree with the page.
- **Never the product.** They are check inputs only, in their own record (`domain.SuppliedOriginFacts`: `source` "user-supplied", `updated_at`, the signed-in `actor` when there is one). The case's facts text and product are never changed; tests compare them before and after.
- **Tied to the part.** A part fact names the part's name and code as they stood. When the parts list changes so they no longer match, the fact is not read and the answer says so (`stale_supplied`); a code may only fill a missing part code or lengthen the part's own, an origin only fill a missing one, and a good code only lengthen the product's.
- **Route.** `PUT /v1/cases/{id}/origin-facts/{market}` (market eu or uk) replaces the market's answers (an empty body clears them), records an `origin_facts` event, and answers with the check re-run. Editor permission (viewers 403), a pinned demo is read-only (403), audited as a case update, rate class basic, no model call. `POST /v1/rules/{eu,uk}-origin` takes the same answers as `supplied` beside a `product`, so the page reads them statelessly.
- **Not changed.** An EU or UK case's stored prediction (made from its codes at predict time) is not re-run when answers are saved; the origin page and All checks show the check with the answers.

## D802 — Missing information versus a rule that is not modelled (24 Nov, #770)
- **Missing information** (`status` undetermined; report `needs_information`): the check can decide once a listed fact is supplied. Labelled "Missing information" and asked.
- **Rule not modelled** (`needs_judgement`, and `review` needs): the good has no list rule, so its origin is the last substantial, economically justified processing (Art. 60(2) UCC; TCTA 2018 s. 17(3)), or a rule is written by description a person has to read. Labelled "Rule not modelled", with the plain reason and the article. No control is rendered for it, on the page or in the report; a need that belongs on the product itself (where it is made, the parts list) links to the product instead.
- **Families.** The deepened product families (#766-#769) merged with #772 (D780-D790). Their intake (family questions through clarify-v2, `POST /v1/cases/{id}/answers`, with document names) follows in a separate PR; it is not part of this one.

## D803 — All checks on one product, each on its own (24 Nov, #771)
- **What runs.** `GET /v1/cases/{id}/evidence-report` runs, on the case's product as stored: the 19 CFR 102.20 tariff shift; Canada's marking rules (SOR/94-23); EU and UK non-preferential origin, with the answers supplied to them (D801); RCEP preference; and the USMCA selected-rule check for the pilot goods. The U.S. country of origin (CBP substantial transformation) is the case's stored model answer, reused, never re-run; on a case for another market it is "not run" and says a U.S. case would need a model call. No model is called. Japan is not included: its engine is configured per market and is out of scope here.
- **Each card.** The legal question it answers, its status (answered, missing information, rule not modelled, not run, not covered), its outcome, the missing facts with the document that settles each, what a person decides, its sources, its rule or data version, its limits, its standing label (rules-only markets: always "needs review") and when it was made.
- **Never one verdict.** No overall line, verdict or score, on the API, in Markdown or on the page; the report says the checks answer different legal questions. Tests assert there is no `overall`, `verdict` or `score`.
- **Inputs a check lacks.** RCEP and USMCA read only the codes and countries on the case; originating status, values and the scope confirmations are not on the case, so every part is "unknown". An RCEP "no" from codes alone is reported as missing information, not as a finding; a USMCA good outside the pilot rows is "not covered".

## D804 — The evidence report document (24 Nov, #771)
- **Markdown**, in the API answer and as the download: generation time, the case's created and updated times, the separate-questions and not-a-ruling statements, a list of each check's outcome (no combination), one section per check, the case's facts and product exactly as stored (facts text in a fenced block, parts as a table), and the supplied answers in their own section with their source and time. Stored values are kept on one line or in their block, so a value cannot start a heading.
- **Print**: the All checks page prints with every fold open. The CBP ruling-request export (`POST /v1/cases/{id}/export`, letters, reviewer notes) is unchanged; reviewer notes stay beside letters, and the evidence report is a separate document.
- **Read only**: nothing is stored and no event is recorded; viewers may read it.

## D805 — Where it lives (24 Nov, #771)
- **Page**: `/cases/{id}/checks`, an optional "All checks" step tab on every case (rules checks only, so every market has it), linked from the origin page. The legacy plan, compare and scenarios goldens were re-captured once for the added tab.
- **MCP**: `get_evidence_report` (read-only, always listed), the report's Markdown as its text. `check_eu_origin` and `check_uk_origin` name what settles each need.

## D806 — Review fixes: supplied answers never break a check; report escaping; access (24 Nov, #770, #771)
- **Read leniently, save strictly.** Saved answers are validated strictly only when saved (`PUT /v1/cases/{id}/origin-facts/{market}`). On every read path (the stateless routes with `supplied`, the case answer, the evidence report) answers that no longer fit are left out and named, never a 400: a removed part, a part whose name or code changed, or a part that now has an origin or a code the answer no longer lengthens (`stale_supplied`); a good code that no longer lengthens the product's, a row or an answer key the rules no longer have (`supplied_dropped`). Before this, a parts change made the page show only an error with no way back.
- **A replaced parts list.** Row and yes/no answers do not name a part, so when a `bom_updated` event is newer than the answers' `updated_at`, the whole set is stale: it is marked on read (`origin_facts.<market>.stale`, never stored), none of it is read (`supplied_stale`), the page and the report say "answer again", and the page does not resend it.
- **Concurrency.** PUT takes `expected_updated_at` (the answers' `updated_at` as the page read them, "" for none) and answers 409 when they changed since. The handler builds a new map instead of writing into the stored one, and the in-memory store clones the answers on Get, List and Update (a concurrent save and report test runs under `-race`). A market whose rules are not loaded answers 400 saying so.
- **Report text.** Stored text in the Markdown report (names, codes, countries, supplied values, reasons) is escaped: `&`, `<` and `>` as entities, Markdown specials with a backslash, so a part named `<script>`, `**x**` or `[x](javascript:...)` is shown, not rendered. The facts text stays byte for byte in a fence longer than any backtick run in it; the report says the product fields are shown one per line, escaped.
- **More documents.** The U.S. tariff-shift card carries its `tariffshift.Guide` missing facts, like Canada's; RCEP part failures and USMCA missing facts name their documents; `material_code` has its evidence wording.
- **Page.** All checks lists the answers given (with who supplied them, when, and a stale mark) beside the case facts, and prints every fold open (`beforeprint`). An invalid field is described by its own message and the "fix the fields" line is an alert; after Re-check, focus moves to the next question or the outcome, which is a polite live region.

## D807 — Japan development candidate: AJCEP general originating criteria and rule-availability diagnostics (24 Nov, refs #694)
A new development-only candidate, separate from the D741 engine. The AJCEP schedule (Annex 2) lists only selected goods, so a code with no Annex 2 row had no rule to retrieve. This adds the main agreement's general originating criteria as a separate embedded bundle: Articles 24-30 and the selected Articles 32-35, plus the Annex 3 text.
- **Scope.** The bundle applies only inside the embedded HS2017 window, 2023-01-01 up to but excluding 2027-02-15, and only when no Annex 2 row applies. A matched row keeps its own evidence. Chapters 50-63 are excluded. Withheld, broad, malformed and invalid codes never fall through to it. Other agreements and the future AJCEP edition are unchanged.
- **Caveats carried in the evidence.** Annex 3 concerns ITA-covered materials only, and its attachments are not embedded, so that status is never assumed. Direct consignment and certification are unverified. The bundle states originating criteria, not full preference entitlement.
- **Tooling.** Lookup now returns a detailed reason, shared with the request preflight, and `jpeval diagnose` reports rule availability by reason and agreement. It runs on `dev_eval` or `dev` only, makes no model call and loads no gateway.
- **Rule-availability counts (native, offline; not accuracy, recall or decisions).** `dev_eval`, 400 cases: eligible requests 365 → 366, abstaining 35 → 34; the one added case is AJCEP under the general rule. Full `dev`, 2,973 cases (400 overlap `dev_eval`): 2,573 callable on an Annex 2 or other schedule row plus 16 on the general rule, 2,589 callable, 384 abstaining before a request. The 16 added are AJCEP cases only. Most remaining abstentions are unsupported agreements (GSP, JP-US TA) or codes with no row in the other agreements' schedules.
- **Status.** This is a new candidate. The `jp-engine-v1` source pin, D741 and D742 results and their artifacts are untouched, and the old runs are not re-executed. Any later model evaluation needs a new pre-registered protocol, fresh data and an explicit budget. Japan remains unavailable publicly and the professional review (#665/#694) is unchanged.

## D810 — Family questions: fixed, from the templates' cited rulings, no model (24 Nov, #770)
- **What is asked.** For the five families deepened in #772 (power supplies, chargers and battery packs; motors, pumps, compressors and industrial machines; furniture; medical devices; displays, cameras and lenses), `clarify.Intake` (`clarify-family-v1`) asks where the part or step a template group covers was made, or whether a step was done: where the cells were made and whether the pack's work is only welding the cells and fitting the BMS; where the BMS or main board was made; where the machine's working unit was made versus its frame and tooling, and the motor, impeller and housing for pumps and compressors; where panels were cut and edged versus where the piece was upholstered, and whether it is sold as a knock-down kit; where cannula tubing or metal blanks, moulded parts, and boards and sensors were made, and whether the last country only sterilises and packs; where lenses were ground versus only polished or coated, and where the camera board or display cell was made. 22 questions, each naming the document that settles it (bill of materials with origins, a supplier's or maker's certificate of origin, a production routing or traveller, a process sheet, a packing list).
- **Grounded.** Each question names template groups; the rulings it shows are those groups' `confers_origin` and `not_enough` citations, read from the template at run time, so it never cites a ruling the template does not. A test checks every group exists and every family's questions rest on at least one cited ruling.
- **Only what is missing.** A question is asked only when the product's text fits it (a plain charger is not asked about cells), and not when the parts list already says it: a part or step in the question's groups with a country, or, for a yes/no question, operations that name every step (`known`, shown, not asked). The parts list requires a "made in" for every part, so "Unknown", "TBD", "N/A", "various" and the like count as not stated: still asked.
- **No model.** The questions are fixed text and their selection is deterministic, so no model runs and no paid call is possible; clarify-v2's model-drafted questions are unchanged (they still run only inside predict and answers). Writing the questions with a model on the user's action was not needed.
- **Where.** `family_intake` on the case answer, only for a case of one of those families or with answers saved, so every other case reads byte for byte as before (the legacy goldens); the U.S. origin page shows it under the reasons.

## D811 — Family answers are kept apart, like the EU and UK answers; the /answers route is not used (24 Nov, #770)
- **Choice.** `POST /v1/cases/{id}/answers` appends answers to the facts text and re-predicts with a model; that would change the case's facts. Family answers use the #774 pattern instead (D801, D806): `PUT /v1/cases/{id}/family-facts` stores them on the case in their own record (`domain.SuppliedFamilyFacts`: source "user-supplied", `updated_at`, actor, the family and template version), never in the facts, product or parts list. Tests compare those before and after. It is the same pattern with its own record, not a third mechanism: same attribution, same `expected_updated_at` precondition (409), same staleness, same editor permission (viewers 403), read-only pinned demos, two-phase audit as a case update, rate class basic.
- **Strict on save.** Only questions the intake asks now (missing or answered); a question the parts list settles, an unknown id, a country on a yes/no question or the reverse, a country not in the picker's table (`domain.KnownCountry`, the keys of `frontend/src/lib/countries.ts`, a test keeps them equal; the European Union is not a country of manufacture), or "Unknown", "TBD" and the like, or any answer to a not-modelled intake is a 400.

## D812 — Stale family answers (24 Nov, #770)
- A `bom_updated` event newer than the answers, or a family that changed since, marks the whole set stale on read (never stored): none is read, the questions are asked again and the page says so. An answer whose question is no longer asked (the product changed, or the parts list now settles it) is left out and named (`dropped`). Never a 400 on read.

## D813 — Missing information versus not modelled, for families (24 Nov, #770)
- `status` is `missing_information` (questions open), `complete`, or `not_modelled` with a code and a plain reason, and no question: `market` (the templates cite CBP rulings, so only U.S. cases are asked), `no_family`, `unknown_family`, `no_questions` (a family with no questions yet), `no_product`, `guard` (`familycheck.Guard` v3, run on the product name, refuses the family: a cordless drill as a battery pack, a floor lamp or pet bed as furniture, toy binoculars as optics, a supplement as a device) and `no_match` (no question fits, e.g. "Widget assembly" as a machine). A not-modelled intake renders a reason and no control, and the API refuses answers to it. Tests cover each code, ambiguous and unsupported products first.

## D814 — The case list says what answers did (24 Nov, #770)
- The U.S. answer is a model answer; family answers do not re-run it (that would be a model call nobody asked for). Honest option: `answers_note: added` on the case list row when family answers or origin facts that are saved and read (not cleared, not stale) were saved after the newest stored prediction and did not re-run it ("Answers added. Open to see them."), and the origin page says the origin above was made before them. The evidence report lists family answers in their own section, apart from the facts; no check reads them.

## D815 — An EU or UK case's stored answer follows its latest check (24 Nov, #770; replaces D801's "Not changed")
- **Choice.** An EU or UK case's stored prediction is that market's rules check, which is deterministic and free. Keeping it stale after answers made the case list disagree with the page. Saving answers to the case's own market's check (`PUT .../origin-facts/{market}` where the case asks that market) now re-runs it with the saved answers and stores the result (`provider: rules`, the table version as prompt), records a `rechecked` event ("was X, now Y"), and keeps the stored answer from before the answers in `prediction_before_answers` (see D818). Clearing the answers re-runs it on the codes alone. Answers to another market's check (a U.S. case's EU answers) do not touch the stored answer; the list marks them `added`. The list shows `answers_note: rechecked` ("Re-checked with your answers") while answers are saved. The PUT answer carries the new `prediction`.

## D816 — MCP `save_case_answers` (24 Nov, #770)
- One write tool for both: `check` "eu" or "uk" calls `PUT /v1/cases/{id}/origin-facts/{market}`, `check` "family" calls `PUT /v1/cases/{id}/family-facts`, in process through the whole middleware chain, so validation, staleness, the precondition, roles, audit and isolation are the REST route's. Fields of the other kind are refused in the tool. Annotations: writes, idempotent, not destructive. docs/MCP.md, the OpenAPI document, the developers catalog, the MCP tool and principal tests, and the audit, roles and isolation tables list it and the new route.

## D817 — Review fixes to the family questions (24 Nov, #770, review of 1441ce51)
- **One group per question.** `pack_work` named two groups, so N346317, N346403 and N347193 showed as both "decided origin" and "not enough". Every question now asks about one template group and shows exactly that group's citations (a test compares them per question). `pack_work` is reworded to "Is the pack's work only welding the cells and fitting the BMS?" under `final_assembly`, where N347193 held pack welding and the BMS not enough. "Formation" is dropped from it: forming cells is a cell-making step (`battery_cells`, N347172) and `cells_made` asks where the cells were made.
- **Partly known stays open.** A country question is settled only when every part and step in its group names a country. One line blank or "Unknown" keeps it asked, with what the parts list says shown beside it ("China; 1 of 2 lines name no country").
- **Answers name a real country.** "Unknown", "TBD", "Mars" and the European Union are refused on save. The page's picker and check use the same table.
- **Smaller.** The intro now reads "The rulings cited turned on these facts." Facts are cut by runes, not bytes. `save_case_answers` is not marked idempotent. A clear says "Cleared". The U.S. not-re-run line appears only when answers were saved. `get_case` says how many family questions are open and to use `save_case_answers`.

## D818 — `prediction_before_answers` follows new predictions (24 Nov, #770, review of 1441ce51)
- D815 kept the first stored answer forever, so it outlived a parts-list change. On each re-check the kept prediction is taken from the newest stored prediction that was not itself a re-check, so a prediction stored since (predict, answers, a BOM update) replaces it. The field is shown only while the newest stored prediction is that re-check. Stores deep-copy it on every read. `answers_note` ignores cleared and stale answers.

## D819 — Japan is live on the production Vertex engine model (24 Nov, #694)
- **Choice.** `JAPAN_ENGINE` now defaults to on. With the Vertex provider and no `JAPAN_LITELLM_*` settings, Japan reuses the production engine model (the shared client, fallback, gate and spend meter) and `ENGINE_MODEL` as its model id. No new client is built and no gateway is assumed. If either `JAPAN_LITELLM_*` variable is set, the validated private LiteLLM path is kept unchanged. If no usable model exists, Japan stays unavailable. `JAPAN_ENGINE=off` disables it. The market picker follows the API's supported flag.
- **What this is not.** The D741 private results come from the LiteLLM route and are not evidence for this Vertex path. No accuracy is claimed for live Japan, and results are not a ruling or a specialist's review.

## D820 — Family follow-ups #777–#780: search universe, screens, template bar and frozen development cases, written before any count was taken with them (24 Nov)
Committed and pushed before the screens below were run and before any candidate was read. No model calls in D820–D839: every measurement is offline and deterministic; the family-check run on the new development set (#781) is left to the coordinator after merge.
- **What was known before this rule.** D780–D790's counts and frozen lists (`b2-hits.json`, `b2-screen.json`, `b2-cases.json`), and one universe size taken while writing this: 24 substantial-transformation rulings with facts, dated 2026 and in no held-out list, are in the bundled corpus (D780's universe stopped before 2026). No ruling's facts or holding had been read for this work.
- **Universe (`eval/families/depth_b3.py`).** D780's universe without its date cutoff: labelled substantial-transformation rulings (`eval/data/labels.jsonl`) with a facts file, in no `final`, `final2`, `pilot` or `tune_check` list of any split file (including `eval/splits/routed/`), and not among the ruling IDs of `labels_final2.jsonl`, `labels_usmca_final2.jsonl` or `facts_final2` (IDs only are read, to exclude them). Japan data (`data/jp`, `eval/jp`) is not read. Pools: **dev** (`splits_final.json` dev), **train** (`splits_tune.json` train), **other** (the rest, now with the non-held-out 2026 rulings). Templates cite train and other only; dev rulings are regression cases and are never cited.
- **Screens, one per scope, fixed in the script.** A ruling is a candidate when a keyword pattern matches its subject and the first 1,500 characters of its facts, or when it states an HTSUS heading of the scope (in `backend/data/hts_index.json` or written in the facts): **battery packs** (#777) 8506, 8507; **lifting and handling machines** (#778) 8425–8428, 8485 (additive manufacturing), with keywords for jacks, hoists, winches, cranes, forklifts, pallet trucks, lifts and 3D printers; **furniture** (#779) 9401, 9403, 9404, with D780's words plus upholstery, cushions, seats, knock-down, ready-to-assemble, flat-pack, unassembled, lacquer, varnish, stain and veneer; **optical and precision instruments** (#780) 9001–9005, 9011–9013, 9015–9017, 9024–9033, with keywords for lenses, scopes, binoculars, microscopes, sights, magnifiers, prisms, rangefinders, levels, calipers, micrometers, gauges, measuring, surveying and eyewear.
- **Hand screen (`eval/families/b3-screen.json`).** Every candidate's subject is read; facts and the held-origin sentence are read for every ruling that may be kept and every subject that does not settle it. A candidate D780 already screened keeps D780's reading unless this scope differs from D780's (lifting machines, the 3D printer, optical instruments apart from medical devices, upholstery, finishing and knock-down furniture), and then it is read again. Kept when the good whose origin CBP decides is in the scope: **battery packs** — cells, modules, packs, power banks, portable power stations, storage systems and battery management boards sold as such (not a device that runs on a battery, not battery materials); **lifting machines** — jacks, hoists, winches, cranes, lifts, forklifts, pallet trucks and other lifting or handling machines and their major subassemblies (not hand tools, not vehicles); **3D printers** are recorded apart as a look-alike of industrial machines; **furniture** — D780's scope (9401, 9403, 9404 goods and their structural parts), each kept ruling also tagged `upholstery`, `finishing` or `knock_down` when its holding turns on that work; **optical and precision instruments** — lenses, optical elements and assemblies, binoculars, telescopes, scopes and sights, microscopes, magnifiers, eyewear, and measuring, checking and surveying instruments (not medical devices, not cameras or displays, not toys). A screened-out candidate that is another product with a scope cue is `ambiguous` and becomes a routing test case. Each kept or ambiguous ruling records its reason in one line.
- **Template bar: D780's, unchanged.** A new template is written for a scope only if at least 10 kept pool (train + other) rulings are goods of the scope not already served by a dedicated template. As in D781, a ruling that a broader template cites in a group (the battery rulings in `power_supplies_chargers`, the lens rulings in `display_camera_modules`) counts, because no template is dedicated to it; a ruling a dedicated template already serves does not. Short of the bar, the work deepens the existing template's groups and the exact count gap is stated.
- **Citations.** A ruling is cited only when its held-origin sentence is in the bundled labels (`backend/data/labels.jsonl` evidence) and its facts say what was done where; each is recorded in `eval/families/b3-citations.json` with the held-origin sentence and the facts read, and `depth_b3.py check` fails on a new group/outcome pairing that is outside a frozen pool, has no held-origin sentence or is unrecorded. A new group, or a new operation in a group, needs at least one such ruling; a group lists rulings where the work was **not enough** wherever the pool has them. Templates keep fact-specific substantial-transformation precedent only: no tariff-shift, value-content or preference logic, no universal rule, and nothing that implies a regulatory approval.
- **Frozen development cases for family matching (`b3-cases.json`, `b3-dev-splits.json`).** Per scope, frozen with the date before any template is written from the screen: (a) dev-split rulings kept by the screen; (b) kept pool rulings that cannot be cited (no held-origin sentence, or facts that do not say what was done where); (c) where (a) and (b) give fewer than 5 cases, kept pool rulings whose only use would be one more citation for an outcome a group already cites, latest date first, until 5, and never one a template's bar depends on. (b) and (c) are never cited. D781's frozen dev cases stay as they are; the new file lists them with the additions. Ambiguous rulings in the dev split are the look-alike cases. The held-out comparison for #781 is the `final` list of `splits_final.json` as it stands, by ID only; nothing in it is read here.
- **Measurements, offline, no model calls.** M1 retrieval as D781 (production BM25, `engine.PrecedentText`, `retrieval.PrecedentFilter`, top 5 and top 20, a hit when a top-k ruling is cited by the scope's template) on the frozen development cases, templates before (main) and after; M2 the guard's tests and its effect on the 469 recorded development family checks, as D784; M3 planner fixtures through `TestFamilyFixturesPlan`; M4 citations and distinct rulings per template before and after. Not run: `familycov` or any held-out scoring (#781).

## D822 — Two new templates: lifting and handling machines, and optical and measuring instruments (24 Nov, #778, #780; from D821's lists)
Written from the frozen citable pools of D821 only; every citation recorded with its held-origin sentence and the facts read (`eval/families/b3-citations.json`, 20 group/outcome pairings; `depth_b3.py check` fails on any pairing outside the frozen pool, without a held-origin sentence or unrecorded, and on any template citing a frozen development case). Fact-specific substantial-transformation precedent only: no tariff-shift, value-content or preference logic, and no single part named as always deciding.
- **`lifting_handling_machines` v1, "Lifting and handling machines"** (11 rulings, 21 citations, 4 groups). **Lifting mechanism and hydraulic power unit** (movable): decided with the rest of the work for floor jacks whose power units were cast and machined in Vietnam or Thailand (N333646, N347256), an engine crane (N348514), a scissor jack (N348905), a guided vehicle with a Korean lift assembly (N343416) and a winch with a Thai motor and drum (N346297); a bottle jack stayed Chinese, where its castings and pump were made, though Thailand machined and assembled them (N344692); a Chinese lifting mechanism did not decide for two guided vehicles with Korean frames (N337718, N340047). **Frame, chassis, arms and boom** (movable): part of what decided for the jacks, crane and scissor lifts (N334276: platform and chassis in Poland); guided vehicles took the origin of the country that made their frames (N337718, N340047 Korea; N336445 China), and a Chinese drive chassis did not decide (N343416). **Drive, controls and electrical parts** (movable): adding drives, batteries, controllers and cabling in Korea was not enough (N336445). **Final assembly**: machining, welding, filling, painting and testing in Thailand (N344692), and wiring, software, calibration and testing in Korea (N336445), were not enough; knock-down packing is listed as a step. The note excludes hand tools, vehicles, stands and 3D printers.
- **`optical_precision_instruments` v1, "Optical and measuring instruments"** (9 rulings, 20 citations, 6 groups). **Lens and optical element shaping** (N342427, N345937 decided) and **lens polishing and coating** (N342427 not enough), the same holdings the display template cites for camera lenses. **Sensing element or measuring scale**: the sensing die or gauge wafer decided for pressure sensors (N349940, N358288), the sensing board for a gas sensor (N335170), the tape reel and blade for a digital tape measure (N344318), the engraved or stamped scale for a speed square (N347948). **Measuring electronics and display**: decided for a cooking thermometer (N335017), not enough for the tape measure, a gas chromatograph or pressure sensors (N344318, N340153, N358288). **Housing, body and blank**: not enough (N335170, N335017, N347948). **Final assembly**: decided once, for a gas chromatograph integrated, programmed and calibrated in Singapore (N340153); not enough for the gas sensor board, pressure sensors and the tape measure (N335170, N349940, N358288, N344318). The note says origin under these rulings says nothing about calibration standards, certification or regulatory approval, and that camera and display modules and medical devices stay with their templates. `display_camera_modules` is unchanged: its lens groups keep the two lens rulings for camera lenses.
- **Not changed.** `power_supplies_chargers` (no new battery ruling), `furniture` (no ruling supports an upholstery-only, finishing-only or knock-down group; N339090 is a development case under D820 (c)), `motors_pumps_compressors`, `medical_devices`, `display_camera_modules`. Their D782 citation check (`depth_b2.py check`) still passes unchanged.
- **Family count 28.** `TestTemplateSetIsPinned`, the union-default pin, the frontend picker mirror (`frontend/src/lib/families.ts`), the plan-scope line (`copy.ts`, re-captured in its golden in place, no markup change) and the docs say 28; `claimscheck` now flags "26 product families" and the like as stale, while dated figures read with 26 (D661) keep their count.

## D823 — Guard v4: printers, stands, lifting and optical look-alikes; two development fixtures (24 Nov, #778, #780)
- **`family-guard-v4`.** New rules: `printer` (motors and lifting templates: a printer, a 3D printer included, is not an industrial or lifting machine; "3D" is dropped as a word with a digit, so "3D printer" reads "printer"), `support-stand` (lifting: a stand or dolly holds a load, it does not lift it: jack stands, engine stands, wheel dollies), `toy-machine` (lifting), `lighting-optics` (a lamp, flashlight or light fitting is not an optical or measuring instrument), `network-optics` (fibre optic cables, patch cords and transceivers), `smart-eyewear` (smart glasses). The vehicle rule now also covers the lifting template and leaves an automated guided vehicle or mobile robot alone; the drug and toy rules also cover the optical template. Plurals in "-sses" read as "-ss" ("glasses" → "glass"). Each rule only takes a match away; none picks a family. `guard_test.go` adds 49 cases, unsupported and ambiguous products first (3D printers, jack stands, dollies, a toy crane, flashlights, fibre cables, transceivers, smart glasses, toy binoculars, a supplement) and each template's own goods kept (jacks, lifts, winches, an engine crane, guided vehicles, a telehandler, a pallet truck; lenses, sights, multimeters, pressure sensors, a gas chromatograph, a tape measure, a laser level, a light meter, reading glasses), plus the rules confined to their families.
- **The 3D printer stretch (#778).** On the recorded #772 run with guard v3 (`families-coverage-dev-all-litellm-f26-b2-g3.jsonl`) the new guard takes away exactly one match, the dental 3D printer H346536 that run matched to the machines template (`eval/families/b3-guard-g3.json`, `TestGuardOnG3Rows`). On the 469 recorded v1 checks it still changes only the pet bed (`b2-guard-dev.json`). The intake's machine questions no longer read "printer" as a machine (D824).
- **Fixtures (D820 M3, `backend/testdata/planner_families_b3/`, `eval/planner/build_b3_fixtures.py`, checked by `make reproduce`).** Written by the agent from the facts of two development rulings, no model draft, target by D171's rule: a low-profile floor jack (N354791, CBP held China; target Thailand, where it is finished) and a MEMS pressure sensor (N351865, held United Kingdom; reverse probe to China). Capabilities and costs are assumptions. Both run through `TestFamilyFixturesPlan` to a precedent-supported plan with the fake engine and verifier: a pipeline check, not plan quality.

## D824 — Family questions for the two new templates (`clarify-family-v2`, 24 Nov, #778, #780)
- **Lifting and handling machines.** Where was the lifting mechanism or hydraulic power unit made (production routing or traveller, or the supplier's certificate of origin; asked when the product names a jack, lift, hoist, winch, crane, forklift, stacker, telehandler, guided vehicle or pallet truck); where were the frame, chassis, arms or boom cut, formed and welded (bill of materials with origins, or the fabricator's invoice); is the last country's work only assembling, wiring, loading software and testing (process sheet).
- **Optical and measuring instruments.** Where were the lenses or optical elements cut and ground (process sheet for lens grinding, or the lens maker's certificate of origin); is the last country's work only polishing or coating them (process sheet); where was the sensing element or measuring scale made (bill of materials with the sensing element's origin, or the die or gauge maker's certificate of origin); where were the measuring boards populated (bill of materials with each board's origin); is the last country's work only assembling, calibrating and testing (process sheet). Each asked only when the product's text fits it.
- **Same rules as D810–D817.** One template group per question, showing exactly that group's citations (the grounding test now checks the version each family's questions were written for: 2 for the #772 families, 1 for the new ones); known from the parts list when every line of the group names a country; the guard refuses look-alikes before any question (`guard` code: a 3D printer as a machine or lifting machine, jack stands, a flashlight, fibre cables, smart glasses); `no_match` when no question fits. No universal rule and no regulatory-approval wording. The version is bumped because questions were added and "printer" no longer counts as a machine word.

An independent review of 76b78031 found that D821 counted rulings D820 excludes. That leaves the four jacks, the winch and the engine crane: 6. D821's "11 of 10" and D822's template were wrong.

The display template's two lens rulings count under D820's own example, since that template is not dedicated to standalone lenses. ## D840 — Is the family work working? Development and held-out family checks and origin accuracy per family, pre-registered (24 Nov, #781)
Committed and pushed before any run below and before any figure of them is computed. Main at e487e3dc (#782 merged: 27 families, `optical_precision_instruments` new, `offroad_vehicles_machinery` v2 with lifting groups, `family-guard-v5`, intake v2). The development families were chosen and their templates and guard tuned on these development cases (D780–D829), so the development figures are not independent; the held-out figures are.
- **Tooling, before any run.** `familycov` now writes each row as it finishes and takes `-resume`: rows already in the result file (failed checks included) are kept and never sent again, and an interrupted held-out run can only be continued with `-resume`, never started again; a dev result file that exists is refused without `-resume` or a new tag. Its RUNLOG row and `eval run`'s now record `dataset_sha256` (labels and splits files, and for `familycov` the SHA-256 of the exact case texts sent), `code_dirty` (tracked changes anywhere in the repository when the run starts), and for `familycov` `resumed`, `invocation_cost_usd`, `llm_no_cache` and `workers`. Template, guard and prompt code are unchanged. A two-ruling gateway smoke test of the resume path ($0.0109, two development-split rulings outside the #781 set, written only to the proof directory) checked it; it is not a measurement.
- **Model and settings, every family check.** `family-check-v1`, gemini-3.8-flash, match bar 0.6, 6 workers, subject plus the first 1,500 characters of the facts, through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini with `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`: as D785/D789, with main's 27 templates and `family-guard-v5`. Each run starts from a clean committed tree (`code_dirty` false); results are committed after each run, before the next.
- **Run 1, development (#781's frozen set).** From `backend/`: `go run ./cmd/eval familycov -split dev -splits ../eval/families/b3-781-run-splits.json -set all -tag f27-781`. `b3-781-run-splits.json` is the 48 cases and 30 look-alikes of `b3-dev-splits-a1.json` (D826), nothing else; 44 cases and all 30 look-alikes are in `splits_final.json` dev, 4 cases are pool rulings (D820 (b), (c)).
- **Run 2, held-out, once.** `go run ./cmd/eval familycov -split final -set all -confirm-final -tag f27-781` on `splits_final.json` `final` (377), after Run 1 is committed and with nothing changed since this commit except result files. Templates are frozen at this commit; nothing is tuned after it. If it stops partway, it is continued with `-resume` (finished rows are not re-sent) and that is disclosed.
- **Run 3, one engine case.** The official development engine run (`dev-gemini-4-argon-prec-engine-v1-vertex`, the development twin of the held-out run behind NUMBERS) already scored 44 of the 48 cases. Of the other 4, three have no CBP held-origin sentence (H338482, N335585, N348790) and cannot be scored; N339090 is run once: `go run ./cmd/eval run -split dev -splits ../eval/families/b3-781-pool-origin-splits.json -facts data/facts -tag 781pool` (production engine defaults: gemini-4-argon, `engine-v1`, BM25 k 5, no router), gateway, cache off. Disclosed: that one row is from the gateway, the 44 from Vertex on 15 Oct.
- **Cost estimate and stop rule.** Run 1 about $0.35 (78 checks), Run 2 about $1.2–1.7 (D661's 377 cost $1.17), Run 3 about $0.01: about $2 against about $95 left of the $100 lane cap. A run whose planned cost would take the lane past the cap is not started; each run's cost is added to the spend ledger.
- **Measured (`eval/families/measure_781.py`, written and pushed with this entry; writes `b3-781-measure.json`; no model calls).** Wilson 95% intervals throughout; a failed check counts as no match.
  1. **Development matching:** per expected template (batteries 7 → `power_supplies_chargers`, machinery 11 → `motors_pumps_compressors`, lifting 7 → `offroad_vehicles_machinery`, furniture 4, optical 9 → `optical_precision_instruments`, medical 10), matched/n; paired against D790's run (`f26-b2-g3`, 26 templates, guard v3, before #782) on the cases both runs answered, with the same expected template (so optical's "before" is 0 by construction: there was no optical template), gained, lost and an exact McNemar p. Look-alikes (30): right when not matched to a family their scope shares a cue with (D785's map; `optical_precision` → optical, `lifting_machines` → off-road).
  2. **Held-out matching:** matched/377 overall and the number and share of the 377 in each family. Held-out rulings carry no expected family, so this is scope (a template exists), not whether the match is right. Compared with D661's run (298/377, 26 families) on rulings both answered, gained/lost/moved and McNemar p, as a different setup (different templates and guard), not a controlled before/after.
  3. **Held-out origin accuracy per family:** the official held-out engine run (`final-gemini-4-argon-prec-engine-v1-vertex`, 340/377) re-sliced by the family each ruling falls in under Run 2 (the matched template, else "none"), and by HTS chapter (first code in `backend/data/hts_index.json`, else "unknown"). No new model calls; nothing held out is re-scored. Families or chapters with fewer than 10 rulings are pooled in the table and listed in the JSON.
  4. **Development origin accuracy per family:** the same slice of the 44 recorded rows plus N339090, per expected template.
- **What counts as correct.** Matching: the expected template at confidence ≥ 0.6. Origin: the engine row's `correct` against CBP's held origin, as scored when the run was made.
- **What counts as working or improved, stated before the results.** A development family is **working** when matched/n ≥ 80% and its Wilson lower bound ≥ 50%; look-alikes are working at ≥ 27 of 30. A family is **improved** over D790 only when the paired change is positive with McNemar p < 0.05; a positive change short of that is "better, not significant". The held-out run is **consistent with the family work helping** when it matches more than 298 and the paired change against D661 is positive with p < 0.05 — with the caveat that more matches is more scope, not more accuracy. Origin accuracy cannot show the family work improving anything: the engine does not read templates and the run is the same scored run; a family is flagged **weak** when its Wilson upper bound is below the overall 340/377 (90.2%).
- **Expectation stated now.** Development: batteries 6–7 of 7, machinery about 7 of 11 (four go to Part 102 machinery parts), lifting 5–7 of 7, furniture 2–4 of 4, optical 5–8 of 9, medical 9–10 of 10; look-alikes 27–30. Held-out: 295–310 of 377, with a few rulings moving to optical and off-road. Origin per family: near 90%, with no prediction which family is low.

## D841 — #781: three development cases Run 1 could not check; one supplementary run; a revision-suffix disclosure (24 Nov, amends D840)
Written after Run 1 and Run 2 finished, with only their printed summary lines seen (Run 1: 62 of 72 answered matched, 3 failed, 75 cases; Run 2: 302 of 372 answered matched, 5 failed) and before any per-case, per-family or origin figure was computed.
- **What happened.** Run 1 checked 75 of the 78 listed rulings, not 78. `familycov` reads rulings through the corpus store, which keeps only rulings with one held origin, and skipped the three frozen pool cases with no held-origin sentence (H338482 upholstered chairs, N335585 mattress, N348790 fibreglass measuring reel; D820 (b)) without a message. D840 did not foresee this.
- **Fix and supplementary run.** `familycov` now names every skipped ruling, and `-no-origin-ok` checks a listed ruling that has facts but no held origin, from its subject and facts exactly as any other check (the family check never reads the origin). One run, same model and settings as D840, from a clean tree: `go run ./cmd/eval familycov -split dev -splits ../eval/families/b3-781-noorigin-splits.json -set all -no-origin-ok -tag f27-781-noorigin` (3 checks, about $0.015). `measure_781.py` joins its three rows to Run 1's; no other change to the measurement. The held-out run is not repeated: no held-out ruling was skipped (377 rows).
- **Disclosure, Run 2's revision.** Run 2's RUNLOG row reads `code_dirty` false (taken at start, at b97de88f) but `git_revision` `b97de88f…-dirty`: the revision is read when the row is written, and the `-no-origin-ok` edit to `familycov.go` was made in the working tree at 18:06:47 while Run 2 (started 18:03:38, built from the clean tree) was running. The binary that ran was built before the edit; templates, guard and prompt were unchanged throughout. Nothing was tuned on Run 2.

## D850 — Machinery: the boundary between machines and machinery parts, and a development-only family check, pre-registered (25 Nov, #785, refs #767, #778)
Committed and pushed before the run below and before any figure from it. The fix is at f8abdfc5 (on main a34f8373). The family check sent only an id, a name and group names to the model. Four of D842's five machinery misses went to `machinery_parts`: N351234 hydraulic cylinders, N351538 impeller and diffuser, N354156 fluid ends and N354169 bearings. The fifth, N351349 water pumps, was a failed check. The recorded `model_reason` quotes the template's name and group: "precision mechanical subassemblies", "cast and machined components ... fitting the machinery_parts operation groups", "perfectly matching the operation groups for machinery parts and subassemblies", "precision-ground ... races". **Root cause:** "Machinery parts and subassemblies", with a group "Bodies, castings and precision-ground parts", reads as any machined or assembled component. The machines template's name ("Motors, pumps, compressors and industrial machines") does not say that it also covers pump working components, although its own rulings decide on them (N333514 impeller, N351810 fluid ends).
- **Fix (f8abdfc5).**
  - **Template `scope`.** An optional plain-words line says what a family covers and which family takes the rest. A test checks that it cites only rulings the template, or a family it names, already cites, and that every family it names exists. The planner does not read it.
    - `machinery_parts`: loose parts and castings imported for machines, such as bodies, housings, shafts, runners, valve bodies and valves, bearings and races, reducer casings and drill rods (N306640, N308442). Complete machines, motors, pumps, compressors, hydraulic cylinders and other working units go to the machines template, as do the impellers and diffusers (N333514) and fluid ends (N351810). Its air-cylinder citation (N303499) is a Part 102 tariff-shift holding for goods of Mexico.
    - `motors_pumps_compressors`: complete machines and working units, citing N346867, N340920, N349312 and N333849, plus the pump and compressor working components named above.
    - **Where these lines come from.** The bearings line follows `machinery_parts`' own operations (heading 8482 races and bearing assembly); the machines template cites no bearing ruling. The hydraulic-cylinder line follows HTSUS heading 8412, which names linear-acting hydraulic cylinders among engines and motors; no cited ruling is about a hydraulic cylinder.
    - No group, operation, citation, name, template version or match bar changes.
  - **`family-check-v2`.** The prompt shows a scope line under the family that has one, and one sentence telling the model to follow it. The other 25 templates' lines are unchanged.
  - **`family-guard-v6` adds `whole-machine`.** When the product word is a whole machine (machine, lathe, robot, pump, compressor, motor, engine, turbine, press, conveyor and the like), it takes a `machinery_parts` match away to review. A part word after it keeps the match ("pump housing", "motor shaft", "spare parts for compressors"). It never picks a family. Cylinders and valves are left out because `machinery_parts` cites both. On the recorded development rows (469 rows of `f26`, the `f26-b2-g3` rows) it changes nothing (`b2-guard-dev.json` and `b3-guard-g3.json` differ only in the version string and rule list).
- **Run, development only.** The held-out family check was spent in D842; no held-out ruling is read or sent. The model and settings are as D840 Run 1 and Run 1b: gemini-3.8-flash, match bar 0.6, 6 workers, subject plus the first 1,500 characters of the facts, through an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini with `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, 27 templates, from a clean committed tree. The prompt and guard are now v2 and v6; that is the change being measured. From `backend/`:
  - `go run ./cmd/eval familycov -split dev -splits ../eval/families/b3-781-run-splits.json -set all -tag f28-850` (the 48 cases and 30 look-alikes of `b3-dev-splits-a1.json`; 75 checks);
  - `go run ./cmd/eval familycov -split dev -splits ../eval/families/b3-781-noorigin-splits.json -set all -no-origin-ok -tag f28-850-noorigin` (the 3 cases with no held origin, as D841).
  - Cost about $0.34 against about $93 left in the lane. Each run is logged in the spend ledger. If a run stops partway, it is continued with `-resume` and that is disclosed. Nothing is re-run to get a better draw.
- **Measured (`eval/families/measure_850.py`, pushed with this entry; writes `b3-850-measure.json`; no model calls).** Per expected template, before (D842: `f27-781` plus `-noorigin`) and after, with Wilson 95% intervals. Paired gained and lost are counted on cases both runs answered, with an exact McNemar p. Also reported: look-alikes right, where each machinery case went and the model's reason, which rows went to `machinery_parts`, and what the guard removed. A failed check is not a match.
- **What counts as a fix, stated now.**
  - Machinery (`motors_pumps_compressors`) is **working by D840's rule**: at least 9 of 11, Wilson lower bound ≥ 50%.
  - At most one of the four `machinery_parts` misses stays with `machinery_parts`, and that one is only the bearings.
  - **No other family regresses:** no case matched in D842 loses its template, except as a failed check, which is disclosed.
  - Look-alikes stay at least 29 of 30.
  - **Partial:** machinery rises but stays under 9. **Not a fix:** machinery does not rise, or another family loses a case.
- **Expectation stated now.** The hydraulic cylinders, the impeller and diffuser and the fluid ends move to the machines template. The bearings stay with `machinery_parts`, as its operations name them, so the frozen label and the scope disagree on that case; the label is not changed. The water pumps match if the check answers. Machinery 9–10 of 11; the other families as D842.
- **Disclosure.** The fault was found, and the scopes and guard written, from these development cases and their recorded reasons. The result is a development figure, not an independent one.

## D852 — Machinery boundary, a second scope revision and one more development run, pre-registered (25 Nov, #785, after D851)
Committed and pushed before the run below. D851 found the machines scope too wide: two bottle jacks and a pool-cleaning robot moved to it. The revision is at 9b605066.

That sentence sends lifting machines (jacks, hoists, cranes, winches, lifts) to `offroad_vehicles_machinery` even with a hydraulic cylinder or pump inside (lifting moved there in D826). ## D854 — Review of #790: scope sources, wording fixes, the output cap, and one confirmation run, pre-registered (25 Nov, #785)
Committed and pushed before the run below. The review fixes are at e71aa708.

  - Under v1 the same case answered in 1,234 tokens (D842). The v2 prompt adds about 400 input tokens. The prompt length does not truncate anything; the output cap does.

  - `go run ./cmd/eval familycov -split dev -splits ../eval/families/b3-781-noorigin-splits.json -set all -no-origin-ok -tag f28-854-noorigin`

  - `measure_850.py . --tag f28-854` gives the table against D842 (`b3-854-measure.json`).
- **Criterion, stated now.** **No answered case regresses against D853.** A dev case matched to its expected template, or a look-alike kept off its cue family, in D853 must stay so in D854 wherever D854 answered it. A failed check is listed, not counted. If anything regresses, that is reported and nothing is tuned again.
- **Expectation.** Machinery 10 of 11. Fewer failed checks, with N350680 answering optical as in D842. No regressions.
