## D856 — U.S. origin accuracy on food and on rulings with no family template: miss table and one change, pre-registered (25 Nov, #815)
Committed and pushed before any run below. Held-out was spent in D842 and is not re-scored and not read for this work, so there is **no independent figure**; everything here is development, and the guidance below was written from development and training rulings (named below), so a development gain is not independent evidence either. Code at be17aac6 on main fb273279.
- **Slices.** D842 gives held-out origin accuracy by family: food 11 of 15, no template 62 of 75. For development the same rule (matched template at confidence 0.6 or more, else "none") is applied to the last family check that covers all 469 development rulings, `families-coverage-dev-all-litellm-f26-b2-g3` (26 templates; no 27-template run covers them all, so this differs from D842's held-out slice). Official development run of the production configuration (`dev-gemini-4-argon-prec-engine-v1-vertex`, gemini-4-argon, engine-v1, BM25 k 5, no router, 422 of 469): **food 16 of 20, none 103 of 118, other 303 of 331.**
- **Miss table** (`eval/accuracy/815-misses.json` and `.md`, from `diagnose_815.py`, no model calls, development rulings only). 19 misses: 4 food, 15 none. Cause, read from the ruling facts, CBP's held origin and the engine's answer and precedents: **rule applied 12** (food 3, none 9), **label or case ambiguous 6** (food 1, none 5; five of the six are answered correctly by another run of the same configuration), **retrieval 1** (none), **missed fact 0**. Food retrieval is not the cause: before the date of the four food misses the bundled corpus holds about 40 food rulings, and the retrieved five are the closest ones. The four food misses: pineapple and banana puree (N350517), razor clams (N352231), fish oil (N352389), chicken skewers (N354481).
- **Also found.** The engine answers China 92 times on development and is right 69 times; 23 of its 47 misses (11 of the 19 here) are China answers. The nine "rule applied" misses outside food are judgments about essential character and assembly in unrelated goods (filters, a lock, a showerhead, a tiara, a pen, borax, leather, a house kit, a spinel). rules-v1 and rules-v2 (D27, D157) already tried general guidance on those and did not move the total (422 of 469 both), so this entry does not repeat them. The largest cause that one change can reach is the food "rule applied" group.
- **Noise, measured on runs that exist.** Four runs of this configuration on the 469: 422, 422, 424, 425 right; food 15 to 16 of 20, none 103 to 105 of 118, other 303 to 305 of 331. A change of two or three rulings in a slice is within run to run variation.
- **The one change: `food-v1`.** `engine.FoodRules` (four short statements on food: preparing the same food keeps origin; a new food with a new name transforms; cooking or canning alone does not, a ready-to-eat dressed and fried or smoked product does; follow the closest precedent when they point both ways) is added to the system prompt of a case only when `engine.FoodCase` says the facts describe a food (one strong food word, or two different weak ones; deterministic, facts only). On development it names **19 rulings, all in the food slice (19 of the 20), none outside it**; 15 of the 19 are right in the official run, and the four misses are the four above. The other 450 development cases get a byte-identical prompt. The text was written from these rulings: development N350517, N352231, N352389, N354481 (the four misses) and training H326919 (tahini), N330420 (sunflower oil), N331014, N335413, N337385, N338956 (squid, scallops, octopus), N339749 (chargrilled chicken), N333864 (smoked salmon), N334669 (grilled salmon) and N345699 (fried chicken). It is **eval-only**: the `-food-rules` flag of `eval run`; the server does not use it, and nothing here changes production. Adopting it would be a separate decision.
- **Runs, gateway only** (an OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM gateway to Gemini; credentials in the environment; `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`; gemini-4-argon; each from a clean committed tree, results committed after each run and before the next). From `backend/`: **control** (same code, flag off, so the paired before is from the same gateway and day): `LLM_PROVIDER=litellm LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1 go run ./cmd/eval run -split dev -facts data/facts -tag 815-control`; **variant**: the same with `-food-rules -tag 815-food-v1`. Each is one run over the 469 development rulings, about $3.2. The control is not a second try; it is the before. A two-ruling smoke test of the flag (N352231, N350517; both answered right; $0.0149; written outside the repository) is not a measurement, and the text was written from those two.
- **Measured** (paired variant against control, and against the official development run as a second before; exact two-sided McNemar on gained and lost; Wilson 95% intervals): development origin accuracy in **food (20), none (118), other (331) and all 469**, with the 19 gated rulings reported on their own.
- **Criteria, stated before the results.** **Helped:** food gains net two or more rulings against the control (gained minus lost, at least +2) and the no-regression rule holds. **No regression:** in none and in other, net change against the control is not worse than -3 (the spread seen above) and the exact McNemar p is 0.05 or more against a loss. Because the other 450 prompts are identical to the control's, any difference there is gateway variation, by design; this measures it. **Not testable as significant:** food has four misses, so even four gained and none lost gives p = 0.125; the best possible verdict on food is "better, not significant", as in D842.
- **Expectation, stated now.** Control about 15 to 16 of 20 in food, as before. Food-v1 16 to 18 of 20 (net 0 to +2). None and other within three of the control. About even odds that "helped" is met, and a result that cannot be told from noise is the likeliest outcome.
- **Cost and stop rule.** Two runs about $6.5 against this task's $25 cap ($0.0149 spent so far on the smoke test); a run that would pass the cap is not started. Each cost is added to the spend ledger. If the criterion is not met, the result is reported as it is and nothing is tuned again without a new entry (D858 at most, one revision).

## D857 — U.S. origin accuracy on food: results of D856 (25 Nov, #815)
Runs as pre-registered, except as disclosed below. Control `dev-gemini-4-argon-prec-engine-v1-litellm-815-control` and variant `dev-gemini-4-argon-prec-engine-v1-litellm-food-v1-815-food-v1`, both through the gateway with `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, each from a clean committed tree (`code_dirty` false, `dataset_sha256` recorded). Figures from `eval/accuracy/measure_815.py` (`815-measure.json`, in `make reproduce`); Wilson 95% intervals; exact two-sided McNemar on gained and lost. **Development only. Held-out was spent in D842, was not read and is not re-scored: there is no independent figure, and the food guidance was written from rulings that include three of the four it fixed.**
- **Food (20), variant against control: 15 → 19 of 20** (75%, 53–89 → 95%, 76–99); 4 gained, 0 lost, McNemar p = 0.125. Gained: N350517 (puree: Costa Rica → France), N352389 (fish oil: China → Peru), N354481 (chicken skewers: China → United States), N350768 (a prepared vegetable, Korea FTA). N352231 (razor clams) was right in both runs. The three rulings in the first group are ones the guidance text was written from (D856), so their gain is not evidence that the text generalises; N350768 was not used. Against the official run (Vertex): 16 → 19, 4 gained, 1 lost (N354493, wrong in every run), p = 0.375. The 19 rulings whose prompt changed: 15 → 19, 4 gained, 0 lost. None of them was outside the food slice.
- **No regression: held.** None (118): 102 → 103 (1 gained, 0 lost, p = 1.0). Other (331): 303 → 302 (1 gained, 2 lost, p = 1.0). All 469: 420 → 424 (89.6%, 86.5–92.0 → 90.4%, 87.4–92.8); 6 gained, 2 lost, p = 0.289. The 450 rulings outside the gate got a byte-identical prompt, so their 2 gained and 2 lost are gateway variation: that is the noise at this size.
- **Criterion, as stated in D856: met.** Food net +4 against the required +2; none +1 and other -1 against a floor of -3, both p above 0.05. The best verdict D856 allowed on food was "better, not significant", and that is the verdict: with four misses to fix, four gained and none lost gives p = 0.125. Against the expectation (16 to 18) the result is one higher.
- **Disclosures.**
  - The control's first invocation wrote 420 of 469 rows: 49 rows were lost (the eval's file write ignores errors; the data volume was at 99% and a write failure is the likely cause, not checked further). The same command with the same tag, resumed after the first invocation's results were committed, ran the 49 missing cases and appended them (second RUNLOG row, 469 of 469; control 420 of 469). The first invocation's 49 calls were paid for and discarded.
  - The variant had one failed gateway call (N351229, an "other" ruling, wrong in the row; right in the control; "model provider unavailable" after four attempts at 134 s). It was counted wrong and not retried. It is one of the two losses in "other"; counted right, other would be 303 → 303.
  - `measure_815.py` was written while the variant run was in progress, before any variant row was read, and was committed after the run. It computes the metrics D856 named.
- **Cost and latency.** Control $3.65 on 469 rows (about $4.04 with the 49 lost rows), variant $3.62, smoke test $0.0149: about $7.7 of the task's $25. Per call $0.0079 in both. Latency p50 7.2 s control, 8.0 s variant; p95 11.9 s and 19.6 s (the variant's tail includes the 134 s failure).
- **Reading.** On development, adding four statements on food to the prompt of the 19 rulings that read as food moved food from 15 to 19 of 20 and nothing else measurably. It cannot be told apart from run to run variation by the test (p = 0.125) and three of the four gains are on the rulings it was written from. It is **eval-only**: the server does not use it and nothing here changes production. The finding that would justify adopting it is a food result on rulings the text was not written from, which this repository does not hold: D842's held-out food (15 rulings, 11 right) is spent, and development has 20. Not addressed: the 15 development misses with no template. Nine are essential-character and assembly judgments of unrelated goods, where rules-v1 and rules-v2 did not help, and the engine's China answers (92, 69 right) are the larger pattern.

## D858 — U.S. origin accuracy on food: a test set food-v1 was not written from, pre-registered (25 Nov, #821)
Committed and pushed before either run below. D857 found food 15 → 19 of 20 on development, but three of the four gains are rulings the food-v1 text was written from, and held-out is spent. This entry tests food-v1, unchanged, on food rulings it was not written from. It is the small set of #821; the larger probe of 2019–2022 rulings is not part of it.
- **Where the rulings come from** (`eval/accuracy/build_foodfresh.py`, `eval/splits/splits_foodfresh.json`; no model calls, no engine output read).
  - **Training (9).** Training and tune_check rulings that pass `engine.FoodCase` with one held origin: 36. Left out: the 9 D856 names as sources, and 17 whose facts and CBP holding the writer of food-v1 printed while writing it (found by searching that work's transcript for each ID). One more has two held origins. 9 remain; two are not food (N333392 pencils, N345287 a yacht) and stay in, because they are what the gate fires on.
  - **Cited (8).** CROSS search now answers 403 ("Security parameters are missing"); it was not worked around. Instead, every ruling number cited in the text of the corpus's food-gated rulings and absent from every labels file (97) was fetched by number (`corpus fetch`; 49 exist on CROSS, 1994–2022) and labelled by `corpus final2-label`. Kept: substantial transformation, one held origin, passes `engine.FoodCase`. Two held origins were added by hand from CBP's holding sentence (`eval/data/foodfresh_manual.json`: N008056 cashews, Brazil; N326044 black garlic, Spain). H317062 (tahini, a trade-agreement claim) is left out by hand: its label is the seeds' origin, not the tahini's, and it shares importer and question with source ruling H326919.
  - **Recent (0).** New York numbers N366801–N367300 fetched by number on 25 Nov (rulings posted after the final2 probe of 21 Nov); none of the 500 numbers exists on CROSS yet, so this group is empty. Numbers below N366801 that were missing on 21 Nov and posted since are not covered.
  - **Total 17**, frozen at 2026-11-25T10:43:07+08:00 before any scoring. Every one passes the food gate, so every variant prompt carries the food text.
- **Bias, stated now.** Cited rulings are ones CBP chose to cite, which tend to be settled practice. Cases dated before 2023 see only earlier rulings in the same set as precedents (the corpus starts in 2023), so they have few or none; both runs get the same retrieval. The training rulings are precedents for development rulings that the writer read; their own facts and holdings were not read.
- **Runs, gateway only** (LiteLLM to gemini-4-argon, `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, each from a clean committed tree, results committed after each run). From `backend/`, with `-split foodfresh -splits ../eval/splits/splits_foodfresh.json -labels ../eval/data/labels.jsonl,../eval/data/labels_final2.jsonl,../eval/data/labels_foodfresh.jsonl -facts data/facts,../eval/data/facts_final2,../eval/data/facts_foodfresh`: **control** `-tag 858-control`; **variant** the same with `-food-rules -tag 858-food-v1`. One run each. No change to food-v1 or the gate.
- **Measured** (`eval/accuracy/measure_858.py`, written before both runs): accuracy with Wilson 95% intervals, gained and lost, exact two-sided McNemar, for all, training and new.
- **Criteria, stated before the results.** **Generalises:** net +2 or better on all 17, and no more lost than gained among training or among new. **Harms:** net -2 or worse. Anything between is **no detectable effect**. With this size no outcome is significant at 0.05 unless the net is about +6 or more; the verdict is directional.
- **Expectation.** The control misses a few (the cited and older rulings have thin precedents); food-v1 fixes one or two and loses up to one. Most likely result: no detectable effect or a small "generalises".
- **What follows.** Enabling food-v1 in the server needs its own entry and is not decided here. If it harms, it stays eval-only and the larger probe is dropped. Otherwise the 2019–2022 probe (#821) is the next measurement.
- **Cost and stop rule.** Two runs of 17 calls, about $0.40; stop at $5. Each cost goes in the spend ledger.

## D859 — U.S. origin accuracy on food: results of D858 (25 Nov, #821)
Runs as pre-registered. Control `foodfresh-gemini-4-argon-prec-engine-v1-litellm-858-control` and variant `foodfresh-gemini-4-argon-prec-engine-v1-litellm-food-v1-858-food-v1`, both through the gateway with `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, each from a clean committed tree (`code_dirty` false, `dataset_sha256` recorded). Figures from `eval/accuracy/measure_858.py` (`858-measure.json`, in `make reproduce`). No failed calls; all 17 variant prompts carried the food text.
- **All 17: 17 → 15** (100%, 81.6–100 → 88.2%, 65.7–96.7); 0 gained, 2 lost, McNemar p = 0.5. **Training 9: 9 → 9.** **New 8: 8 → 6.**
- **Criterion, as stated in D858: harms** (net -2). The control answered all 17 right, so no gain was possible on this set; the test could only find harm, and it did, though not significantly.
- **The two losses are the same kind of case.** N284246 (2017): U.S. salmon filleted in China, marinated in the United States; CBP held China, food-v1 answered United States. N320603 (2021): tuna caught by Chinese-flagged vessels, loined and trimmed in Japan; CBP held Japan, food-v1 answered China. In both, CBP held that cutting a fish into fillets or loins in a second country changed its origin. food-v1's first statement says the opposite, which is what the 2023–2025 rulings it was written from hold (frozen fish, squid, halibut, scallops). Without the text the engine followed the precedents and answered both right.
- **Reading.** food-v1 fixes the development rulings it was written from and overrides older fish rulings that went the other way. Whether CBP changed practice or these are fact-specific was not checked. Either way, a fixed rule on fish processing is wrong for some real rulings the engine otherwise gets right. **food-v1 stays eval-only and is not proposed for the server.** As D858 set out, the larger 2019–2022 probe is dropped: those rulings are the period where the conflict sits.
- **Not shown.** Nothing here is significant (n = 17, two discordant pairs). The set is small and skewed to cited, older rulings, where the control was perfect.
- **D886.** D886 (a protocol for this test written while D858 was being built, merged to main before these results) also left out training rulings already served by a family template. D858 did not; all training rulings stayed. That does not touch the finding: both losses are in the new group, and training went 9 → 9. The provenance D886 asked for in #823 is here: the 17 rulings the writer read are listed in `build_foodfresh.py`, the cited rulings and their labels are in `labels_foodfresh.jsonl` and `facts_foodfresh/` (both hash-pinned in `eval/SHA256SUMS`), and the 25 Nov post-cutoff probe found no usable ruling: N366801–N367300 were not on CROSS, and numbers below N366801 that were missing on 21 Nov and posted since were not covered.
- **Cost.** Control $0.115, variant $0.125: $0.24. Latency p50 8.0 s and 7.7 s.

## D860 — U.S. origin accuracy: China against the assembly country, one change and an unseen check, pre-registered (25 Nov, #831)
Committed and pushed before any run below. Held-out was spent in D842 and is not read.
- **The pattern** (official development run `dev-gemini-4-argon-prec-engine-v1-vertex`, 422 of 469). The engine answers China 92 times, 69 right (75%; its other answers about 92%). 34 misses involve China: in 23 it kept China where CBP held the country that assembled or finished the goods (Vietnam 5, Thailand 5, Cambodia 2, others), and in 11 it moved away from China where CBP kept China (filters, a lock, sensors, lamps). Both directions are the same judgment: the country that made the main parts versus the country that assembled or finished the goods. rules-v1 and rules-v2 (D27, D157) gave general guidance on it and did not move development accuracy.
- **The one change: `china-v1`.** `engine.ChinaRules` (four statements: origin goes to the last country whose work makes the good, not where most or the costliest parts were made; building the mechanism, circuit board or main body, or complex assembly, moves origin; kits, a few screws, housing a complete core, coating, testing and packing do not; weigh each country's work and follow the closest precedent) is added to the system prompt only when `engine.ChinaCase` says the facts name China and another country of the picker table (the United States, the usual importer, does not count). Deterministic, facts only. It fires on **391 of 469** development rulings (354 right in the official run), so it is close to a general prompt change. It was written from the decisive steps of the 34 development misses above (in both directions). Eval-only: `eval run -china-rules`; the server does not use it.
- **Unseen check.** `eval/splits/splits_chinacheck.json` (`build_chinacheck.py`, frozen 2026-11-25T11:08:44+08:00): the **623** training and tune_check rulings the gate fires on. The writer of china-v1 has read none of them, their labels or any result on them (they were counted, not opened). A Go test checks the list equals `engine.ChinaCase` over the training facts. They are precedents for the development rulings, and their own precedents are earlier training rulings.
- **Runs, gateway only** (LiteLLM to gemini-4-argon, `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, each from a clean committed tree, results committed after each). From `backend/` with `-facts data/facts`: development control `-split dev -tag 860-control`, variant the same with `-china-rules -tag 860-china-v1`; check control `-split train -splits ../eval/splits/splits_chinacheck.json -tag 860-control`, variant the same with `-china-rules -tag 860-china-v1`. One run each.
- **Measured** (`eval/accuracy/measure_860.py`, written before the runs): for development (all, gated, ungated) and the check, accuracy with Wilson 95% intervals, gained and lost, exact two-sided McNemar; and China answers with how many are right.
- **Criteria, stated before the results.** **Helped:** development net +3 or better against its control **and** check net +5 or better, with development ungated not worse than -3. **Harms:** development net -3 or worse, or check net -5 or worse. Anything else is **no detectable effect**. Only the check can be read as evidence that the text generalises; a development gain alone is not (the text was written from development misses). Run-to-run variation is about ±2 on development (D856, D857) and is expected to be about ±4 on the check.
- **Expectation, stated now.** No detectable effect is the likeliest result (D27, D157). China answers may drop and their accuracy rise while the total stays level, because misses go both ways.
- **What follows.** "Helped" would justify a separate decision on the server; nothing changes in production here. Otherwise china-v1 stays eval-only and this group is closed for prompt text.
- **Cost and stop rule.** Development about $3.7 a run, the check about $4.9 a run: about $17 in all, against a $25 cap for this task; a run that would pass the cap is not started. Each cost goes in the spend ledger.

## D861 — U.S. origin accuracy: results of D860, china-v1 (25 Nov, #831)
Runs as pre-registered, each from a clean committed tree through the gateway with `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1` (`code_dirty` false, `dataset_sha256` recorded); no failed calls. Figures from `eval/accuracy/measure_860.py` (`860-measure.json`, in `make reproduce`); Wilson 95% intervals; exact two-sided McNemar.
- **Development (469): 422 → 424** (90.0%, 86.9–92.4 → 90.4%, 87.4–92.8); 10 gained, 8 lost, p = 0.81. Gated (391): 353 → 354, 9 gained, 8 lost. Ungated (78, byte-identical prompts): 69 → 70, gateway variation.
- **Unseen check (623 training rulings): 534 → 539** (85.7%, 82.7–88.2 → 86.5%, 83.6–89.0); 10 gained, 5 lost, p = 0.30.
- **China answers did not change.** Development 68 right of 93 → 68 of 92; check 80 of 121 → 79 of 118. The text moved individual rulings both ways without changing how often the engine picks the parts country over the assembly country.
- **Criterion, as stated in D860: no detectable effect.** "Helped" needed development +3 and the check +5; development was +2. Not "harms". The check's +5 is the size D860 set for it, but with 15 discordant rulings it is not significant, and the China answers, the pattern this targeted, stayed the same.
- **Reading.** A written statement of CBP's parts-versus-assembly test does not shift the engine's judgment on these cases, as with rules-v1 and rules-v2 (D27, D157). china-v1 stays eval-only and this group is closed for prompt text. The remaining China misses are essential-character calls that CBP itself makes both ways for similar goods (air filters: N351081 China, N352485 Thailand).
- **Cost and latency.** Development $3.69 and $3.93, check $4.88 and $5.24: $17.74, inside the $25 cap. Per call $0.0079 control, $0.0084 variant (longer prompt). p50 7.4 s and 7.2 s on development; p95 11.0 s and 11.6 s.

## D862 — Batteries and furniture: rulings outside the corpus, found by search and fetched by number, pre-registered (25 Nov, #777, #779, #826, #827)
Committed and pushed before any query below is run and before any candidate is read. #826 and #827 asked for rulings the committed corpus does not hold; the corpus starts in 2023, and older CBP rulings were never searched. This entry searches for them.
- **Search (`eval/families/b4-queries.json`, frozen).** Six web-search queries per scope, run once each. CROSS search answers 403 and is not used; rulings are fetched by number (`corpus fetch`). Candidates: every N or H ruling number in the results, and, one hop, every N or H number cited in the text of a fetched candidate kept below. Rulings numbered without N or H (before about 2004) are left out: the product's ruling IDs are N or H plus six digits.
- **Exclusions, applied first by ID.** Any ID in any split file (`eval/splits/`, routed included), in `labels_final2.jsonl`, `labels_usmca_final2.jsonl` or `labels_foodfresh.jsonl`; any ID already in `backend/data/labels.jsonl` (those were screened by D820); rulings dated 2026 or later (D660); rulings CROSS marks `revokedBy`, `modifiedBy` or `operationallyRevoked`, or that a fetched ruling revokes or modifies.
- **Labels.** `corpus final2-label` (regex holding), with manual corrections from CBP's holding sentence in `eval/families/b4-manual.json`, each with the sentence. Kept only with one held origin and a facts section that says what was done where.
- **Scope, D820's, unchanged.** Battery packs: cells, modules, packs, power banks, portable power stations, storage systems and battery management boards sold as such. Furniture: 9401, 9403 and 9404 goods and their structural parts, each tagged `upholstery`, `finishing` or `knock_down` when its holding turns on that work alone.
- **Where they go.** Kept rulings go in a cited-only pool, `backend/data/labels_cited.jsonl` and `backend/data/facts_cited/`. Templates may cite them; retrieval and the engine do not read them, so no answer changes. `TestTemplateCitationsAreRealRulings` accepts a citation from either file, with the same rules.
- **Development cases, by rule.** Within each scope, kept new rulings in date order: every third (3rd, 6th, …) is a development case and is never cited. Fixed before any template is written.
- **Bar.** Battery packs: D820's bar, at least 10 kept pool rulings not served by a dedicated template (the committed 6 plus new kept, non-development rulings); if met, a `battery_packs` template with cells, modules and BMS PCBA, and pack assembly groups, keeping N346317 and N348871. Furniture: a group or operation for upholstery, finishing or knock-down needs at least one kept ruling whose holding turns on it.
- **Measured.** Offline, as D820: M1 retrieval, M2 guard, M3 planner fixtures, M4 citations and distinct rulings per template. Then one family check of the development set with the new cases (`familycov`, through the LiteLLM gateway only), before (main) and after, reporting family matches per scope.

## D868 — Older rulings as retrieval precedents: a test on the development cases they change, pre-registered (25 Nov, #837)
Committed and pushed before the runs. Development only; held-out is not read.
- **The change tested.** The cited-only pool of D862 (`backend/data/labels_cited.jsonl`, 15 rulings dated 2009–2021: 5 battery, 10 furniture) joins the BM25 precedent pool. Eval-only: `eval run -labels ../eval/data/labels.jsonl,data/labels_cited.jsonl -facts data/facts,data/facts_cited`; the server and production are unchanged.
- **Which cases can change** (`eval retrdiff`, new, offline, no model; `eval/accuracy/868-retrdiff.json`). Of 469 development cases, **16** get a different top-5; **4** retrieve an older ruling (H331375 gets H316545, N351341 gets N306161, N353511 and N356481 get N300248), and 12 only reorder or swap one precedent because the larger pool shifts BM25's term weights. Every other case gets a byte-identical prompt, so only these 16 are run (`eval/splits/splits_retrdiff.json`, key `subset`). In D860's development control, 12 of the 16 were right.
- **Runs, gateway only** (gemini-4-argon, `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, clean committed tree, results committed after each). From `backend/`, `-split subset -splits ../eval/splits/splits_retrdiff.json -facts data/facts,data/facts_cited`: control `-tag 868-control` (labels as production), variant `-labels ../eval/data/labels.jsonl,data/labels_cited.jsonl -tag 868-cited`.
- **Measured** (`eval/accuracy/measure_868.py`, written before): gained, lost and exact McNemar on all 16, on the 4 that retrieve an older ruling and on the 12 that only reorder; against D860's control too.
- **Criteria.** **Helped:** net +2 or better on the 16 and no loss among the 4. **Harms:** net -2 or worse. Otherwise **no detectable effect**. With 16 cases nothing here can be significant, and the ceiling is small: at most 4 misses in D860's control.
- **Expectation.** No detectable effect: the pool is 15 rulings against 2,790, and 12 of the 16 changes are reorderings. The question this answers is whether a pool this small is worth wiring into production; a larger pool of older rulings would be the follow-up.
- **Cost.** About $0.25 for both runs; cap $2.

## D870 — Japan: a reviewed HS-edition correlation, applied only when the lookup finds no rule (24 Nov, #791 94fb24f6)
Some Japan Customs rulings carry a code from a later HS edition than the schedule uses, so the lookup returned `no_match` and the case went to review. A short list of correlations (`backend/internal/jprules/data/correlations.json`) now sits behind that outcome.
- **Decision.**
  - The list applies only on `no_match`, for an exact agreement and six-digit code. A matched rule, `too_broad`, `withheld`, `invalid_code` and the general rules are untouched.
  - **Map or hint.** `mapped` when every parent code in the older edition returns the same schedule row; the case then goes to the model with that row behind a plain note that the link is administrative and partial. `edition_hint` when the parents differ: the case goes to review naming the parents, with no rule text.
  - **The edition comes from the code, never from the case date.**
  - JP-EU 2404.11 is mapped (WCO Table I, both parents inside one row). CPTPP 2202.99 and 3824.99 and JP-Malaysia 3824.99 are mapped. CPTPP 0307.43 is a hint: its two parents have different rules.
  - Sibling codes 2404.12 to 2404.99 stay `no_match`; their WCO sources include a second chapter.
- **Why.** Japan published no later-edition annex for JP-EU or CPTPP in the sources checked, so the only evidence for these codes is the older row and the WCO table. A hint where the rules differ avoids choosing one.
- **Result, development split (offline, no model, no label read).** Eligible 2589 → 2674 of 2973. Mapped 85; 0307.43 as hint for 14. This counts cases that can show a rule source, not accuracy.
- **Cost if wrong.** A mapped rule is shown for a code whose HS 2017 parents' rule differs from the shown row. The identical-rows requirement is the guard: if the parents do not return identical rows, the entry downgrades to a hint. The model still answers from the case facts and may return "undetermined".
- **Evidence.** `docs/japan/hs-edition-correlation.md` (sources with sha256 and pages); `go run ./cmd/jpeval diagnose -split dev`.

## D871 — Japan: missing-facts text in the review message, and where the input check stops (24 Nov, #792 f0351172)
- **Decision.** When a Japan check ends "undetermined" and the case has a structured product, the review message adds up to three things the user can fill in (no materials, a material with a blank origin, no production steps, a step with no resolved plant country), then "And N more". It is advisory. Qualifies and does not-qualify results are untouched. The model prompt bytes are unchanged (`TestPSRRequestBytesUnchanged` passes).
- **Corpus check boundary.** The current English-input projection was checked across the 2973 development cases: no truncation. Structured countries (222 of 272 verbatim, 50 spelling variants) and percentage and threshold counts were compared. Not verified: semantic translation fidelity, structured `inputs[]` chapters and headings, the contents of `other_ja`. No corpus change was made.
- **Why.** Unknowns reach the user only as a bare "undetermined" today. A prompt change to render unknowns would need a PromptVersion bump, so it was not done.
- **Cost if wrong.** A user is asked for a fact the case already holds in free text (negations are not parsed). Names are bounded and sanitised after review found the first version could print unbounded user text.
- **Evidence.** `docs/japan/missing-facts-review.md`.

## D872 — Japan: split-row repair and Thailand scope notes (24 Nov, #793 3a44d562, #795 c5f7b4eb)
- **Decision.**
  - **Parser fix (#793).** `eval/jp/build_psr.py` no longer lets a wrapped line starting with a code-like token open a new row, keeps code-less continuation lines in six-column tables, and completes merged cells in five-column tables. Only the changed schedules were regenerated; the rest are byte-identical.
  - **Rows before → after.** Malaysia 574 → 339, Mexico 1640 → 877, Philippines 1139 → 716, Chile 1000 → 680, India 410 → 378, Vietnam 1218 → 1212. Thailand (739) and AJCEP HS 2022 (559) keep their counts with changed text.
  - **Dropped notes.** Independent review found the first repair had dropped "Note N:" scope notes for Malaysia, Philippines and Mexico. They were restored as notes with an `applies` list of code ranges read from each note's own wording, validated on load.
  - **Thailand (#795).** 20 scope notes were missing from the data and are now captured, each with applicability.
- **Result, development split.** Eligible 2674 → 2673: Vietnam 2817.00 moved from `psr` to `no_match` because the PDF lists no 2817 rule. Evidence text changed for 51 rulings after #793 and for 25 Thailand rulings after #795.
- **Known remaining gaps.** Indonesia's notes were not audited. Thailand p3 General Notes 1 and 2 are omitted (no chapter or section to scope them to), so some rule text uses terms the model is not shown. Some Vietnam and AJCEP rows may still hold a product description in place of a rule.
- **Cost if wrong.** A rule's evidence misses text that changes its meaning. This is checked only by the audit and tests, not by the held-out set.
- **Evidence.** `docs/japan/psr-split-row-repair.md`, `docs/japan/thailand-scope-notes.md`.

## D873 — Japan: AJCEP general fallback only for a real HS 2017 code (24 Nov, #794 c6be884a)
- **Decision.** The AJCEP general criteria used to be returned for any code with no product row, including codes in no HS 2017 subheading. Now they are returned only for a code in an embedded HS 2017 list (5,387 six-digit codes, codes only). Reserved chapters 00, 77, 98, 99 return `invalid_code`. Any other absent code returns `not_in_schedule_edition`, because the lookup cannot tell a later-edition code from a typo. Product rows still come first.
- **Source.** UN Comtrade reference file H5 (retrieved 24 Nov), cross-checked against five UNSD tables and a Japan Customs tariff. The licence is unclear (UN copyright notice; no open licence found), so only bare numeric codes are embedded, with no descriptions or hierarchy. This is a recorded caveat, not a clearance.
- **Result, development split.** Eligible 2673 → 2672 (code 3907.29 is not in HS 2017). No AJCEP correlation exists for it.
- **Cost if wrong.** A real HS 2017 code missing from the list is sent to review instead of getting the general rules. Tests check every code the HS 2017 schedules cite against the list.
- **Evidence.** `docs/japan/ajcep-general-validity.md`.

## D874 — Japan: Japan-US Trade Agreement pilot (24 Nov, #796 d990d606, selector #798 d9ce88dc)
- **Decision.**
  - **Japanese text accepted.** Annex I Section C is published only in Japanese; rows and notes are stored in Japanese as the authoritative text.
  - **Edition not stated.** The agreement names no HS edition, so citations say so and no edition label is shown in the selector.
  - **Default rows.** The Subsection 3 head sets CC for the goods in Subsection 2 note 1(a) to (p) unless a table row says otherwise. Default rows are quoted for those goods only, apply only to real HS 2017 codes, and never overlap an explicit row (review caught overlaps).
  - **HS 2022 codes.** 20 codes exist only in HS 2022; 19 are mapped through the WCO table and one (0403.20) is a hint.
  - **National items.** 2206.00-100 and 2207.10-199 return `too_broad`.
  - **Partial.** General rules, Subsection 1 paragraphs 4 to 10, and Annex II are not embedded. Every result carries a caveat that the text is partial. Later Annex I amendments are unchecked. A Japanese customs specialist has not reviewed the text.
- **Result, development split.** Of 149 JP-US TA cases, all `unsupported_agreement` before; after, 148 `psr` and 1 `too_broad` (2207.10).
- **Cost if wrong.** A default CC row is shown where an unembedded paragraph (for example accessories or third-country transport) changes the answer. The caveat names this.
- **Evidence.** `docs/japan/jp-us-ta-pilot.md`; source `us2.pdf` sha256 `af460808…962d6`.

## D875 — Japan: answer validation hardening, and what was left as documentation (24 Nov, #797 d4a1a23b)
- **Shipped.** A qualifying answer's origin must be one country or territory from a closed list (UN M49 names, the shared country table, listed aliases) or the EU. The resolver both accepts and returns the name. Blank deciding rules are rejected. Reasoning and deciding rule are length-capped and stripped of control characters. Unshown ruling numbers in free text become "an unverified reference". Case ids are normalised before retrieval. This is a well-formedness check, not a treaty-party or eligibility check.
- **Documented only (changes what the model sees).** Irrelevant precedents (the agreement code in the query matches every ruling of that agreement) and duplicate precedents (295 same-agreement groups with identical facts; 6.3% of precedent slots).
- **Offline replay.** The archived D712 `dev_eval` outputs were replayed through the new checks: 400 ids, 348 comparable, 0 new rejects, 0 of 244 origins changed. The archive stores origins already normalised, so regressions on raw alias spellings cannot be tested. This is not an accuracy result.
- **Cost if wrong.** A valid but uncommon country spelling is rejected until added. It errs toward review, not toward a guess.
- **Evidence.** `docs/japan/answer-validation.md`.

## D876 — Japan campaign: process rulings (24 Nov, campaign start 17:08Z; #791 to #798)
- **One writer, one PR at a time.** Each batch was built on the merged main of the one before. Rule-core edits were serialised.
- **Independent review rounds that caught defects before merge.**
  - Overlapping default and explicit rows returned two rules for the same code (#796).
  - Default rows answered for non-HS codes (#796).
  - Dropped "Note N:" scope conditions after the split-row repair (#793).
  - Unbounded user names in the review message (#792).
  - Origin false rejections for official spellings, then permissive acceptance of non-country text, then alias gaps, over three rounds (#797).
  - A rule was not merged until a covering approval of the exact head.
- **Authenticated smoke paused and untouched.** No product backend call, no credentials.
- **Frozen D741 untouched.** Only development ids were analysed; no held-out label was read.
- **Deployment through the normal merge path.** No workflow, script or infrastructure change.

## D877 — Japan: Generalized System of Preferences rule pilot, current window only (24 Nov, #800 20b39a82)
- **Decision.**
  - **Source.** The Appendix Table of the Ministerial Ordinance for Enforcement of the Temporary Tariff Measures Law, from the e-Gov law API. It is published only in Japanese, so rows and notes are stored in Japanese.
  - **One window.** Only the window from 2023-04-01 is embedded. The three earlier windows were extracted and checked against their XML but not shipped; earlier dates return `no_dated_source`.
  - **What is stored.** 251 rows, 9 quoted notes, and an Unde Labs caveat note that is shown first. Rows are located by a `ref` into the table, not by page.
  - **HS 2022 gate.** The ordinance names no edition; HS 2022 is an inference, and the citation says so. A list of 5,612 HS 2022 codes (UN Comtrade H6, codes only, same licence caveat as D873) gates the group rows, so a code in no edition never gets a chapter row.
  - **No qualifying answer.** A model answer of `qualifies` is changed to `undetermined` for this agreement, because the beneficiary country, Cabinet Order coverage, Form A, cumulation and least-developed-country relaxations are not modelled. `does_not_qualify` and `undetermined` stay as the model said. The prompt is unchanged. The new-case selector does not list this agreement.
- **Result, development split (offline, no model).** Of 131 GSP cases: all `unsupported_agreement` before; after, 130 with a rule and 1 `no_match`. This is rule-reference coverage only, not decisions and not accuracy.
- **Cost if wrong.** A GSP `does_not_qualify` can be given on a row that covers only part of a heading: 33 entries read "of which" (のうち) in their description, and the lookup cannot tell whether the product is in that part. These are disclosed in the doc and the caveat. Narrowing words inside other rows were not enumerated.
- **Evidence.** `docs/japan/gsp-pilot.md` (revision ids and sha256, earlier windows table, gaps).

## D878 — Japan: withheld rows reviewed, three narrowed or restored (24 Nov, #802 e289e798)
- **Decision.** The 41 rows blocked before this change (JP-EU 4, CPTPP 12, Switzerland 25) were reviewed against the official footnotes. A block stays unless the footnote proves the exact limit.
  - **JP-EU 7007.** Footnote 1 names only 7007.11 and 7007.21, so those two stay withheld and the rest of 7007 to 7009 is a normal row with the footnote as a note.
  - **Switzerland 3501 to 3505.** The merged row is split into its four source lines.

  - **Stay withheld.** CPTPP dagger rows (the appendix is an optional RVC route and an unblock needs a note citing a second PDF; no dev case), JP-EU and JP-UK 84 and 87, and the other 24 Switzerland rows.
- **Result, development split.** Eligible 2950 → 2952 (JP-EU 7007.29 and Switzerland 3504.00 moved from withheld to a rule). Code-level differences are in the doc on its stated basis. Rule availability only, not accuracy.
- **Cost if wrong.** A narrowed row shows a rule for a code whose appendix has a different threshold. The footnote text bounds this for 7007 and 3501 to 3505. A restored UK row stays withheld, so it adds no text.

## D879 — Japan: selector contract and a process lesson; net measurement (24 Nov, #798, #801; measured at 20b39a82)
- **Contract.** The frontend selector test derives each agreement's declared edition from "(HS yyyy)" in the schedule citations. Agreements with no stated edition (Japan-US, GSP) must show none.
- **What happened.** #800 changed only backend data, so the frontend CI job was skipped by its path filter. The GSP citation contains "validated against HS 2022", which the test read as a declared edition, and the test failed on main. #801 fixed it: the test now parses only a parenthesised stated edition and asserts that schedules without one say "not stated".
- **Rule.** A PR that changes `backend/internal/jprules/data` must also run the frontend `japan-preference` test locally before merge. A skipped job is not a pass.
- **Net measurement at 20b39a82 (offline, no model).** Development split eligible rule reference 2589 → 2950 of 2973. `dev_eval` 366 → 395 of 400, a subset of the development split, so the two are not additive. GSP is counted as rule reference only. Not accuracy.
- **Cost if wrong.** A citation whose wording happens to look like an edition changes what the selector shows; the stricter parse and the "not stated" assertion guard it.
- **Evidence.** `docs/japan/gsp-pilot.md`, `docs/japan/jp-us-ta-pilot.md`.

## D880 — Japan-UK: header rows no longer copy the previous rule (24 Nov, #808)
- **Decision.** In the Japan-UK schedule, 38 headings whose rule cell is empty had copied the previous row's rule. The parser now keeps one row per "-" sub-line branch, keyed to the heading's own code range (before, they were keyed to the chapter, which the copied heading row shadowed), and gives an empty-cell heading no rule of its own. Rows 462 → 424.
- **Why.** A copied rule is text from a different product, shown as evidence for the heading.
- **Result.** 198 codes (of the 5,387 HS 2017 codes, two dates) return different or fuller evidence. On the development split, 0 of 24 UK rulings hit a copied row. This is parser correctness, not accuracy.
- **Cost if wrong.** A heading whose real rule sits in a sub-line is shown the sub-line rows, not one rule. Withheld and footnote rows are unchanged.
- **Evidence.** `docs/japan/uk-header-rows.md`.

## D881 — Japan: General Notes and Annex notes are evidence, not optional (24 Nov, #809 to #813)
- **Rule.** Definitions, tolerances and value notes are source-needed evidence. A note is not suppressed to keep the request short.
- **What shipped.**
  - **#809.** The gap and the notes already embedded are documented.
  - **#810.** EU and UK Annex 3-A notes (22 and 20), each with its own source link and citation.
  - **#811.** Australia column 4: 530 rows and 28 notes.
  - **#812.** AJCEP Annex 2 provisions returned with product rows. Article 26 is left out so that product rows keep precedence. The HS 2022 window has a gap.
  - **#813.** 45 notes across nine annexes. CPTPP paragraph 5 is deliberately not attached.
- **Cost.** `dev_eval` plan request bytes 5,118,030 (at 20b39a82) → 7,332,525 (at 33598601), +43%. This is evidence only; the prompt text is unchanged. Clarification: 5,118,030 bytes is at 20b39a82 with 395 requests; 7,332,525 is at 33598601 with 396 requests. The +43% is an aggregate, not a per-ID matched evidence effect, and not literal Vertex usage or cost. It is not the programme's initial 366 baseline.
- **Cost if wrong.** More input tokens and latency per request, and a long note may dilute the rule that decides the case. Neither is measured.
- **Evidence.** `docs/japan/general-notes-gap.md`, `general-notes-embedded.md`, `annex-3a-notes.md`, `australia-column4.md`, `ajcep-annex2-provisions.md`.

## D882 — Japan: schedule date windows (24 Nov, #809)
- **Decision.** No date was changed. A treaty's entry into force is not the validity of a given HS schedule edition, so a date moves only on a source that says so.
- **Unverified starts.** Thailand 2023-01-01 (the Japanese index labels an edition "2022.1.1~"; the two files were compared and are not shown to differ) and the AJCEP HS 2017 start.
- **RCEP.** `rcepStart` stays 2023-01-01. The 2022 original is an image-only PDF and is not lowered.

## D883 — Japan: net measurement of the campaign, and what it is not (24 Nov, at 33598601)
- **Measured (offline, no model, no label read).** Development split eligible rule reference 2589 → 2952 of 2973. `dev_eval` 366 → 396 of 400, a subset of the development split, so the two are not additive. GSP is counted as rule reference only. The `dev_eval` plan has 396 requests.

## D884 — Japan-India chapter 3 amendment and a typed declared edition (24 Nov, #817 d728a309, #818 f52f46e6)

Of 224 HS 2017 six-digit codes in chapter 3: 210 keep the same rule, 0304.99 is CC, 5 are hints and 8 have no rule.
