## D886 — U.S. food-v1: independent-test protocol reserved before any new run (25 Nov, #821, #823)
- **Status.** Protocol only. No independent split is frozen and no model call has been made for this decision. D856/D857's development gain (food 15 → 19 of 20, McNemar p = 0.125, three of four gains on rulings the text was written from) stays eval-only and is not evidence of accuracy on unseen food rulings.
- **Blocker.** The exact IDs remain unavailable: D856 names 14 written-from rulings and the writer read 17 more that are not recorded; the 7 cited older rulings need raw full texts or the author's list; the ~2 rulings after the 13 Nov final2 cutoff are not in the repository. Gateway credentials are also absent. #823 records the owner asks.
- **Pre-registered rule.** Once #823 supplies the IDs: exclude every D856-written-from ruling and any ruling whose facts/holdings the writer read; exclude the spent D842 held-out food slice and the already-scored final2 split; keep only train/other rulings not already served by a dedicated template for the training-rule part; freeze an ID-and-date manifest in `eval/splits/` before the first call. Cases dated before 2023 see only earlier rulings in the same set as precedents; both arms get identical retrieval.
- **Runs.** One control and one `-food-rules` arm through the approved gateway with `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, same code, model, facts, split and workers. The ~16-ruling small set is directional only; no accuracy claim or enablement follows from it alone.
- **Report and decision.** `eval/accuracy/measure_food_independent.py` pairs the committed result files, reports Wilson 95% intervals and exact two-sided McNemar, and lists gained/lost IDs. Its `--self-test` is in `make reproduce`. A later decision records enable/no-enable; until then the server does not wire `CaseRules` and no number is published.
- **Cost if wrong.** Calling D857 an accuracy gain, or scoring a split whose provenance is unknown, would claim what the test cannot support.
- **Evidence.** `docs/issues/` protocol in #823; `eval/accuracy/measure_food_independent.py`.

## D887 — Self-service API keys: the verified account owns the key (25 Nov, #788)
- **Decision.** A signed-in user creates a named key through `POST /v1/api-keys`, sees it in `/settings`, and revokes it through `DELETE /v1/api-keys/{id}`. The owner is `identity.owner`, set from `userOwner(u.Email)` when the sign-in token is verified (D69's account owner, not `keyOwner(k)`, which hashes a key id for case ownership), and is an internal field (`json:"-"`): a request body cannot set it, the wire never returns it, and a Firestore equality query on `owner` needs no composite index. The quota is fixed at **200 requests per UTC day**; a `daily_quota` in the body is refused. Admin-issued keys keep their own path and quota, have no owner, and are invisible to the self-service list and revoke.
- **Reach.** The secret returns once from create; the stored record and later list carry only id, name, creation time, quota and status. Revoked keys stay listed with `disabled: true`. A borrowed, admin or unknown id is a 404 on revoke, so ids cannot be probed. Keys work through the existing `X-API-Key` REST header and `Authorization: Bearer` MCP route, with the same case isolation, limits, spend cap and audit as admin keys. The self-service routes need both `API_KEYS` and `TEAMS` and are 404 otherwise.
- **Audit.** Issue, list and revoke are recorded as `apikey.issue`, `apikey.list` and `apikey.disable` in the requester's tenant, with a pseudonymous user actor. No owner, hash or secret enters the trail. The three routes are `noCaseData` in the isolation matrix and id probes are denied before an intent is stored. A probe of another account's or an admin key's stored id is recorded as a hidden denial with an opaque object; an unknown id is a plain 404 with nothing recorded.
- **Cost if wrong.** Taking an owner from the body would let one account revoke or enumerate another's keys; returning the secret more than once would turn a listing into a credential leak. A quota field would let one user bypass the shared limit policy.
- **Evidence.** `apikey.Store.ListByOwner` / `DisableForOwner`, `httpapi.issueOwnAPIKey` / `listOwnAPIKeys` / `disableOwnAPIKey`, `docs/api/openapi.yaml`, `/settings`, `docs/MCP.md`, `docs/api/SECURITY.md`.

## D900 — Precedent support as a triage gate, pre-registered (25 Nov)
Committed and pushed before any figure on the fit set was read. This lane takes D900–D919 (D850–D869 is used up; the Japan session holds D870–D899). No model calls in D900–D901.
- **Why.** On D860's development control, read offline while looking for levers (so development is not untouched): when none of a case's five precedents held the predicted country, 112 of 133 answers were right (84%); when all five did, 80 of 81 (99%). Answers whose precedents were on average under 6 months older than the case were right 94% of the time, against 85–87% for older ones. Calibration (D160) uses stated confidence only.
- **The change considered.** A second triage gate beside the calibrated-confidence gate (`triage.AllGates`): an answer is auto-accepted only when it also has precedent support. It never changes an answer; it only sends weakly supported ones to review.
- **Gates, fixed now** (`eval/accuracy/measure_900.py`). agree = how many of the five precedents held the predicted country; age = mean months between the case and its precedents. S1: agree ≥ 1. S2: agree ≥ 2. A12: age ≤ 12. S1A6: agree ≥ 1 or age ≤ 6.
- **Fit and pick.** Fit on the 623 training rows of D860's check control (unread for this purpose). Among gates that keep at least 85% of the auto-accepted fit rows, pick the one that removes the most auto-accepted errors (ties: fewer rows removed). Auto-accepted = in scope and stated confidence ≥ 0.92, the same cases as calibrated ≥ 0.90 on this engine (D160).
- **Test.** The official development run (`dev-…-vertex`, primary) and D815's and D860's development controls. **Passes** when on the primary the picked gate cuts auto-accepted errors by at least 30% and lowers auto-accepted coverage by at most 10 points, and raises auto-accepted accuracy in both secondary runs. Held-out is not read.
- **What follows.** If it passes: the gate goes into production triage (`triage.SupportGate`, configurable, on by default), with its reason shown, in a separate decision. If not, nothing changes.

## D901 — Precedent support as a triage gate: results of D900
`eval/accuracy/900-measure.json` (`measure_900.py`, in `make reproduce`); no model calls.
- **Fit (623 training rows; 477 auto-accepted, 32 wrong, 93.3%).** S1 keeps 327 (15 wrong), S2 234 (6 wrong), A12 421 (25 wrong), S1A6 396 (20 wrong). Only A12 keeps 85% of the auto-accepted rows, so **A12 is picked** (precedents on average at most 12 months older than the case).
- **Test, official development run:** auto-accepted 376 (16 wrong, 95.7%, 80.2% coverage) → 320 (13 wrong, 95.9%, 68.2%). Errors cut 19% (30% needed), coverage down 11.9 points (10 allowed). Secondary runs: D815's control 95.5% → 95.4%, D860's 95.8% → 95.7%. **Criterion: not met.** Nothing changes in production.
- **Every gate, for the record (official run, auto-accepted, wrong):** none 376/16; S1 287/11; S2 216/8; A12 320/13; S1A6 324/12. Each removes about 10–20 right answers per wrong one.
- **Reading.** The support signal is strong over all answers (D900: 84% with no supporting precedent, 99% with five) but weak among auto-accepted ones: the confidence bar already sends most weakly supported errors to review. As a gate it costs far more coverage than it saves errors. It stays a diagnostic. Not tried, and not pre-registered here: support as an input to the calibration map itself.
## D902 — Precedent support inside the confidence score, pre-registered (25 Nov)
Committed and pushed before the fit. No model calls. D901 found that support as a separate gate costs too much coverage; this tests it as part of the score that decides auto-accept.
- **Score** (`eval/accuracy/measure_902.py`). Logistic regression on stated confidence, agree/5 and capped mean precedent age (as D900), with an intercept, fitted on the 623 training rows of D860's check control (target: answer right), L2 1e-3, deterministic Newton steps.
- **Test at matched coverage.** In each development run, keep the number of auto-accepted answers today's rule gives (in scope, stated ≥ 0.92) and take that many in-scope answers by the new score instead; count the wrong ones. Same coverage, so a gain is fewer wrong answers auto-accepted.
- **Passes** when on the official development run it auto-accepts at least 3 fewer wrong answers (16 today), and in D815's and D860's controls no more, and fewer in at least one.
- **If it passes**, wiring it into production calibration is a separate decision. **If not**, D904 tests recency in retrieval, as asked.
## D903 — Precedent support inside the confidence score: results of D902
`eval/accuracy/902-measure.json` (in `make reproduce`); no model calls. Fitted weights: confidence 18.15, agree 0.78, age −1.45, intercept −14.92 (support adds little next to confidence).
- **Matched coverage, wrong answers auto-accepted (today → support score):** official development run 16 → 19 (376 auto-accepted; 12 swapped); D815's control 17 → 17; D860's control 16 → 19. **Criterion: not met**; it is worse. Nothing changes.
- **Reading.** With D901: precedent support predicts errors over all answers but not among confident ones, as a gate or inside the score. Closed. Next, as asked: recency in retrieval (D904).
## D904 — Recency in retrieval, pre-registered (25 Nov)
Committed and pushed before the runs. Development only; held-out is not read.
- **Why.** On D860's development control, cases whose precedents were on average under 6 months older were right 94% of the time, against 85–87% for older ones (D900), and the fish rulings of D859 showed CBP practice changing over years. The age signal may only mark rare products, so this tests whether preferring newer precedents helps.
- **The change, eval-only (`retrieval.Recency`, `recency-v1`).** BM25's top 20 candidates are re-scored by 1 + 0.10·exp(−months/12), where months is how much older the precedent is than the case: +10% for a same-month ruling, +3.7% at a year, +1.4% at two years. Then the top 5 are kept. It only reorders near ties. `eval run -retrieval recency`; the server is unchanged.
- **Reach** (`eval retrdiff -recency`, `904-retrdiff.json`, offline). 296 of 469 development cases change: 172 get at least one different precedent, 124 only a different order. So both arms run on all 469.
- **Runs, gateway only** (gemini-4-argon, `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, clean committed tree, results committed after each). From `backend/` with `-split dev -facts data/facts`: control `-tag 904-control`, variant `-retrieval recency -tag 904-recency`.
- **Measured** (`measure_904.py`, written before): paired gained, lost and exact McNemar, Wilson intervals, on all 469 and split into new-precedent, order-only and unchanged cases.
- **Criteria.** **Helped:** net +4 or better on all 469 (identical prompts moved ±2 between runs in D857). **Harms:** net −4 or worse. Otherwise **no detectable effect**. Helped would justify a separate decision on production retrieval.
- **Expectation.** No detectable effect is likeliest; D22's retrieval variants did not move accuracy.
- **Cost.** About $7.5 for both runs; cap $12.
## D905 — Recency in retrieval: results of D904
Runs as pre-registered (`dev-…-904-control`, `dev-gemini-4-argon-recency30-engine-v1-litellm-904-recency`; gateway, clean tree); `eval/accuracy/904-measure.json` (in `make reproduce`). One failed call in the variant (N350720, "unchanged", counted wrong).
- **All 469: 421 → 422** (89.8% → 90.0%); 6 gained, 5 lost, McNemar p = 1.0. New precedent (172): 148 → 149. Order only (124): 111 → 112. Unchanged (173): 162 → 161, the failed call.
- **Criterion, as D904 stated: no detectable effect** (net +1; ±4 needed either way). Production retrieval stays BM25.
- **Reading.** Preferring newer precedents among near ties changes the precedents of most cases and the answers of almost none; the age signal of D900 marks harder cases, not worse retrieval. With D901 and D903, the support and recency signals are closed.
- **Cost.** $3.69 and $3.68.
## D906 — Authenticated live ADK evaluation: results of D732 (25 Nov)
Run as D732 pre-registered: a01–a12 once each, batches of three, 25 Nov 2026 17:05–17:48 +08:00, live `https://undelabs.dev/mcp` with an evaluator-scoped API key as a bearer credential (`--require-bearer`), agent on Gemini 3.8 Flash through the LiteLLM gateway. Rows `eval/agent/results/live-v2-authenticated-run1.jsonl`, scored by `eval/agent/score.py` unchanged. The key was kept in a local 0600 file and loaded only into the eval process; the rows hold no key, no gateway host and no case key (checked). A first invocation at 16:55 started no session: a shell loop passed each batch's three ids as one and `run_eval.py` stopped on the unknown id before any network call, so no product ran twice.
- **10/12 passed every D510 check** (D450 rules: 8/12; a03 and a05 drafted the current setup after no plan, which D510 counts right). Both no-plan answers say no move is supported and the origin stands, read by hand; the scorer agrees.
- **The two failures.** a06: the agent's first `predict_origin` call broke the input schema (an operation name over the length limit), the second worked, and a repeated call fails tool order (an agent error). a07: `extract_product` returned 502 `model_unavailable`, a production model-provider outage, and the agent stopped and said so (a server error, counted as the rules say).
- **Against run 1 (anonymous, 22 Nov, D511):** 9/12 then, 10/12 now; a01–a08 passed 8/8 then and 6/8 now (a06, a07 above); a09–a12, cut by the anonymous budget in run 1, all passed now. Private-case auth, the 22 Nov to 25 Nov server changes and production load prevent a controlled repeat; this is descriptive, as D732 says.
- **Time and cost.** Median 492 s per run (166–796 s); live plan searches took 6–13 minutes. Agent $0.5361 gateway-reported (D732 cap $1.5811). The server's own model calls ran on production's model path and budget; their cost was not observed from here.
## D907 — A 2019–2022 pool of older New York rulings as retrieval precedents, pre-registered (25 Nov, #839)
Committed and pushed before the pool is labelled and before the runs. Development only; held-out is not read.
- **Why.** Since D22 every prompt, retrieval, model and voting change has landed within about ±1 point (D850–D905). The precedent pool starts in 2023, so a product that CBP last ruled on before then has no precedent at all. D869's 15 older rulings reached 16 of 469 development cases and moved one; this tests the idea at full size.
- **Fetching.** `corpus probe` walks New York ruling numbers N301000–N326500 (about January 2019 to early 2023) at about one request a second per stream, three streams, on 25–26 Nov 2026. CROSS search answers 403 and is not used. Every number tried and CROSS's answer is kept in the probe index; a ruling is saved when its category line names origin or its text says "country of origin", as in D150. Headquarters rulings are numbered at intake and are not walked.
- **The pool.** `corpus final2-label` labels every saved ruling dated 2019-01-01 to 2022-12-31 that is not already in `labels.jsonl`, `labels_usmca.jsonl` or `labels_cited.jsonl`, with the regex labeller and regime rule that reproduce `labels.jsonl` (D150's check: held origin 1,620/1,620 on substantial-transformation rows, regime precision 97.6%, recall 98.4%). All regimes are kept, as in the production pool; there are no manual corrections. Output `backend/data/labels_older.jsonl` and `backend/data/facts_older/`, frozen (committed) before either run.
- **The change, eval-only.** The pool joins BM25's precedent pool: `-labels ../eval/data/labels.jsonl,data/labels_older.jsonl -facts data/facts,data/facts_older`. Precedents stay strictly earlier than the case, and every development case is from 2023 or later. The server is unchanged.
- **Reach** (`eval retrdiff`, offline, written to `eval/accuracy/907-retrdiff.json` before the runs): which cases retrieve an older ruling, which only reorder. Both arms run on all 469, as in D904, because a large pool shifts term weights for most cases.
- **Runs, gateway only** (gemini-4-argon, `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, clean committed tree, results committed after each). From `backend/` with `-split dev`: control `-facts data/facts -tag 907-control`; variant `-labels ../eval/data/labels.jsonl,data/labels_older.jsonl -facts data/facts,data/facts_older -tag 907-older`.
- **Measured** (`eval/accuracy/measure_907.py`, written before): paired gained, lost and exact McNemar, Wilson intervals, on all 469 and split into cases with an older ruling, order-only and unchanged.
- **Criteria.** **Helped:** net +4 or better on all 469 (identical prompts moved ±2 between runs in D857). **Harms:** net −4 or worse. Otherwise **no detectable effect**. Helped would justify a separate decision on the production pool and a held-out check.
- **Expectation.** 1–3 points at best, possibly nothing.
- **Cost.** The probe has no model cost. About $7.5 for both runs; cap $12.
## D908 — Older-ruling precedent pool: results of D907 (26 Nov)
Runs as pre-registered (`dev-…-907-control`, `dev-…-907-older`; gateway, clean tree, 26 Nov 06:09–06:52 +08:00); `eval/accuracy/907-measure.json` (in `make reproduce`). One failed call in the variant (N353851, "unchanged", counted wrong; right in the control). A first attempt on 25 Nov returned no model output (the gateway refused every call) and its rows were removed before these runs.
- **The pool.** The probe tried 25,501 numbers; 1,507 saved rulings are dated 2019-02-05 to 2022-06-22 (2019: 464, 2020: 538, 2021: 338, 2022: 167), and 1,388 not already labelled form `labels_older.jsonl` (substantial transformation 683, other 305, Part 102 158, single country 119, pharmaceutical 114, 9802 9; 448 with no single held origin).
- **Reach.** 261 of 469 cases change; 203 retrieve at least one older ruling, 58 only reorder. The variant cites an older ruling in 97 cases.
- **All 469: 422 → 420** (90.0% → 89.6%), McNemar p = 0.81. With an older ruling (203): 170 → 172, 8 gained and 6 lost, p = 0.79. Order only (58): 55 → 52. Unchanged (208): 197 → 196, the failed call.
- **Criterion, as D907 stated: no detectable effect** (net −2; ±4 needed either way). The production pool stays 2023 onward; no held-out check.
- **Reading.** Older rulings reach almost half the development cases and are cited in a fifth of them, yet answers move no more than between identical runs (D857). A missing precedent was not what made the model wrong; with D901, D903 and D905, the retrieval levers tried since D22 are closed. The pool has a gap: nothing from July to December 2022, the months just before the production pool starts.
- **Cost.** $3.70 and $3.69.
## D912 — South Korea and Australia as RCEP rules-check markets; no "soon" markets in the picker (26 Nov)
- **Decision.** South Korea and Australia are registered as rules-only markets (`httpapi.RCEPAuthority`). A case for either gets the RCEP check (Chapter 3, Annex 3A) from the product's codes, as the Canada, EU and UK markets get theirs: no model, no rulings, every answer for review. A good that qualifies takes the origin of the Party where it was produced (Art. 3.2). Parts from outside RCEP are non-originating; parts from a Party are "not known to be originating" (Art. 3.5.4), so the answer never assumes a supplier declaration.
- **Why these two.** Neither publishes origin rulings (Korea: 18 all-rights-reserved pre-reviews; Australia: confidential), so a ruling-based engine cannot be built or tested. Both are RCEP Parties and RCEP's product-specific rules are common to all Parties, so the existing RCEP check (71 of 98 held-out Japan Customs approvals found, deciding criterion right in 71 of 71, D717) applies unchanged.
- **Picker.** Only supported markets are listed; the "soon" label and the "Other markets: not yet" line are removed. A case whose text names an unsupported market still gets the plain "not supported" answer.
- **Not claimed.** No Korean or Australian decision tests these answers; preference qualification is not marking or non-preferential origin.
## D911 — Canada, EU and UK rules checks scored against decided cases (26 Nov)
The three rules-only markets had no score. Neither publishes a usable ruling corpus (CBSA: 14 rulings under a no-redistribution licence; EU BOI: no facts; UK AORs: unpublished), so each is scored on the best decided cases that state facts and outcome. Deterministic checks, no model call; nothing was tuned on these cases, and they were not pre-registered.
- **Canada** (`eval/markets/canada-cbp-part102.json`): Canada's SOR/94-23 Schedule III table on the inputs already read from 104 CBP Part 102 rulings (D360/D361; goods processed in Canada or Mexico, CBP's holding as gold). **Decided 29 of 104; agrees 26 of 29** (89.7%, 73.6–96.4). The 3 that differ (H339179, H341021, N356375) are rows where Schedule III is wider than 19 CFR 102.20 ("from any other good of that subheading"), so Canada's text gives a different answer from CBP's; the rows were read by hand. 75 are undetermined, almost all for missing material codes. The U.S. 102.20 table on the same inputs decides 12, all agreeing. This tests the rule table on real facts, not Canadian practice.
- **EU and UK** (`eval/markets/eu-uk/cases.jsonl`, `eval/markets/eu-uk-cases.json`): 16 cases built from CJEU judgments, Commission guidance examples and UK tribunal decisions; each input quotes the source, 14 have an inferred code or share. Under the current rules (Annex 22-01, Part Four), 6 cases: **1 decided, agreeing; 5 go to a person** (no list rule for the chapter, or a fact the codes cannot show). The 10 decided under the pre-2016 rules: 2 decided by the current table and both differ (Thomson, Vestel: today's 8528 rule is CTH except 8529, where the old Annex 11 rule was 45% value added), 8 go to a person.
- **Reading.** Canada's check answers about one case in four from ruling text and is right on its own rule text when it does. The EU and UK checks almost never answer a disputed case: the disputes are about goods with no list rule, where the law sends origin to the general test. That is the honest limit of a rules-only check for those markets; their answers stay "for review".
- **Recompute.** `go run ./cmd/marketeval canada -check` and `euuk -check`, in `make reproduce`.
## D909 — Japan: what the D870–D885 campaign did to answers, pre-registered (26 Nov)
Committed and pushed before any model call. Design A of `docs/japan/prospective-evaluation-plan.md`: regression on the development set, not a held-out figure. The D741 held-out set stays burned and is not read.
- **Why.** The campaign raised rule coverage on `dev_eval` from 366 to 396 of 400 requests (D885) but measured no answers. Japan is listed as supported while its last measured figures are 243 of 400 development (D712) and 260 of 633 held-out (D741).
- **Run.** `jp-engine-v1` unchanged, `gemini-4-argon` through the LiteLLM gateway, `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, at the commit of this entry: `go run ./cmd/jpeval candidate -split dev_eval -tag d909-dev`. Plan at this tree: 396 requests, 9,279,221 request bytes, `requests_sha256` 2d5b8b49…; worst case $51 at the D741 rates ($2/$10 per million, unverified estimate), expected about $5.
- **Measured** as D712: criterion match, positive recall, named-origin match, all out of 400 with every abstention and error counted, paired against D712's rows (gained, lost, exact McNemar).
- **Criteria.** **Improved:** criterion match net +8 or better (about 2 points). **Worse:** net −8 or worse. Otherwise no detectable change. A provider or gateway change since 23 Nov is a confound and is reported, not corrected.
- **What follows.** The misses of this run are read (development only) to design `jp-engine-v2`, which gets its own pre-registration and a test with negatives, so a prompt that answers "qualifies" more often cannot pass on positives alone.
## D910 — Japan: the D870–D885 campaign, results of D909 (26 Nov)
Run as pre-registered (`jp-dev_eval-gemini-4-argon-jp-engine-v1-litellm-d909-dev`, gateway, 26 Nov; the ledger tooling commit after D909 changed no request, `requests_sha256` 2d5b8b49… as planned). Development set only; held-out not read.
- **Criterion match 243 → 272 of 400** (60.8% → 68.0%, 63.3–72.4); 30 gained, 1 lost, exact McNemar p < 0.001. Positive recall 244 → 273. Named origin 177 → 187 of 292 including the EU; named country 51 → 58 of 111. No errors (1 in D712).
- **Criterion, as D909 stated: improved** (net +29; +8 needed). The campaign's rule text turned abstentions into answers; the prompt is unchanged.
- **What is still wrong (read for v2).** 127 undetermined: JP-EU EPA 52, AJCEP 30, CPTPP 19, GSP 7 (GSP never answers "qualifies", by design). Most are refusals where an intermediate material of the good's own chapter or heading (footwear counters and insoles, rice-bran ferment) is listed without a stated originating status, although the facts describe it being made in the exporting Party from materials that do shift. That is a prompt-level gap, not missing rule text.
- **Limits.** Development rulings only, all of them published approvals, so this run cannot show wrong approvals; the gateway model may differ from production's Vertex path.
- **Cost.** $5.47 gateway-reported.
## D913 — Japan jp-engine-v2: intermediate materials, tested with negatives, pre-registered (26 Nov)
Committed and pushed before any v2 call and before the v1 negatives run. Development only.
- **Why.** D910 left 127 of 400 development approvals undetermined; most refuse because a material of the good's own chapter or heading has no stated originating status although the facts say the producer made it in the exporting Party. A prompt that answers "qualifies" more often would also pass on approvals alone, so v2 is tested on negatives too.
- **Negatives (`dev_neg`).** `jpeval dev-negatives` takes the first 80 `dev_eval` approvals (by id) decided under CC, CTH or CTSH, outside GSP, and appends one fact: a non-originating semi-finished article of the good's own six-digit code, from Brazil (party to none of the agreements), incorporated without further working and worth 70% of the ex-works price. That fails every tariff-shift rule, the listed value thresholds and de minimis, so the right answer is anything but "qualifies". File `eval/jp/dev-negatives.jsonl`, committed here.
- **The change (v2, prompt only; `PromptVersion` jp-engine-v2).** Two sentences added after "Do not assume a material is originating…": "When the facts say the producer itself made a material in the exporting Party from other listed materials, treat it as an intermediate material and apply the rule to the materials it was made from. Treat a material whose originating status is not stated as non-originating and decide whether the rule is still met; answer undetermined only when a tariff code, value or production fact the rule needs is missing." And one after "For a qualifying outcome…": "The origin country of a qualifying good is the Party where it was produced, not a material's country."
- **Runs** (gateway, `gemini-4-argon`, `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`): v1 on `dev_neg` (`-tag d913-neg-v1`) at this commit; then v2 on `dev_eval` (`-tag d913-dev-v2`) and `dev_neg` (`-tag d913-neg-v2`).
- **Criteria for adopting v2.** (1) `dev_eval` criterion match net +8 or better against D909's 272 (paired, exact McNemar reported); and (2) v2 wrong approvals on `dev_neg` at most v1's plus 2, and at most 8 of 80. Both or v1 stays. No held-out figure follows from this; the D741 set stays burned.
- **Cost.** About $7.7 for three runs.
## D915 — Japan jp-engine-v2: results of D913, not adopted (26 Nov)
Runs as pre-registered (gateway, 26 Nov): `d913-neg-v1`, `d913-neg-v2`, `d913-dev-v2`. Development only.
- **Negatives (80).** v1 approved 0 and v2 approved 0 (v2: 67 declined, 13 undetermined; v1: 62 and 18). Criterion (2) passes.
- **Development approvals (400).** v2 criterion match **269**, against v1's 272 in D909: 2 gained, 5 lost, McNemar p = 0.45. v2 also declined 14 published approvals outright, which v1 never did. Named origin 187 → 186 of 292. Criterion (1), net +8, **fails**.
- **Decision.** v1 stays; the prompt is back to `jp-engine-v1`, word for word. The intermediate-materials instruction moved answers from "undetermined" to wrong refusals as often as to right approvals. With food-v1 (D858) and china-v1 (D861), this is the third prompt-text rule that did not help; the gains in D910 came from rule text the model is given.
- **What it leaves.** Japan stands at 272 of 400 development approvals (68%) with no wrong approval on 80 constructed negatives. The negatives file and `dev_neg` split stay for any later change.
- **Cost.** $0.94, $0.98 and $5.62.
## D914 — Mexico as a rules-only market: the non-preferential origin rules (26 Nov)
- **Decision.** Mexico is registered as a rules-only market (`httpapi.MexicoAuthority`), like Canada (D725). A case for Mexico gets the check of Mexico's own country-of-origin rules from the product's codes: no model, no rulings, every answer for review.
- **Source.** The Acuerdo on rules for determining the country of origin of imported goods (DOF 30-08-1994), Anexo I articles 3 to 7 and its Apéndice de Reglas Específicas, from the SNICE consolidation (Word file dated 1 August 2016; the rows were last amended by DOF 16-10-2008). It applies to goods from any country, for non-preferential purposes (quotas, trade remedies, marking). The Word file and its text export are not committed; `rules_mx.json` keeps each row's Spanish text (`text_es`) with its SHA-256. Licence: DOF texts, cited to the DOF; legal texts are outside copyright under Mexican law (LFDA art. 14 VIII); no reuse terms were found for SNICE.
- **How rows are read.** `go run ./cmd/tariffshift rules-mx` renders each Spanish row into the English phrasing the existing parser reads by a fixed list of replacements (partida → heading, "de cualquier otra partida" → "from any other heading", and so on). A row with any Spanish left keeps its Spanish text and is never decided by code. 943 rows (deleted rows left out); 788 are encoded (83.6%), 155 are not (provisos on content or process, goods described by words, two alternatives in one row). The general rules differ from 19 CFR 102 in one way the check applies: the text has no de minimis rule, so none is applied.
- **Score** (`eval/markets/mexico-cbp-part102.json`, as D911 scored Canada): Mexico's table on the inputs read from 104 CBP Part 102 rulings. **Decided 16; agrees with CBP's holding in 16 of 16** (80.6–100). 75 are undetermined (missing material codes), 13 fall in chapters 1 to 24, which have no rows. This tests the rule table on real facts, not Mexican practice.
- **Limits.** The rows are in the HS 2007 edition (2008 amendment), so a code from a later edition may match no row or the wrong one. Chapters 1 to 24 have no specific rules: origin there is the last substantial transformation with a change of classification (art. 3 II), which a person judges. Not preferential origin (USMCA or other agreements) and not a marking ruling.
## D917 — Japan asks for the missing facts instead of only saying "needs more evidence" (26 Nov)
- **Decision.** When the Japan check cannot decide, the result now carries up to five questions, built from the case without a model call: for each part, whether it has proof of origin under the chosen agreement (Yes, No, Not sure), or where it is made when that is blank; the production steps when none are listed; and, for a case with no parts list, one typed question about the materials without proof of origin. The page shows them in one card with a single "Check again". The answers go through the existing `POST /v1/cases/{id}/answers`, which adds them to the case facts and runs the check again; "Not sure" adds nothing. A question already answered is not asked again. After the re-check the heading shows what it was before.
- **Why.** Most undetermined development answers (D910) stop on a part whose origin status the facts never state. The user usually knows it, and asking is cheaper than a specialist reading the case.
- **Fixed on the way.** Re-running a Japan case after answers or a new parts list dropped its agreement and tariff code, so the re-run could only answer "choose the trade agreement"; both paths now keep them.
- **Not changed.** The `jp-engine-v1` prompt, the rule text and GSP (its answer turns on the beneficiary country, so it gets no part questions). The local fake model now returns "undetermined" for a case with a parts list and no answers, so the card can be tried without a model; production refuses the fake.
- **Not measured.** No evaluation shows how often an answered question turns into a right decision; the development rulings carry no user answers.

## D919 — Japan: rulings published after the 22 Nov snapshot, pre-registered measurement (26 Nov)
Committed and pushed before any model call on these cases. A measurement, not an adoption decision: nothing in production changes whatever the result.
- **Data.** The Japan Customs list was read again on 26 Nov (3,599 results, against 3,606 on 22 Nov). 44 rulings are new (issued 14 May to 13 Nov 2026; RCEP 18, JP-EU EPA 11, CPTPP 9, JP-Indonesia EPA 4, JP-UK CEPA 1, AJCEP 1) and are kept in `data/jp/fresh-1126/` (rulings, translations, labels, snapshot). 51 rulings are no longer listed; they stay in the frozen corpus. `data/jp/rulings.jsonl`, `splits.json` and every existing label are unchanged. Translations: `eval/jp/translate.py --data data/jp/fresh-1126`, $0.08. Labels: `eval/jp/labels.py --fresh`, written without being read.
- **Near-duplicates.** 41 of the 44 are repeat requests: an earlier ruling has a difflib ratio of at least 0.85 on the Japanese product, inputs, process and reasoning (`eval/jp/fresh_twins.py`, `twins.json`). So this is not a clean test of generalization, and two pools are run.
- **Runs** (gateway, `gemini-4-argon`, `jp-engine-v1`, the D885 evidence, `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, at this commit). `fresh_1126`: precedents from every earlier ruling (dev and held_out), as production retrieves. `fresh_1126_notwin`: the same 44 cases with all 1,167 earlier rulings that are a near-duplicate of any fresh case removed from the pool. Commands: `go run ./cmd/jpeval candidate -split fresh_1126 -tag d919-fresh` and `-split fresh_1126_notwin -tag d919-notwin`. Offline plans: 44 eligible requests each (0 ineligible), `requests_sha256` fa827281… and 62b2f47c…, worst case $5.13 and $5.17.
- **Reported.** Criterion match k/44 with Wilson 95% CI for each run, against development 272/400 (68.0%, D909) and the burned held-out 260/633 (41.1%, D741); by agreement; wrong approvals (a published negative answered "qualifies"); undetermined count; and the same for the 3 cases with no near-duplicate. No threshold: n = 44 is too small to adopt or reject anything.
- **Cost.** About $1 per run.
## D920 — Japan rulings published after 22 Nov: results of D919 (26 Nov)
Runs as pre-registered at b2632d1c (gateway, 26 Nov): `d919-fresh`, `d919-notwin`.
- **Criterion match: 37 of 44 (84.1%, Wilson 95% CI 70.6% to 92.1%) in both runs**, case for case identical. Development D909: 68.0% (272/400). Burned held-out D741: 41.1% (260/633, before the D910 rule text).
- **By agreement.** RCEP 18/18, CPTPP 8/9, JP-Indonesia EPA 4/4, JP-UK CEPA 1/1, JP-EU EPA 6/11, AJCEP 0/1. At the development rates per agreement this mix would be expected to score about 32 of 44, so part of the higher rate is the easier mix (RCEP and CPTPP repeat requests).
- **Near-duplicates do not explain the score.** The no-twin pool showed the model 0 near-duplicate precedents (against 103 of 126 shown in the full pool), with the same 37 correct. The 3 cases with no near-duplicate: 1 correct (JP-UK CTSH), 2 answered "qualifies" with the wrong rule (product-specific instead of CTSH, both JP-EU).
- **Wrong approvals.** All 44 published answers are approvals, so this set cannot measure wrong approvals; D913's 0 of 80 constructed negatives remains the evidence for that.
- **Misses (7).** 5 undetermined (JP-EU 3, CPTPP wholly obtained 1, AJCEP 1) and the 2 wrong-rule approvals above. No case was declined.
- **Reading.** On rulings the system could not have seen, the Japan engine names the right rule in about 5 of 6 cases; n = 44 is small and the set leans to easy agreements. JP-EU stays the weakest agreement, as in development.
- **Cost.** $0.47 and $0.48, plus $0.08 of translation.
## D921 — Japan after one round of question-card answers, pre-registered (26 Nov)
Committed and pushed before any model call. A measurement of the product as a user meets it, not an engine change: `jp-engine-v1`, `gemini-4-argon`, the production evidence, unchanged.
- **Why.** Of the 53 JP-EU EPA misses in D909, 52 are undetermined with "missing production or materials facts". The model sees the case facts only (product, tariff number, agreement, materials list, process); the ruling states which materials are originating only in its reasoning, which the model never sees. Those abstentions are correct. The product's answer is the D917 question card, which asks "Which materials have no proof of origin under <agreement>, and what are their tariff codes?" when a case has no parts list.
- **The answers.** `eval/jp/answer_oracle.py` reads, from each ruling's reasoning, only the sentences before the one that applies the rule, and from them only each numbered material's status (originating, wholly obtained, neutral element, non-originating). It never reads the rule, criterion or conclusion; unreadable sentences give no answer ("Not sure", no fact). Coverage: 3,644 of 3,730 rows (corpus, fresh set and `dev_neg`); 20 hand-checked, 20 correct; unit tests in `eval/jp/test_answer_oracle.py`. For `dev_neg` the added Brazil part is listed with the materials that have no proof of origin.
- **What is re-checked.** Only cases the base run left undetermined, the card asks about (not GSP or non-preferential) and the oracle answers, with the question and answer appended by `clarify.AppendAnswers` exactly as the product does. Every other case keeps its base row, as in the product, where the card shows only on an undetermined result. Base runs (request hashes match today's plan): `dev_eval` D909 `d909-dev` (127 undetermined, 119 re-checked, 116 requests, `requests_sha256` 671c7e44…); `fresh_1126` D919 `d919-fresh` (5 undetermined, 5 re-checked, f1ba1778…); `dev_neg` D913 `d913-neg-v1` (18 undetermined, 18 re-checked, f0c10083…).
- **Runs** (gateway, `LITELLM_NO_CACHE=1`, at the commit of this entry): `go run ./cmd/jpeval candidate -split dev_eval_answered -tag d921-dev`, `-split fresh_1126_answered -tag d921-fresh`, `-split dev_neg_answered -tag d921-neg`.
- **Report** (`eval/jp/answered_summary.py`): criterion match before → after on each full split, gained and lost with exact McNemar, Wilson 95% CI after, by agreement with JP-EU EPA called out, wrong approvals (approved under a criterion that is not the published one) before and after, and `dev_neg` negatives approved (at most 2 of 80 is the bar the engine has met). No adoption decision; a `dev_eval` gain under +8 will be stated as no measurable effect.
- **Also noted.** The 2 fresh JP-EU wrong-rule approvals (3903.90: the model cites the chemical-reaction alternative, Japan Customs CTSH; both are alternatives of the same Annex 3-B rule) and the 1 development JP-EU WO→SP (almonds: "all Chapter 8 materials wholly obtained" against Art. 3.2.1(a)) name a rule that is also met; origin is right, the cited alternative differs. Not changed here.
- **Cost.** Worst case $15.39 + $0.68 + $2.23; expected about $2.5.
## D922 — Japan after one round of question-card answers: results of D921 (26 Nov)
Runs as pre-registered at c6dcbf4d (gateway, 26 Nov): `d921-dev`, `d921-fresh`, `d921-neg`. Summary: `eval/jp/d922-answered-summary.json`.
- **Development (400): criterion match 272 → 374 (93.5%, Wilson 95% CI 90.7% to 95.5%)**, 102 gained, 0 lost (exact McNemar p < 0.001). 119 undetermined cases were re-checked with the answer; 20 stay undetermined.
- **JP-EU EPA: 128 → 179 of 181.** AJCEP 26 → 53 of 56, CPTPP 66 → 78 of 85, RCEP 26 → 28 of 31, JP-US TA 19 → 22 of 22. GSP (7) is never asked and stays at 0.
- **Rulings published after 22 Nov (44): 37 → 42 (95.5%, CI 84.9% to 98.7%)**, 5 gained, 0 lost; JP-EU EPA 6 → 9 of 11. The two left are the 3903.90 cases below.
- **Negatives (80): 0 approved before and after**; of 18 re-checked with the Brazil part listed as having no proof of origin, 6 were declined and 12 stay undetermined.
- **Wrong approvals** (approved under a rule other than the published one): development 1 → 6, fresh 2 → 2. The 5 new ones: 3 WO → PE (RCEP, CPTPP: the published ruling says wholly obtained, the model "produced exclusively from originating materials", given every material originating), 1 CC → CTSH, 1 CTH → the 2009.69 rule's wholly-obtained-grapes condition. In each the good is still found originating.
- **What gained.** By the published rule: CC 47, CTH 21, CTSH 18, specific rule 15, PE 1; 100 of the 102 answers were mixed (some materials originating, the rest not), so the gain is the tariff-shift test run on the right materials, not a restated conclusion.
- **Noted, not changed.** The 2 fresh JP-EU approvals under the 3903.90 chemical-reaction alternative where Japan Customs cites CTSH, and the 1 development JP-EU almonds case (Art. 3.2.1(a) wholly obtained, the model the Chapter 8 rule): the good meets both, and the cited alternative differs.
- **Reading.** Japan's remaining misses were missing facts, not missing rules: once the requester states which materials have proof of origin, which is what the D917 card asks, Japan names the published rule in about 19 of 20 development cases and 42 of 44 unseen ones, with no wrong approval of the constructed negatives. This holds only when the requester answers the card, and the answers here come from the ruling's own statement of the facts the applicant submitted.
- **Cost.** $1.75, $0.08 and $0.26.
## D923 — Canada: published CBSA rulings shown on Canada cases, display only (26 Nov)
- **Source.** The CBSA's public list "Rulings issued by the CBSA" (CARM), published with each applicant's consent. On 26 Nov 2026 it held 1,240 rulings: 1,217 tariff classification, 11 origin advance rulings, 9 valuation and 3 marking national customs rulings. All 14 origin and marking rulings (2015-07-23 to 2024-07-26; CUSMA 5, CPTPP 3, NAFTA 1, CETA 1, Canada–Ukraine 1 for origin; NAFTA and non-CUSMA marking rules for marking) are kept; none is excluded. Classification and valuation rulings are out of scope. Fetched by `eval/ca/fetch.py` (robots.txt allows it; plain client name; 1.2 s apart; no sign-in), parsed by `eval/ca/parse.py` into `data/ca/rulings.jsonl`, embedded in `backend/internal/carulings`. The one-line holding of each ruling is our summary; the full text is the CBSA page.
- **Licence.** Canada.ca Terms and Conditions: non-commercial reproduction with attribution and a link is allowed; commercial reproduction needs the CBSA's permission (`data/ca/LICENSE-SOURCE.md`). Before commercial use of this data, get that permission.
- **What a Canada case shows.** Up to three related rulings, deterministically: same subheading, then heading, then chapter of the good's code; without a code match, a ruling needs two words in common with the product and its parts, one of them in the ruling's product name; ties go to the newer ruling. None when nothing relates. Shown under the SOR/94-23 check as "CBSA rulings", one line each (holding, product, date, link). Also on the API as `prediction.canada_rulings`.
- **Display only.** The rulings play no part in the rules-check answer, its confidence or its route (test `TestCanadaCaseShowsCBSARulings`). Most are preferential-origin rulings under a trade agreement, a different question from marking origin under SOR/94-23; the agreement is shown with each.
- **No accuracy claim.** Fourteen rulings, three of them marking, are too few to test the check against; the Canada label now says "too few published rulings" instead of "no published rulings".

## D927 — ATIGA preferential origin check, behind `ATIGA_CHECK` (off), pre-registered reference test (27 Nov, #878)
- **What.** `backend/internal/atiga`: deterministic ATIGA (ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement) origin from a bill of materials, modelled on the RCEP check (D690). `POST /v1/atiga/check` and the MCP tool `check_atiga_preference`, both served only with `ATIGA_CHECK=on` (default off: production unchanged). No model call, nothing stored.
- **Source, pinned.** Annex 3 product-specific rules, HS 2022 (endorsed by the 36th AFTA Council, in force 1 April 2023): the ASEAN Secretariat workbook `ATIGA-PSR-HS-2022-endorsed-AFTAC36.xlsx`, SHA-256 bb4d6a6f…ba07, 2,868 rows kept verbatim (code, description, concise and full text) in `backend/internal/atiga/data/psr_hs2022.json`, read by `eval/atiga/parse_psr.py` (standard library; `check` re-reads every rule from the stored text). Every parsed requirement was cross-checked against the row's full text (0 mismatches). Agreement text: ATIGA (Cha-am, 26 February 2009), SHA-256 46c6d336…f6, Articles 25 to 37; Annex 6 (partial cumulation) a38dc731…5195362; Attachment 1 (textiles) 60ea8486…af16. The workbooks and PDFs are not committed.
- **Implemented.** Art. 26 and 27; Art. 28.1 general rule (RVC40 or CTH) for the subheadings Annex 3 does not list; Art. 28.2 Annex 3 rules: RVC40, CC/CTH/CTSH with "except from" headings or subheadings, RVC35 with CTSH, eight product-dependent rows as variants, and six conditions written in words (textile process rule, cut and sewn in a Member State, refining, wet to dry, recording, parts of the same subheading), which the caller states; Art. 29 direct and indirect RVC (Art. 29.3: `method` limits it to the exporting Member State's); Art. 30.1 cumulation; Art. 30.2 and Annex 6 partial cumulation (a Member State material with its own RVC from 20 % to under 40 % adds that share of its value, RVC criterion only); Art. 31 minimal operations; Art. 33 de minimis (10 % of FOB, value only). Missing facts are undetermined, never no.
- **Not implemented.** Art. 28.3 and Annex 4 (ITA goods), Art. 32 direct consignment, Art. 34 to 37, the Attachment 1 textile list itself, proof-of-origin procedures. Timor-Leste (ASEAN since October 2025) is not treated as an ATIGA party. The First Protocol (2019) is a scanned PDF and was not read; it is not known to change Chapter 3.
- **Published decisions.** None found: no ASEAN Member State publishes ATIGA origin rulings (searches 27 Nov; the OECD 2025 ASEAN trade facilitation review recommends publishing them). So no accuracy figure is possible.
- **Pre-registered reference test.** `eval/atiga/reference-cases.json`: 7 worked examples published by authorities (MITI Malaysia examples 1 to 5; Singapore Customs handbook, Dec 2025, examples B and F), each with the result the source states, written and pushed before the check was run on them. Pass: the outcome (and, where the source states it, the alternative, the RVC and accumulation) matches. Where Annex 3 has changed since the example was written (MITI examples 3 and 5 predate the HS 2022 table), the check must still reach the stated outcome, and the rule that decided is reported.
- **Results (run after the pre-registration was pushed at 1103d2ba).** 7 of 7 examples reach the outcome the source states. Every pre-registered alternative, accumulation and RVC check passed except one number: Singapore Customs example B prints RVC 36 %, while its own figures give 36.67 % both ways, so the pre-registered range (35.9 to 36.1) copied the source's rounding down; the stated result, RVC40 not met, matches. With today's Annex 3, MITI examples 3 to 5 are decided by the Art. 28.1 general rule (their goods are no longer listed), and every one also qualifies by RVC40; example 5 (copper wire from brass wire of the same heading) no longer qualifies by a tariff change, only by RVC (73.4 %). These are worked examples, not rulings: this shows the arithmetic and the rule reading agree with the authorities' teaching material, not that the check matches customs decisions.
- **Cost.** No model spend.

## D924 — Audit export, workspace case retention, SOC 2 / ISO 27001 controls map (27 Nov, #871, #875, #876)
Backend only, both features off by default; production behaviour is unchanged until an operator sets the flags.
- **Audit export (#871).** `AUDIT_EXPORT=on` registers `GET /v1/audit/export` (same readers as `GET /v1/audit`). JSONL: a header with the head and retention checkpoint read first (a snapshot), events as stored with their chain hashes, and a summary with the count and the SHA-256 of the bytes before it; CSV has the same columns. `cmd/auditverify` re-checks a JSONL file offline with the chain rules of `verify` (exit 0 intact, 1 findings, 2 unreadable). A store error mid-stream leaves no summary, so a cut file never verifies. New action `audit.export` (details `jsonl`, `csv`). The trail already existed (#284); export adds no immutability: it is a copy the customer keeps.
- **Case retention (#875).** `RETENTION=on` (with `TEAMS=on`): `GET` and `PUT /v1/workspaces/{id}/retention` (`case_days` 0 or 7 to 3650; setting it is a sensitive `workspace.retention` write) and `GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/tombstones` (admins). `cmd/retention` is a dry run unless `-apply`; it deletes the workspace's cases not updated for `case_days`, oldest first, writing a tombstone and then a system `case.delete` event (detail `retention`) before each hard delete, and never touches pinned demo cases or cases outside a workspace. A user's delete of a workspace case also leaves a tombstone. Tombstones hold the case ID, dates, reason and policy, no content. The operator schedules the command; the server runs no timer. Not done: caches derived from case facts are still not purged with the case (data-handling.md item 7), and audit retention stays one global setting.
- **SOC 2 / ISO 27001 (#876).** `docs/compliance/soc2-iso27001-controls.md` maps each Trust Services criterion and the matching Annex A controls to the evidence in this repository and lists the gaps, most of them owner actions (policies, auditor, period, access reviews, vendor reports, backups). No report or certificate is claimed.
- **Checks.** New tests: export round trip, edit/drop/truncation detection, snapshot, window, cap and post-purge anchoring; purge (expiry, pinned, dry run, limit, tombstone-before-delete, audit failure stops the delete); routes (access, 404 with flags off, fail-closed retention write, user-delete tombstone); both commands end to end on the file store. No model spend.

## D925 — Broker workflow: review queue, collaboration and an eRulings-ready filing package, behind BROKER_WORKFLOW (27 Nov, #879, #881, #882)
- **Decision.** Ship the backend of three roadmap items behind one flag, `BROKER_WORKFLOW` (on|off, default off: the routes are not registered, production is unchanged). API only; no screens. Design: docs/design/broker-workflow.md.
- **Review queue (#881).** `PUT /v1/cases/{id}/queue`, `POST /v1/cases/{id}/queue/transition`, `GET /v1/queue`. Priorities set the due time from queueing (urgent 4 h, high 24 h, normal 72 h, low 7 days). States queued → assigned → in_review → decided; a decision needs an outcome (approve, changes, reject) and a reason, and records whether it beat the due time. In a workspace only an admin assigns someone else; only the assignee decides. The list sorts overdue first and suggests cases the model routed to review that nobody queued.
- **Collaboration (#882).** Threaded comments for anyone who can see the case (a viewer included) and for the broker on an open review link (`/v1/review/comments`, review rate class, authors shown by role only). Sign-offs with a reason unless approving; per-case broker and reviewer roles that never widen visibility. A broker's approval, in the case or as an approve or file_request answer on a review link, is what a filing needs.
- **Filing package (#879).** `POST /v1/cases/{id}/filing` fills the 19 CFR 177.2 letter (the cfr177 export, or the broker's edit) from the requester's answers and checks eleven required contents against 177.2(b) and the eRulings origin checklist; `GET …/filing?format=json|zip|pdf` returns a reproducible package (letter PDF and Markdown, Exhibit A and B, package JSON with SHA-256); `POST …/filing/status` tracks submitted (eRulings reference; only when every element is present and a broker approved), acknowledged, ruling_issued (ruling number) and withdrawn. Nothing is submitted to CBP: eRulings has no public submission API. The check is about form, not merit.
- **Storage and audit.** Inside the case document, like the review links (D200). Seven new audit actions (`queue.change`, `case.comment`, `case.approval`, `case.collaborator`, `filing.prepare`, `filing.status`, `filing.download`), none fail-closed, no free text in the trail. Every new route is in the isolation matrix, the role table, the audit table and openapi.yaml.
- **Not done.** Screens, automatic queueing of below-bar answers, notifications, tracked letter edits, attachment upload.

## D926 — ERP import and per-workspace usage metering with budgets (27 Nov, #880, #886)
Backend only, both features off by default; production behaviour is unchanged until an operator sets the flags.
- **ERP import (#880).** `ERP_IMPORT=on` registers `POST /v1/products/erp-import` (same access as a batch prediction). Input is a CSV export, as JSON or a multipart file, in one of three column layouts: `generic`, `sap_s4` (a BOM explosion: Material, Component, Country of Origin, Plant Country, Commodity Code) and `netsuite` (assembly items with member items); or `json` items. Lines are grouped by assembly; a line with a missing name, unknown country, bad HTS code or a header that changes between lines drops its assembly and is reported with its row number, and the other assemblies go on. Each assembly becomes one plant, one final-assembly operation and its distinct components. The default is a dry run (new, changed or unchanged per assembly, no model call); `commit` files up to 20 assemblies. **Idempotent:** the case ID is derived from the caller's scope, the source label and the ERP ID, and a fingerprint of the product decides the outcome: unchanged costs nothing, a changed BOM updates the same case, re-predicts, clears answers and the chosen origin, and records a `bom_updated` event. Fixtures for each layout are tested. Not done: live ERP API pulls, routings, write-back.
- **Usage metering (#886).** `USAGE_METERING=on` (needs `TEAMS=on`) counts, per workspace and UTC month, predictions, plan searches and model cost. Model cost comes from the existing daily spend meter, which now tells the workspace meter every charge, so nothing is double-priced. `GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/usage` (members, `?month=YYYY-MM`); `PUT`/`DELETE /v1/workspaces/{id}/budget` (admins, audited as `workspace.budget`) set a monthly USD budget, an alert percentage (default 80) and an optional hard cap. At the cap, a member's model call is refused with 402 `workspace_budget_reached` and `Retry-After` until the next month; a plan search is refused before it runs when the D87 estimate's upper bound would pass the cap, and the estimate response says whether it fits. A soft budget only reports. Metering fails open: a store error is logged and the call goes on. API-key and anonymous calls are not metered. No payments or invoices.
- **Checks.** New tests: parsers on SAP, NetSuite and generic fixtures, row errors, HTS cleanup, fingerprint; dry run, commit, unchanged re-import with no model call, changed re-import, per-caller IDs, limits, JSON and multipart; usage counts, admin-only budget, hard cap on predict and plan, estimate block, members-only, flags off. No model spend.
